Core idea: Tegusõna to be kasutatakse, kui räägime sellest, kes või mis keegi või miski on, kus keegi või miski asub, kust keegi pärit on, kui vana keegi on või millises seisundis keegi on.
Main rule / explanation: Olevikus on to be-l kolm vormi: am, is, are. Vorm sõltub alusest: I → am; he/she/it → is; you/we/they → are. To be on eriline tegusõna: koos sellega ei ole vaja do/does. Eituses paneme not pärast vormi am/is/are. Küsimuses paneme am/is/are aluse ette.
Form / structure: Jaatus: I am; he/she/it is; you/we/they are. Eitus: I am not; he/she/it isn't; you/we/they aren't. Küsimus: Am I...? Is he/she/it...? Are you/we/they...?
When / why we use it: Kasutame isiku ja elukutse kirjeldamiseks: She is a teacher. Koha jaoks: They are at home. Päritoluriigi või -linna kohta: He is from Spain. Vanuse ja seisundi kohta: I am ten. / She is tired. Kirjeldamiseks: The room is small.
Examples:
I’m ten. → Ma olen kümneaastane.
She is from Italy. → Ta on Itaaliast.
We are at school. → Me oleme koolis.
He isn't tired. → Ta ei ole väsinud.
Are they your friends? → Kas nad on sinu sõbrad?
Where are you? → Kus sa oled?
Special cases / exceptions: Lühivorme kasutatakse tavalises kõnes väga sageli: I’m, you’re, he’s, she’s, it’s, we’re, they’re. Lühivastustes kordame to be vormi: Yes, I am. / No, she isn't. / Yes, they are.
Common mistakes:
❌ He are a student. → ✅ He is a student.
❌ Do you be tired? → ✅ Are you tired?
❌ Is cold. → ✅ It is cold.
❌ Are she from Spain? → ✅ Is she from Spain?
Don't confuse with: Ära aja to be-d segi tavaliste tegusõnadega. ✅ Is she happy? Aga ✅ Does she work? To be-ga ei kasutata do/does.
Quick summary / memory hook:
I → am.
He/She/It → is.
You/We/They → are.
Eitus: lisa not.
Küsimus: pane am/is/are aluse ette.
Ära kasuta to be-ga do/does.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: This, that, these, those on sõnad, millega osutame inimesele või esemele. Need näitavad, kas räägime ühest või mitmest asjast ning kas see on lähedal või kaugemal.
Main rule / explanation: This = üks inimene või ese lähedal. That = üks inimene või ese kaugemal. These = mitu lähedal. Those = mitu kaugemal.
Form / structure: This + singular noun: this book. That + singular noun: that house. These + plural noun: these books. Those + plural noun: those houses.
When / why we use it: Kasutame siis, kui osutame inimestele ja asjadele või neile viitame. Sõna võib olla nimisõna ees või asendada nimisõna, kui on selge, millest räägime.
Examples:
This is my bag. → See on minu kott.
That is your teacher. → Too inimene on sinu õpetaja.
These are my shoes. → Need on minu kingad.
Those are our bikes. → Need seal on meie jalgrattad.
This book is interesting. → See raamat on huvitav.
Special cases / exceptions: This/that võivad viidata mitte ainult meie ees olevale esemele, vaid ka juba mainitud ideele või olukorrale: That idea is interesting. Peamine on eristada arvu ja kaugust.
Common mistakes:
❌ These is my book. → ✅ This is my book.
❌ This are my keys. → ✅ These are my keys.
❌ Those is your bag. → ✅ That is your bag.
Don't confuse with: This/these viitavad tavaliselt millelegi lähedal olevale ehk „see/need siin”. That/those viitavad kaugemal olevale ehk „too/need seal”. Ära aja this-t segi it-iga: it lihtsalt asendab juba teadaolevat eset, this osutab sellele.
Quick summary / memory hook:
This = 1 + lähedal.
That = 1 + kaugemal.
These = mitu + lähedal.
Those = mitu + kaugemal.
This/that — singular.
These/those — plural.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Subject pronouns näitavad, kes tegevust teeb. Possessive adjectives näitavad, kellele ese kuulub.
Main rule / explanation: Subject pronouns: I, you, he, she, it, we, they. Need on tavaliselt verbi ees: She works. Possessive adjectives: my, your, his, her, its, our, their. Nende järel tuleb tavaliselt nimisõna: her phone, our house.
Form / structure: I → my; you → your; he → his; she → her; it → its; we → our; they → their.
When / why we use it: Kasuta subject pronoun-i selle kohta, kes tegevust teeb: They live here. Kasuta possessive adjective'i enne eset või inimest, mis kellelegi kuulub: their house.
Examples:
I like my room. → Mulle meeldib minu tuba.
She has her phone. → Tal on tema telefon.
They love their dog. → Nad armastavad oma koera.
We clean our classroom. → Me koristame oma klassiruumi.
He knows his teacher. → Ta tunneb oma õpetajat.
Special cases / exceptions: Possessive adjective'i vorm ei muutu sõltuvalt eseme arvust: my book, my books; their friend, their friends. Its = „selle/tema” eseme või looma kohta. It's = it is / it has — see on teine konstruktsioon.
Common mistakes:
❌ My is phone. → ✅ My phone.
❌ She likes she room. → ✅ She likes her room.
❌ They are in theirs house. → ✅ They are in their house.
❌ Its raining. → ✅ It's raining.
Don't confuse with: I / my: I work. / My job is interesting. He / his: He works. / His office is big. Subject pronoun vastab küsimusele „kes teeb?”, possessive adjective küsimusele „kelle?” enne nimisõna.
Quick summary / memory hook:
I → my.
You → your.
He → his.
She → her.
It → its.
We → our.
They → their.
Pronoun + verb; possessive adjective + noun.

Lesson / Topic: a/an, plurals – singular and plural forms
Core idea: Inglise keeles võib nimisõna olla ainsuses või mitmuses. Ühe tavalise loendatava asja puhul kasutatakse sageli a/an. Mitme asja puhul kasutatakse tavaliselt mitmuse vormi.
Main rule / explanation: A/an kasutatakse ühe loendatava nimisõnaga, kui räägime ühest asjast, mitte konkreetsest teadaolevast asjast. A tuleb enne kaashäälikuhäälikut, an enne täishäälikuhäälikut.
Form / structure: a + singular noun: a book. an + singular noun: an apple. Enamik nimisõnu saab mitmusesse -s: book → books. Mõne lõpu järel kasutatakse -es: box → boxes. Kui sõna lõpeb kaashääliku + y-ga, muutub y sageli ies-ks: city → cities. Mõni -o-lõpuline sõna saab -es: potato → potatoes. Mõnel -f/-fe-lõpulisel sõnal muutub lõpp: leaf → leaves, knife → knives; kuid mitte kõigil: roof → roofs.
When / why we use it: A/an ainult ainsuses olevate loendatavate nimisõnadega. Mitmuses a/an ei kasutata: a dog → dogs, an apple → apples.
Examples:
I have a pen. → Mul on pastakas.
She has an umbrella. → Tal on vihmavari.
We need three books. → Meil on vaja kolme raamatut.
One box → two boxes. → Üks kast → kaks kasti.
A city → two cities. → Üks linn → kaks linna.
Special cases / exceptions: Vali a või an hääliku, mitte esimese tähe järgi: an hour, kuid a university. Mõnel sõnal on ebareeglipärane mitmus: man → men, woman → women, child → children, person → people.
Common mistakes:
❌ an book → ✅ a book.
❌ a apple → ✅ an apple.
❌ two book → ✅ two books.
❌ a books → ✅ books / some books.
Don't confuse with: A/an räägib ühest asjast. Mitmuses kasutatakse plural-vormi. Ära aja seda teemat segi kogu artiklisüsteemiga: the ja zero article tulevad eraldi.
Quick summary / memory hook:
A/an = üks loendatav asi.
A enne kaashäälikuhäälikut.
An enne täishäälikuhäälikut.
Tavaliselt plural = noun + s.
Mõni sõna saab -es.
Mõnel sõnal on ebareeglipärane plural.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Adjective on sõna, mis kirjeldab inimest, eset või olukorda: suur, väike, huvitav, kallis.
Main rule / explanation: Omadussõna seisab tavaliselt nimisõna ees: a small house, an interesting book. See võib olla ka pärast to be-d ja mõnda siduvat verbi: The house is small. The soup smells good.
Form / structure: Enne nimisõna: adjective + noun. Pärast be/linking verb: subject + be/linking verb + adjective.
When / why we use it: Kasutame omadussõnu, et öelda, milline inimene või ese on: a young teacher. Võime öelda, milline ta on: The teacher is young. Omadussõna võib kirjeldada ka olukorda või seisundit: The task is difficult.
Examples:
It is a big house. → See on suur maja.
The house is big. → Maja on suur.
She is happy. → Ta on õnnelik.
We have an interesting lesson. → Meil on huvitav tund.
The bag is expensive. → Kott on kallis.
Special cases / exceptions: Baastasemel ei saa omadussõna eraldi mitmuse vormi: one small car, two small cars. Samuti ei muutu see soo järgi.
Common mistakes:
❌ two expensives cars → ✅ two expensive cars.
❌ a house big → ✅ a big house.
❌ She is beautifully. → ✅ She is beautiful. (beautiful — adjective; beautifully — adverb).
Don't confuse with: Ära aja adjective'i ja adverb'i segi. Adjective kirjeldab eset või inimest: a slow car. Adverb kirjeldab tegevust: drive slowly. Adverbs of manner tuleb eraldi tunnis.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Adjective vastab küsimusele „milline?”.
Nimisõna ees: a nice day.
Pärast be-d: The day is nice.
Omadussõnad tavaliselt mitmuses ei muutu.
Ära aja adjective'i adverb'iga segi.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Present Simple kasutatakse harjumuste, korduvate tegevuste, faktide ja tavaliselt kehtivate asjade kohta.
Main rule / explanation: Jaatuses kasutavad I/you/we/they verbi põhivormi. He/she/it puhul lisame tavaliselt -s või -es. Eituses kasutame don't/doesn't. Küsimustes kasutame Do/Does. Pärast does/doesn't läheb põhiverb tagasi algvormi.
Form / structure: Positive: I work. / She works. Negative: I don't work. / She doesn't work. Question: Do you work? / Does she work?
When / why we use it: Harjumuste puhul: I play tennis on Sundays. Korduvate tegevuste puhul: He checks his email every morning. Faktide puhul: Water boils at 100°C. Selle kohta, mis tavaliselt juhtub: We start school at nine.
Examples:
I walk to school every day. → Ma lähen iga päev jalgsi kooli.
She plays tennis on Saturdays. → Ta mängib laupäeviti tennist.
We don't watch TV in the morning. → Me ei vaata hommikuti televiisorit.
He doesn't like coffee. → Talle ei meeldi kohv.
Do you live here? → Kas sa elad siin?
Does Anna work on Fridays? → Kas Anna töötab reedeti?
Special cases / exceptions: Ainsuse 3. isikus lisatakse enamasti -s: play → plays. Pärast ch, sh, s, x, o lisatakse sageli -es: watch → watches, go → goes. Kaashäälik + y muutub sageli -ies-ks: study → studies. Kõnes hääldatakse lõppu -s/-es erinevalt: plays /z/, watches /ɪz/, stops /s/.
Common mistakes:
❌ He work here. → ✅ He works here.
❌ She doesn't likes tea. → ✅ She doesn't like tea.
❌ Does he works here? → ✅ Does he work here?
❌ Do she live here? → ✅ Does she live here?
Don't confuse with: Ära aja tavalisi verbe segi to be-ga. ✅ Does she work? Aga ✅ Is she tired? To be-ga ei kasutata do/does.
Quick summary / memory hook:
I/you/we/they → V1.
He/she/it → V-s/es.
Eitus: don't / doesn't + V1.
Küsimus: Do / Does + subject + V1.
Pärast does/doesn't — ainult V1.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Questions – word order and question words
Core idea: Inglise küsimustel on kindel sõnajärg. Tavalauset ei saa lihtsalt lõppu küsimärgi lisamisega küsimuseks muuta.
Main rule / explanation: To be-ga küsimustes paneme am/is/are aluse ette. Tavaliste verbidega kasutame do/does/did. Kui on küsisõna, seisab see tavaliselt lause alguses.
Form / structure: Yes/No: Be + subject...? / Do/Does/Did + subject + V1...? Wh-question: question word + auxiliary/be + subject + main verb?
When / why we use it: What — mis/milline objekt. Where — kus. When — millal. Who — kes. Why — miks. Which — milline/mitmest valikust milline. Whose — kelle. How — kuidas; how old — kui vana; how often — kui tihti.
Examples:
Are you ready? → Kas sa oled valmis?
Do you like pizza? → Kas sulle meeldib pitsa?
Where do you live? → Kus sa elad?
Why is Tom late? → Miks Tom hilineb?
What do you want? → Mida sa tahad?
How old is Mia? → Kui vana Mia on?
Special cases / exceptions: Kui küsimus on to be-ga, do/does ei ole vaja: Is she at home? Mitte Does she be at home? Tavalise verbiga otseses küsimuses kasutatakse pärast küsisõna tavaliselt abiverbi: Where do you work?
Common mistakes:
❌ Where you live? → ✅ Where do you live?
❌ What does she likes? → ✅ What does she like?
❌ Why he is late? → ✅ Why is he late?
❌ Does she be tired? → ✅ Is she tired?
Don't confuse with: Ära aja otsest küsimust segi tavalise väitega. Subject questions on eraldi keerukam teema; siin ei ole vaja seda erandit õppijale üle koormavalt sisse tuua.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Kõigepealt vali be või auxiliary.
Be → pane see subject'i ette.
Tavaline verb → do/does/did.
Wh-word on tavaliselt alguses.
Pärast does/did on põhiverb = V1.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Adverbs of frequency with present simple
Core idea: Adverbs of frequency näitavad, kui sageli midagi toimub: alati, tavaliselt, sageli, mõnikord, harva või mitte kunagi.
Main rule / explanation: Põhisõnad: always, usually, often, sometimes, rarely, never. Tavalise verbiga seisab määrsõna tavaliselt põhiverbi ees. To be-ga seisab see tavaliselt am/is/are järel.
Form / structure: Subject + frequency adverb + main verb: She usually walks. Subject + be + frequency adverb: She is usually tired.
When / why we use it: Kasutame siis, kui räägime mitte praegu toimuvast tegevusest, vaid selle kordumise sagedusest. Neid võib kasutada koos every day, on Mondays ja teiste ajaväljenditega.
Examples:
I always do my homework. → Ma teen alati kodutööd.
We usually eat at home. → Me sööme tavaliselt kodus.
He often plays football. → Ta mängib sageli jalgpalli.
She sometimes reads at night. → Ta loeb mõnikord öösiti.
They are never late. → Nad ei jää kunagi hiljaks.
Special cases / exceptions: Sometimes on paindlik: Sometimes I walk to school. / I sometimes walk to school. Küsimustes ja eituses jääb määrsõna tavaliselt põhiverbi lähedale: Do you usually walk? / She doesn't often go there.
Common mistakes:
❌ He plays usually football. → ✅ He usually plays football.
❌ She always is late. → ✅ She is always late.
❌ They are never not late. → ✅ They are never late. (baastasemel ära loo kahekordset eitust).
Don't confuse with: Ära aja adverb of frequency't segi ajaväljendiga: every day ütleb, millal või kui sageli graafiku järgi; usually näitab tüüpilist sagedust. To be-ga on asukoht teistsugune kui tavalise verbiga.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Always = alati.
Usually = tavaliselt.
Often = sageli.
Sometimes = mõnikord.
Rarely = harva.
Never = mitte kunagi.
Tavaline verb → enne verbi.
Be → pärast be-d.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Object pronouns vs subject pronouns – me or I, she or her?
Core idea: Subject pronoun on see, kes tegevust teeb. Object pronoun on see, kellele või millele tegevus suunatakse, või asesõna pärast eessõna.
Main rule / explanation: Subject forms: I, you, he, she, it, we, they. Object forms: me, you, him, her, it, us, them.
Form / structure: Subject + verb: She called. Verb + object: She called me. Preposition + object: with him, for her, between us.
When / why we use it: Subject pronouns seisavad verbi ees, kui asesõna teeb tegevust. Object pronouns seisavad pärast verbi või eessõna.
Examples:
I know him. → Ma tunnen teda.
She helps me. → Ta aitab mind.
They invited us. → Nad kutsusid meid.
Can you call her? → Kas sa saad talle helistada?
This gift is for him. → See kingitus on talle.
Tom and I are friends. → Tom ja mina oleme sõbrad.
Special cases / exceptions: You ja it on subject- ja object-vormis samad: You help me. / I help you. It is small. / I like it. Erilist tähelepanu vajavad I/me ja he/him, she/her, we/us, they/them.
Common mistakes:
❌ She called I. → ✅ She called me.
❌ This is for he. → ✅ This is for him.
❌ Me and Tom are friends. → ✅ Tom and I are friends.
❌ Between you and I. → ✅ Between you and me.
Don't confuse with: Subject vastab küsimusele „kes teeb?”, object küsimustele „keda/kellele/mida?”. Võrdle: I like her. Siin teeb I tegevust, her saab tegevuse osaliseks.
Quick summary / memory hook:
I → me.
You → you.
He → him.
She → her.
It → it.
We → us.
They → them.
Before the verb = subject; after the verb/preposition = object.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Whose, possessive 's – Whose is this? It's Mike's
Core idea: Whose? küsib, kellele mingi ese kuulub. Possessive 's näitab omanikku: Maria's bag = Maria kott.
Main rule / explanation: Küsimus Whose + noun? tähendab „kelle?”. Et näidata ühe inimese või tavalise nimisõna omandisuhet, lisame 's: Tom's bike, the teacher's desk. Tavalise -s-lõpulise mitmuse puhul lisame tavaliselt ainult apostroofi: the students' books.
Form / structure: Question: Whose + noun + is/are ...? Answer: It's + name + 's. Possession: singular noun/name + 's + thing. Regular plural ending in -s + apostrophe + thing.
When / why we use it: Kasutame Whose't, kui tahame teada omanikku. Kasutame 's-i, kui tahame näidata, kellele miski kuulub.
Examples:
Whose bag is this? → Kelle kott see on?
It's Emma's. → See on Emma oma.
Whose phone is that? → Kelle telefon too on?
This is David's jacket. → See on Davidi jope.
The girl's bike is red. → Tüdruku jalgratas on punane.
The students' books are on the table. → Õpilaste raamatud on laual.
Special cases / exceptions: Kui omanik on juba arusaadav, võib vastata lühidalt: Whose is this? — It's Alex's. Ära aja who's ja whose't segi: who's = who is / who has; whose = kelle.
Common mistakes:
❌ Whose this bag? → ✅ Whose bag is this?
❌ Who's bag is this? → ✅ Whose bag is this?
❌ Tom bike → ✅ Tom's bike.
❌ the girls's room → ✅ the girls' room.
Don't confuse with: Whose? — küsimus omaniku kohta. Who? — küsimus inimese kohta. Who's? — lühend who is / who has. Possessive 's erineb tavalisest mitmuse tunnusest.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Whose? = Kelle?
Tom's book = Tomi raamat.
The girl's bag = tüdruku kott.
The students' books = õpilaste raamatud.
Whose ≠ who's.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: At, in, on – prepositions of time
Core idea: At, in ja on aitavad öelda, millal sündmus toimub. Kõige tähtsam on vaadata, mida me nimetame: täpset aega, päeva/kuupäeva või pikemat ajavahemikku.
Main rule / explanation: Kasutame at täpse kellaaja ja mõne kindla väljendi puhul: at 8:30, at night. Kasutame on päevaste ja kuupäevadega: on Monday, on 12 June. Kasutame in kuude, aastate, aastaaegade ja pikemate ajavahemikega: in July, in 2026, in winter.
Form / structure: at + clock time / fixed expression. on + day/date. in + month/year/season/longer period.
When / why we use it: At — kui aega saab ette kujutada kella ühe punktina. On — kui nimetame päeva või konkreetse kuupäeva. In — kui nimetame pikemat ajavahemikku.
Examples:
The lesson starts at nine. → Tund algab kell üheksa.
We meet at 8:30. → Me saame kokku kell 8:30.
I play tennis on Saturday. → Ma mängin laupäeval tennist.
Her birthday is on 12 June. → Tema sünnipäev on 12. juunil.
School starts in September. → Kool algab septembris.
He was born in 2015. → Ta sündis 2015. aastal.
We travel in summer. → Me reisime suvel.
Special cases / exceptions: At kasutatakse ka mõnes kindlas ajaühendis, näiteks at night. Ära proovi iga väljendit sõna-sõnalt tõlkida — õpi väljend tervikuna.
Common mistakes:
❌ at Monday → ✅ on Monday.
❌ in 8:30 → ✅ at 8:30.
❌ on July → ✅ in July.
❌ at 2026 → ✅ in 2026.
Don't confuse with: Pea meeles lihtsat skaalat: at = täpne aeg; on = päev/kuupäev; in = kuu/aasta/aastaaeg/pikem periood.
Quick summary / memory hook:
AT = täpne aeg.
ON = päev või kuupäev.
IN = kuu, aasta, aastaaeg või pikem periood.
at 7:00
on Monday
in July
in 2026.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: At, in, on – prepositions of place
Core idea: At, in ja on võivad näidata, kus inimene või ese asub. Siin on oluline ette kujutada, kuidas ese ruumis paikneb.
Main rule / explanation: At — punkt või konkreetne koht: at the door, at the station, at work. In — ruumi sees või territooriumi/ala piires: in the room, in the office, in Ukraine. On — pinnal: on the table, on the wall.
Form / structure: at + point/specific place. in + enclosed space/area. on + surface.
When / why we use it: At kasutame siis, kui tähtsam on koht kui punkt. In — kui keegi või miski on millegi sees või mingi ala piires. On — kui ese asub pinnal.
Examples:
She is at the station. → Ta on jaamas.
We are at work. → Me oleme tööl.
The children are in the room. → Lapsed on toas.
He lives in Ukraine. → Ta elab Ukrainas.
The keys are on the table. → Võtmed on laual.
There is a picture on the wall. → Seinal on pilt.
Special cases / exceptions: Vali eessõna ruumilise tähenduse järgi, mitte ainult sõna „sees” või „peal” tõlke järgi. Mõnda ühendit on parem õppida tervikuna: at work, in the room, on the table.
Common mistakes:
❌ The keys are at the table. → ✅ The keys are on the table. (kui need asuvad laua pinnal)
❌ She is on the room. → ✅ She is in the room.
❌ He is in work. → ✅ He is at work.
Don't confuse with: AT — koht kui punkt. IN — sees / ala piires. ON — pinnal. Näiteks: at the station, in the station building, on the wall.
Quick summary / memory hook:
AT = punkt / konkreetne koht.
IN = sees / ala piires.

Core idea: Can ja can't aitavad rääkida sellest, mida inimene oskab, mis on võimalik või mis on kellelegi lubatud.
Main rule / explanation: Pärast can ja can't kasutatakse alati verbi põhivormi ilma to-ta. Can ei muutu: I can, she can, they can. Küsimus moodustatakse nii: Can + subject + verb?
Form / structure: Positive: subject + can + V1. Negative: subject + can't/cannot + V1. Question: Can + subject + V1?
When / why we use it: Ability: I can swim. Possibility: We can start at nine. Permission: Can I ask a question? / Can I use this?
Examples:
I can swim. → Ma oskan ujuda.
She can speak English. → Ta oskab inglise keelt rääkida.
We can start at nine. → Me võime kell üheksa alustada.
You can't open this door. → Sa ei saa seda ust avada.
Can I use your phone? → Kas ma võin sinu telefoni kasutada?
Can he help us? → Kas ta saab meid aidata?
Special cases / exceptions: Can on kõigi isikute puhul sama: I can, he can, we can. Ära lisa he/she/it järel -s-i. Pärast can kasutatakse V1: can go, can help, can swim.
Common mistakes:
❌ She cans swim. → ✅ She can swim.
❌ I can to swim. → ✅ I can swim.
❌ Can you to help me? → ✅ Can you help me?
❌ He can helps us. → ✅ He can help us.
Don't confuse with: Can võib tähendada võimet, võimalust või luba. Ära aja can + V1 segi konstruktsiooniga want to + V1: can swim, aga want to swim.
Quick summary / memory hook:
CAN = oskan / saan / tohin.
CAN'T = ei oska / ei saa / ei tohi.
Can + V1.
Can ei muutu: I can, she can, they can.
Pärast can ei panda kunagi to-d ega -s-i.

Lesson / Topic: Present continuous – I'm doing, I'm not doing, Are you doing?
Core idea: Present Continuous näitab tegevust, mis toimub praegu, või ajutist olukorda praeguse aja ümber.
Main rule / explanation: Present Continuous moodustatakse nii: am/is/are + verb lõpuga -ing. Eituses lisame not pärast am/is/are. Küsimuses paneme am/is/are aluse ette.
Form / structure: Positive: I am working. / She is working. / They are working. Negative: I'm not working. / He isn't working. Questions: Are you working? / Is she working?
When / why we use it: Praegu toimuva tegevuse jaoks: I'm writing now. Ka ajutise praeguse olukorra jaoks: We're testing a different system this month.
Examples:
I’m reading now. → Ma loen praegu.
She is waiting for the bus. → Ta ootab bussi.
They are playing outside. → Nad mängivad õues.
We aren't working today. → Me ei tööta täna.
Are you listening? → Kas sa kuulad?
Is Tom using the computer? → Kas Tom kasutab arvutit?
Special cases / exceptions: Tavaliselt lisame -ing. Kui verb lõpeb hääldamata -e-ga, jääb e tavaliselt ära: make → making. Lühikestes verbides, millel on lühike rõhuline vokaal, võib lõppkonsonant kahekordistuda: run → running. Seisundiverbe, näiteks know, want, need, believe, understand, tavaliselt Continuous-is ei kasutata, kui kirjeldame seisundit. Verbid think, have, see võivad tähenduse muutudes esineda ka Continuous-is.
Common mistakes:
❌ She working now. → ✅ She is working now.
❌ They are play outside. → ✅ They are playing outside.
❌ I am write an email. → ✅ I am writing an email.
❌ Is he work? → ✅ Is he working?
Don't confuse with: Present Continuous = praegu/ajutiselt. Present Simple = tavaliselt/regulaarselt/faktina. Võrdle: I work every day. / I'm working now.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Present Continuous = am/is/are + V-ing.
Praegu või ajutiselt.
Eitus: be + not.
Küsimus: be + subject + V-ing.
make → making.
run → running.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Mõlemad ajavormid räägivad olevikust, kuid vaatavad olukorda erinevalt. Present Simple näitab tavalist, regulaarset või püsivat olukorda. Present Continuous näitab seda, mis toimub praegu või ajutiselt.
Main rule / explanation: Present Simple: harjumus, kordumine, fakt või püsiv olukord. Present Continuous: tegevus praegu või ajutine olukord praeguse aja ümber.
Form / structure: Present Simple: I work. / She works. Negative: don't/doesn't + V1. Present Continuous: am/is/are + V-ing. Negative: am/is/are not + V-ing.
When / why we use it: Present Simple esineb sageli sõnadega usually, often, every day, never. Present Continuous esineb sageli sõnadega now, today, this week, at the moment. Kuid kõigepealt määra tähendus ja alles siis vaata vihjesõna.
Examples:
I walk to school every day. → Ma lähen iga päev jalgsi kooli.
I’m walking to school now. → Ma lähen praegu jalgsi kooli.
She usually takes the bus. → Tavaliselt sõidab ta bussiga.
Today she’s taking the train. → Täna sõidab ta rongiga.
Our team works with monthly reports. → Meie meeskond töötab kuukokkuvõtetega.
Our team is preparing a special report this week. → Meie meeskond valmistab sel nädalal ette eriaruannet.
Special cases / exceptions: Sõnad now, every day, today jne aitavad, kuid ei vali ajavormi automaatselt. Oluline on mõista, kas tegu on tavalise/püsiva olukorra või praegu/ajutiselt toimuva tegevusega.
Common mistakes:
❌ I am going to school every day. → ✅ I go to school every day. (kui see on tavaline rutiin)
❌ I go to school now. → ✅ I am going to school now.
❌ She usually is driving to work. → ✅ She usually drives to work.
Don't confuse with: Present Simple = usual / regular / generally true. Present Continuous = now / around now / temporary.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Tavaliselt? → Present Simple.
Fakt? → Present Simple.
Praegu? → Present Continuous.
Ajutiselt? → Present Continuous.
Ära vali ajavormi ainult ühe sõna järgi.

Lesson / Topic: The imperative – Sit down! Don’t talk!
Core idea: Imperative on vorm, mida kasutame, kui ütleme inimesele, mida teha või mida mitte teha: juhis, käsk, hoiatus või lihtne suunis.
Main rule / explanation: Positiivse käsu puhul kasutame verbi põhivormi ilma to-ta: Open the door. Negatiivse käsu puhul kasutame Don't + V1: Don't talk.
Form / structure: Positive imperative: V1. Negative imperative: Don't + V1.
When / why we use it: Juhiste puhul: Turn left. Käskude puhul: Sit down. Hoiatuste puhul: Don't touch that. Lihtsate suuniste puhul: Follow me.
Examples:
Open the window. → Ava aken.
Wait here. → Oota siin.
Check your answer. → Kontrolli oma vastust.
Don't run. → Ära jookse.
Don't touch that button. → Ära puuduta seda nuppu.
Turn left. → Pööra vasakule.
Special cases / exceptions: Imperative võib olla lühike ja otsene. Viisakamates olukordades lisatakse sageli please: Please sit down.
Common mistakes:
❌ To open the door. → ✅ Open the door.
❌ Don't to talk. → ✅ Don't talk.
❌ Opens the door. → ✅ Open the door.
Don't confuse with: Imperative ei vaja subject pronoun'i. Võrdle: Open the door. Aga You open the door every day.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Käsk: V1.
Keeld: Don't + V1.
Open!
Don't open!
Ära lisa to-d ega -s-i.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: There is / There are kasutatakse, kui tahame öelda, et kusagil on keegi või miski olemas või asub.
Main rule / explanation: There is kasutatakse ainsuses ja loendamatu nimisõnaga. There are kasutatakse mitmuses loendatavate nimisõnadega.
Form / structure: Positive: There is + singular/uncountable noun. There are + plural noun. Negative: There isn't / There aren't. Question: Is there...? / Are there...?
When / why we use it: Kasutame, kui tutvustame midagi, mis mingis kohas olemas on: There is a book on the table. / There are two chairs in the room.
Examples:
I was tired yesterday. → Olin eile väsinud.
She was at home. → Ta oli kodus.
He wasn't late. → Ta ei hilinenud.
We were at school. → Olime koolis.
You weren't busy. → Sa ei olnud hõivatud.
Were they at the park? → Kas nad olid pargis?
Special cases / exceptions: Igapäevases kõnes kasutatakse lühendeid: there's = there is. There are lühivormi tavaliselt ei ole. Ära aja there is/are segi it is-iga.
Common mistakes:
❌ There is two books. → ✅ There are two books.
❌ There are a problem. → ✅ There is a problem.
❌ Is there any students? → ✅ Are there any students?
Don't confuse with: There is/are = midagi on olemas või asub kusagil. It is = me räägime juba teadaolevast asjast või olukorrast.
Quick summary / memory hook:
There is = 1 / uncountable.
There are = plural.
Question: Is there...? / Are there...?
Negative: isn't / aren't.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Past Simple näitab lõpetatud tegevust minevikus. Sageli teame või ütleme, millal see juhtus.
Main rule / explanation: Tavalised verbid saavad Past Simple-is tavaliselt lõpu -ed. Ebareeglipärased verbid kasutavad erilist minevikuvormi V2: go → went, see → saw, make → made.
Form / structure: Regular: V1 + -ed → V2. Irregular: special V2. Peamine on osata ära tunda ja kasutada õiget mineviku vormi.
When / why we use it: Lõpetatud minevikusündmuse puhul: I visited London last year. Minevikus toimunud sündmuste jada puhul: He opened the door and walked inside.
Examples:
I finished my homework yesterday. → Lõpetasin eile oma kodutöö.
She cleaned her room last Saturday. → Ta koristas eelmisel laupäeval oma toa.
We visited the museum two days ago. → Külastasime kaks päeva tagasi muuseumi.
He went to London last year. → Ta käis eelmisel aastal Londonis.
I saw Tom yesterday. → Nägin Tomi eile.
She made a cake on Sunday. → Ta tegi pühapäeval koogi.
Special cases / exceptions: Ebareeglipäraseid verbe ei saa moodustada lihtsalt -ed lisamisega: go → went, see → saw, make → made, take → took. Tavalistel verbidel on -ed kirjapildireeglid: like → liked, stop → stopped, study → studied. Lõppu -ed hääldatakse /t/, /d/ või /ɪd/: watched, played, wanted.
Common mistakes:
❌ go → goed → ✅ go → went.
❌ see → seed → ✅ see → saw.
❌ Yesterday I go to school. → ✅ Yesterday I went to school.
❌ Last week she work here. → ✅ Last week she worked here.
Don't confuse with: Past Simple = lõpetatud tegevus minevikus. See ei ole sama mis Past Continuous, kus tegevus oli mineviku kindlal hetkel pooleli.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Past Simple = lõpetatud minevik.
Regular → tavaliselt -ed.
Irregular → eriline V2.
yesterday / last... / ... ago viitavad sageli Past Simple'ile.
go → went.
see → saw.
make → made.

Core idea: Past Simple-is tavalise verbiga eituse või küsimuse moodustamiseks kasutame did/didn't. Põhireegel: pärast did või didn't läheb verb tagasi algvormi V1.
Main rule / explanation: Eitus: subject + didn't + V1. Küsimus: Did + subject + V1? See reegel kehtib võrdselt I, you, he, she, it, we, they puhul.
Form / structure: Positive: She worked. Negative: She didn't work. Question: Did she work? / Did they go?
When / why we use it: Kasutame did/didn't tavaliste verbidega Past Simple-is. Was/were jaoks on eraldi reegel eelmisest tunnist.
Examples:
I didn't send the message. → Ma ei saatnud sõnumit.
She didn't call me. → Ta ei helistanud mulle.
They didn't go to school. → Nad ei läinud kooli.
Did you finish the task? → Kas sa lõpetasid ülesande?
Did he see Anna? → Kas ta nägi Annat?
Did they play football yesterday? → Kas nad mängisid eile jalgpalli?
Special cases / exceptions: Pärast did/didn't ei kasutata minevikuvormi V2: did go, didn't go; mitte did went, didn't went. See on eriti tähtis ebareeglipäraste verbide puhul.
Common mistakes:
❌ Did she went home? → ✅ Did she go home?
❌ He didn't worked yesterday. → ✅ He didn't work yesterday.
❌ Did they saw him? → ✅ Did they see him?
❌ Did you were tired? → ✅ Were you tired?
Don't confuse with: Tavaline verb: Did you work? To be: Were you tired? Ära aja did-i segi was/were-vormidega.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Past Simple negative = didn't + V1.
Past Simple question = Did + subject + V1?
Pärast did/didn't ei kasutata kunagi V2.
Reegel on sama kõigi subject pronouns puhul.
Was/were — eraldi reegel.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Pärast erinevaid inglise verbe võib järgmine verb olla kujul to + verb või verb + -ing. Seda nimetatakse verb pattern-iks — mudeliks, mida tuleb õppida koos esimese verbiga.
Main rule / explanation: Mõned verbid nõuavad tavaliselt to-infinitiivi: want to learn, need to check, plan to travel. Teised nõuavad tavaliselt -ing-vormi: enjoy reading, finish working, avoid making.
Form / structure: Verb + to + V1: want to learn, need to check, plan to travel. Verb + V-ing: enjoy reading, finish working, avoid making.
When / why we use it: Kui kaks verbi järgnevad üksteisele, ei saa automaatselt to-d panna. Tuleb teada esimese verbi mudelit.
Examples:
I want to learn English. → Ma tahan inglise keelt õppida.
We need to check the answer. → Me peame vastust kontrollima.
They plan to travel in summer. → Nad plaanivad suvel reisida.
I enjoy reading. → Mulle meeldib lugeda.
She finished working. → Ta lõpetas töötamise.
He avoids making mistakes. → Ta väldib vigade tegemist.
Try to arrive early. → Proovi varakult kohale jõuda.
Special cases / exceptions: Selle teema puhul on kõige tähtsam meelde jätta verb + pattern: want to, need to, plan to; enjoy -ing, finish -ing, avoid -ing. Mõnel verbil võib olla mitu mudelit või erinev tähendus, kuid neid tuleb õppida eraldi.
Common mistakes:
❌ I enjoy to read. → ✅ I enjoy reading.
❌ She wants going. → ✅ She wants to go.
Don't confuse with: to-infinitive: want to learn. -ing: enjoy learning. Vormi ei saa valida ainult vene keele tõlke järgi — õpi verb koos selle mudeliga.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Mõned verbid + to + V1.
Mõned verbid + V-ing.
want → want to learn.
need → need to check.
enjoy → enjoy reading.
finish → finish working.
Õpi verb koos selle mudeliga.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Would you like...? on viisakas viis midagi pakkuda või küsida, mida inimene soovib. I'd like... on viisakas viis oma soovi väljendada.
Main rule / explanation: Would you like...? kasutame pakkumise või eelistuse küsimise puhul. I'd like... kasutame, kui ütleme, mida tahame saada või teha.
Form / structure: Would you like + noun ...? / Would you like + to + V1 ...? I'd like + noun. / I'd like + to + V1.
When / why we use it: Viisakaks pakkumiseks: Would you like some tea? Viisakaks sooviks või tellimuseks: I'd like a sandwich. / I'd like to sit here.
Examples:
Would you like some water? → Kas sa sooviksid vett?
Would you like to play with us? → Kas sa tahaksid meiega mängida?
I'd like a new notebook. → Ma sooviksin uut vihikut.
I'd like to ask a question. → Ma sooviksin küsimuse esitada.
Would you like some help? → Kas sa sooviksid abi?
Special cases / exceptions: Pärast would like võib olla nimisõna või to + V1: I'd like some juice. / I'd like to drink some juice. Tavalist verbi ei panda kohe pärast would like ilma to-ta.
Common mistakes:
❌ I like to a coffee. → ✅ I'd like a coffee.
❌ I'd like go home. → ✅ I'd like to go home.
❌ Would you like going with us? → ✅ Would you like to go with us?
Don't confuse with: Ära aja I like ja I'd like segi. I like = mulle üldiselt meeldib. I'd like = ma sooviksin praegu / selles olukorras.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Would you like + noun?
Would you like + to + V1?
I'd like + noun.
I'd like + to + V1.
See on viisakas pakkumise või soovi vorm.

Core idea: Have got kasutatakse sageli selle ütlemiseks, et kellelgi on midagi: ese, sugulane või mingi omadus.
Main rule / explanation: I/you/we/they puhul kasutame have got. He/she/it puhul has got. Eituses: haven't got / hasn't got. Küsimustes: Have ... got? / Has ... got?
Form / structure: Positive: I/you/we/they have got; he/she/it has got. Negative: haven't got / hasn't got. Question: Have/Has + subject + got?
When / why we use it: Omamise puhul: I've got a bike. Suhete puhul: She has got two brothers. Mõne omaduse puhul: He has got blue eyes.
Examples:
I've got a new backpack. → Mul on uus seljakott.
She has got two sisters. → Tal on kaks õde.
We haven't got a car. → Meil ei ole autot.
Has Tom got a dog? → Kas Tomil on koer?
Have you got any brothers? → Kas sul on vendi?
Special cases / exceptions: Kõnekeeles kasutatakse väga sageli ka tavalist have-i: I have a bike. Have got ja have võivad väljendada sama omamist. Ära sega vorme: has got, mitte has have got.
Common mistakes:
❌ She have got a cat. → ✅ She has got a cat.
❌ Does she has got a cat? → ✅ Has she got a cat?
❌ He hasn't has got a bike. → ✅ He hasn't got a bike.
Don't confuse with: Have got on eraldi mudel. Ära moodusta küsimust do/does abil: Have you got...? / Has he got...?
Quick summary / memory hook:
I/you/we/they → have got.
He/she/it → has got.
Eitus: haven't/hasn't got.
Küsimus: Have/Has ... got?
Have got = possession.

Lesson / Topic: A, some, any – countable and uncountable nouns
Core idea: Countable nouns saab kokku lugeda: one apple, two apples. Uncountable nouns käsitleme massi või ainena: water, money, information. Some ja any aitavad rääkida kogusest ilma täpset arvu ütlemata.
Main rule / explanation: Loendatavatel nimisõnadel võib olla ainsus või mitmus. Loendamatutel ei ole tavaliselt tavalist mitmuse vormi. Some esineb sageli jaatavates lausetes. Any esineb sageli küsimustes ja eitustes.
Form / structure: Countable singular: a/an + noun. Countable plural: some/any + plural noun. Uncountable: some/any + uncountable noun.
When / why we use it: Some: We have some books. / We have some water. Any: Do you have any books? / We don't have any water.
Examples:
I have a book. → Mul on raamat.
I have some books. → Mul on mõned raamatud.
We need some water. → Me vajame vett.
Do you have any questions? → Kas sul on küsimusi?
We don't have any money. → Meil ei ole raha.
Special cases / exceptions: Some esineb tavaliselt jaatavates lausetes. Any on tavaliselt küsimustes ja eitustes. Kuid some on võimalik ka siis, kui pakume või palume midagi: Would you like some juice? Mitte two informations, vaid two pieces of information.
Common mistakes:
❌ an information → ✅ some information.
❌ two advices → ✅ two pieces of advice.
❌ Do you have some questions? → ✅ Do you have any questions? (tavaline neutraalne küsimus)
❌ a water → ✅ some water / a bottle of water.
Don't confuse with: Ära aja countable ja uncountable segi. Countable: one book, two books. Uncountable: water, advice, information. A/an kasutatakse singular countable'iga, mitte uncountable'iga.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Countable → saab kokku lugeda.
Uncountable → tavaliselt ei loe tükikaupa.
Some → sageli positive.
Any → sageli questions/negative.
A/an → ainult singular countable.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: There is, there are – there was, there were
Core idea: There is / There are ütlevad, et kusagil on või asub midagi. Minevikus kasutatakse there was / there were.
Main rule / explanation: Ühe eseme või loendamatu nimisõnaga kasutame there is. Mitmega kasutame there are. Minevikus: there was + ainsus/loendamatu; there were + mitmus.
Form / structure: Present: There is + singular/uncountable. There are + plural. Past: There was + singular/uncountable. There were + plural.
When / why we use it: Kasutame siis, kui teatame esimest korda millegi olemasolust või asukohast: There is a park near my house. / There are two windows in the room.
Examples:
There is a book on the desk. → Laual on raamat.
There are three students in the room. → Toas on kolm õpilast.
There was a problem yesterday. → Eile oli probleem.
There were two cafés here. → Siin oli kaks kohvikut.
Special cases / exceptions: Is/are valimisel vaatame konstruktsioonile järgnevat nimisõna: one chair → there is; two chairs → there are. Loendamatu nimisõnaga: There is some water.
Common mistakes:
❌ There are a book. → ✅ There is a book.
❌ There is three cars. → ✅ There are three cars.
❌ There was two people. → ✅ There were two people.
Don't confuse with: Ära aja there is-i segi it is-iga. There is tutvustab olemasolu: There is a problem. It is viitab kindlaks tehtud asjale: The problem is difficult. It is difficult.
Quick summary / memory hook:
There is = on üks / loendamatu.
There are = on mitu.
There was = oli üks / loendamatu.
There were = oli mitu.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Mõlemad sõnad võivad tõlkes tähendada „see/ta/see”, kuid töötavad erinevalt. There tutvustab olemasolu. It viitab tavaliselt juba teadaolevale asjale või olukorrale.
Main rule / explanation: There kasutatakse, kui teatame, et miski eksisteerib või asub kusagil. It asendab või tähistab tavaliselt konkreetset asja, olukorda, ilma või aega või vahemaad.
Form / structure: Existence: There is/are + noun. Reference: It + be/verb ...
When / why we use it: Võrdle: There is a new message. → Tutvustame sõnumit esimest korda. It is important. → Nüüd räägime juba teadaolevast sõnumist. It kasutatakse ka väljendites It is cold, It's five o'clock.
Examples:
There is a new shop near our house. → Meie maja lähedal on uus pood.
It is very popular. → See on väga populaarne.
There are two chairs in the room. → Toas on kaks tooli.
They are comfortable. → Need on mugavad.
It's cold today. → Täna on külm.
It's ten o'clock. → Kell on kümme.
Special cases / exceptions: Konstruktsioonis there is/are tuleb pärast there tavaliselt nimisõna. It võib esineda ilma eraldi nimisõnata: It's raining. / It's late.
Common mistakes:
❌ There is cold today. → ✅ It is cold today.
❌ There are two chairs. It are comfortable. → ✅ There are two chairs. They are comfortable.
❌ It is a new message on my phone. (kui tutvustame sõnumit esimest korda) → ✅ There is a new message on my phone.
Don't confuse with: Kas midagi on olemas? → mõtle there is/are. Kas räägid juba teadaolevast asjast, ilmast, ajast või vahemaast? → mõtle it.
Quick summary / memory hook:
There is/are = tutvustame olemasolu.
It = viitame juba teadaolevale või olukorrale.
It's cold.
It's late.

Lesson / Topic: Next to, under, between, in front of, behind, over, etc.
Core idea: Need eessõnad aitavad kirjeldada, kus ese asub teiste esemete suhtes: kõrval, all, vahel, taga või ees.
Main rule / explanation: Next to = kõrval. Under = all. Between = kahe objekti vahel. Behind = taga. In front of = ees.
Form / structure: next to + noun. under + noun. between + A + and + B. behind + noun. in front of + noun.
When / why we use it: Kasutame, kui kirjeldame esemete, inimeste ja kohtade asukohta.
Examples:
The printer is next to my desk. → Printer on minu laua kõrval.
The ball is under the chair. → Pall on tooli all.
The café is between the bank and the hotel. → Kohvik on panga ja hotelli vahel.
The car is behind the house. → Auto on maja taga.
The bus is in front of the school. → Buss on kooli ees.
Special cases / exceptions: Baastasemel on between hea meelde jätta kui „kahe vahel”: between A and B. Ära aja behind ja in front of segi — need on vastandlikud asukohad.
Common mistakes:
❌ between the bank → ✅ between the bank and the hotel.
❌ The bag is under of the chair. → ✅ The bag is under the chair.
❌ The car is in front the house. → ✅ The car is in front of the house.
Don't confuse with: Eessõnad töötavad nagu väike kaart: next to = kõrval, under = all, behind = taga, in front of = ees, between = kahe vahel.
Quick summary / memory hook:
next to = kõrval.
under = all.
between A and B = vahel.
behind = taga.
in front of = ees.

Lesson / Topic: Much, many, a lot of, a little, a few
Core idea: Quantifiers on sõnad, mis näitavad kogust: palju, natuke, mõned, vähe.
Main rule / explanation: Many kasutatakse mitmuses olevate loendatavate nimisõnadega. Much — loendamatute nimisõnadega. A lot of sobib nii loendatavate mitmuste kui ka loendamatute nimisõnadega. A few — mõned loendatavad mitmused; a little — natuke loendamatut.
Form / structure: many + plural countable. much + uncountable. a lot of + plural countable/uncountable. a few + plural countable. a little + uncountable.
When / why we use it: Kasutame kogusest rääkides, kui täpset arvu ei nimetata. Küsimustes ja eitustes esineb much/many eriti sageli.
Examples:
We have many books. → Meil on palju raamatuid.
We don't have much time. → Meil ei ole palju aega.
She has a lot of friends. → Tal on palju sõpru.
I have a few questions. → Mul on mõned küsimused.
There is a little milk in the fridge. → Külmikus on natuke piima.
Special cases / exceptions: Oluline on eristada a few ja few ning a little ja little. A few ja a little tähendavad väikest, kuid olemasolevat kogust; few ja little annavad sageli mõtte „peaaegu mitte ühtegi/üldse mitte”.
Common mistakes:
❌ much books → ✅ many books.
❌ many information → ✅ much information / a lot of information.
❌ a little people → ✅ a few people.
❌ a few water → ✅ a little water.
Don't confuse with: Kõigepealt määra nimisõna: kas seda saab lugeda või mitte? Seejärel vali quantifier.
Quick summary / memory hook:
many + countable plural.
much + uncountable.
a lot of + both.
a few + countable plural.
a little + uncountable.

Lesson / Topic: Comparative adjectives – older than, more important than, etc.
Core idea: Comparative adjectives võrdlevad kahte inimest või eset: kumb on pikem, kiirem, odavam või huvitavam.
Main rule / explanation: Paljud lühikesed omadussõnad saavad lõpu -er: small → smaller. Paljud pikemad kasutavad more: more interesting. Teise objekti nimetamisel kasutatakse sageli than-i.
Form / structure: Short adjective: adjective + -er + than. Long adjective: more + adjective + than.
When / why we use it: Kasutame, kui võrdleme kahte objekti, inimest või olukorda.
Examples:
My bike is faster than yours. → Minu jalgratas on sinu omast kiirem.
This room is smaller than the kitchen. → See tuba on köögist väiksem.
The new game is more interesting than the old one. → Uus mäng on vanast huvitavam.
This bag is more expensive than that one. → See kott on sellest kallim.
Special cases / exceptions: Mõned vormid on ebareeglipärased: good → better, bad → worse, far → farther/further. Kirjapilt võib samuti muutuda: big → bigger, happy → happier.
Common mistakes:
❌ more faster → ✅ faster.
❌ beautifuler → ✅ more beautiful.
❌ My car is faster that yours. → ✅ My car is faster than yours.
Don't confuse with: Comparative = võrdleme kahte. Superlative = valime ühe kui kõige... Ära aja -er-i ja -est-i segi.
Quick summary / memory hook:
2 objekti → comparative.
Short adjective → often -er.
Long adjective → often more.
Teine objekt → than.
fast → faster; useful → more useful.

Lesson / Topic: Superlative adjectives – the oldest, the most important, etc.
Core idea: Superlative adjectives näitavad, et üks inimene või ese on grupis kõige suurem, kõige kiirem, kõige huvitavam jne.
Main rule / explanation: Paljud lühikesed omadussõnad saavad lõpu -est: fast → fastest. Paljud pikad kasutavad the most: the most interesting. Tavaliselt seisab superlative'i ees the.
Form / structure: Short adjective: the + adjective-est. Long adjective: the most + adjective.
When / why we use it: Kasutame, kui võrdleme ühte objekti kogu grupiga: kõige pikem klassis, kõige kiirem meeskonnas.
Examples:
Tom is the tallest boy in the class. → Tom on klassi kõige pikem poiss.
This is the fastest train here. → See on siin kõige kiirem rong.
It is the most interesting book in the library. → See on raamatukogu kõige huvitavam raamat.
She is the best player on the team. → Ta on meeskonna parim mängija.
Special cases / exceptions: Mõned vormid on ebareeglipärased: good → the best, bad → the worst. Mõne lühikese sõna kirjapilt muutub: big → biggest, happy → happiest.
Common mistakes:
❌ She is best student. → ✅ She is the best student.
❌ the most fastest → ✅ the fastest.
❌ the beautifulest → ✅ the most beautiful.
Don't confuse with: Comparative võrdleb kahte: faster than. Superlative tõstab ühe grupist esile: the fastest.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Superlative = kõige...
Short adjective → -est.
Long adjective → the most.
the fastest.
the most useful.

Core idea: Going to kasutatakse peamiselt plaani või kavatsuse väljendamiseks ning ennustuseks, millel on praegu nähtavad tunnused.
Main rule / explanation: Going to moodustatakse vormiga be + going to + V1. Kasutame seda juba olemasoleva plaani või kavatsuse puhul ning ennustuseks, kui praegu on selle jaoks tõendeid.
Form / structure: Positive: subject + will + V1. Negative: subject + won't + V1. Question: Will + subject + V1? Shall I/shall we + V1?
When / why we use it: Plaani puhul: I'm going to study tonight. Tunnuse põhjal tehtud ennustuse puhul: Look at those clouds. It's going to rain.
Examples:
I'll call you tonight. → Helistan sulle täna õhtul.
I think the test will be easy. → Ma arvan, et test on lihtne.
We won't be late. → Me ei jää hiljaks.
Will you help me? → Kas sa aitad mind?
Shall we start? → Kas alustame?
Shall I open the window? → Kas ma avan akna?
Special cases / exceptions: Ära unusta be-d: I am going to, he is going to, they are going to. Ilma be-ta ei saa: mitte I going to...
Common mistakes:
❌ I going to study. → ✅ I am going to study.
❌ She is going to buys it. → ✅ She is going to buy it.
❌ Are you going to went there? → ✅ Are you going to go there?
Don't confuse with: Will sobib sageli otsuse või ennustuse jaoks kõnehetkel. Going to sobib eriti hästi juba olemasoleva plaani või praegu nähtavatel tunnustel põhineva ennustuse jaoks.
Quick summary / memory hook:
be + going to + V1.
I am going to...
He is going to...
They are going to...
Plaan või kavatsus.
Ennustus praeguste tunnuste põhjal.

Lesson / Topic: Be going to – future plans and predictions
Core idea: Adverb of manner näitab, kuidas tegevus toimub: slowly, carefully, happily. Adjective kirjeldab inimest või eset: slow, careful, happy.
Main rule / explanation: Adjective kirjeldab tavaliselt nimisõna või seisab to be järel. Adverb of manner kirjeldab verbi. Paljud sellised määrsõnad moodustuvad -ly abil: slow → slowly, careful → carefully.
Form / structure: Positive: I am going to study. / She is going to travel. Negative: I’m not going to study. / She isn’t going to travel. Question: Are you going to study?
When / why we use it: Kui vastame küsimusele „milline?”, vajame adjective'i. Kui küsime „kuidas tegevus toimub?”, vajame sageli adverb'i.
Examples:
I'm going to visit my grandmother on Sunday. → Lähen pühapäeval oma vanaemale külla.
We're going to start a new project next month. → Alustame järgmisel kuul uut projekti.
Look at the sky — it's going to snow. → Vaata taevast — kohe hakkab lund sadama.
Are you going to watch the match? → Kas sa kavatsed mängu vaadata?
He isn't going to buy a new phone. → Ta ei kavatse uut telefoni osta.
Special cases / exceptions: Kõik määrsõnad ei lõpe -ly-ga. Tähtis näide: good — adjective, well — adverb. Mõnel sõnal on sama vorm: fast → drive fast.
Common mistakes:
❌ She sings beautiful. → ✅ She sings beautifully.
❌ He is carefully. → ✅ He is careful.
❌ He sings good. → ✅ He sings well.
Don't confuse with: Adjective kirjeldab noun/person/state: a slow car. Adverb kirjeldab action: drive slowly.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Adjective = milline?
Adverb = kuidas?
slow → slowly.
careful → carefully.
good → well.
a fast car / drive fast.

Core idea: Articles aitavad mõista, kas räägime ühest ebamäärasest asjast, konkreetsest tuntud asjast või sellistest asjadest üldiselt.
Main rule / explanation: a/an kasutame ühe loendatava nimisõnaga, kui see ei ole konkreetne või mainitakse esimest korda: a dog, an apple. The kasutame, kui on selge, millisest konkreetsest asjast räägime: the dog. Zero article esineb sageli, kui räägime asjadest üldiselt: Dogs are friendly. Water is important.
Form / structure: a/an + singular countable. the + specific/known noun phrase. Ø + plural or uncountable noun for general meaning.
When / why we use it: Esmakordne mainimine: I saw a dog. Korduv/konkreetne: The dog was friendly. Üldine väide: Dogs are friendly. / Water is important.
Examples:
She is a careful driver. → Ta on ettevaatlik juht.
She drives carefully. → Ta sõidab ettevaatlikult.
The dog is quiet. → Koer on vaikne.
The dog walks quietly. → Koer kõnnib vaikselt.
He is a good singer. → Ta on hea laulja.
He sings well. → Ta laulab hästi.
Special cases / exceptions: Elukutsega pärast to be-d on vaja a/an: She is a teacher. Unikaalsete asjade puhul kasutatakse tavaliselt the: the sun, the moon. Mõnes püsiväljendis artiklit ei panda: go to school, play football, by bus.
Common mistakes:
❌ I saw dog. → ✅ I saw a dog.
❌ I bought a book. A book is interesting. → ✅ I bought a book. The book is interesting.
❌ The books are useful. (kui räägime raamatutest üldiselt) → ✅ Books are useful.
Don't confuse with: Ära aja a/an ja the segi: a/an = üks, kuid mitte konkreetne; the = konkreetne/tuntud või ainulaadne; Ø = üldine tähendus või mõned püsiväljendid.
Quick summary / memory hook:
a/an = üks, mitte konkreetne.
the = konkreetne/tuntud või ainulaadne.
Ø = üldine tähendus.
a teacher, the sun, Dogs, go to school, by bus.

Lesson / Topic: A/an, the, no article – the use of articles in English
Core idea: Conjunctions seovad sõnu ja lauseosi. And lisab infot, but näitab vastandust, or annab valiku, so näitab tulemust ja because selgitab põhjust.
Main rule / explanation: Iga sõna näitab kahe idee vahelist seost: and = ja, but = aga/kuid, or = või, so = seega/seetõttu, because = sest/kuna.
Form / structure: Clause A + and + Clause B. Clause A + but + Clause B. Choice: A or B. Result: A, so B. Reason: A because B.
When / why we use it: Kasutame, et mitte teha igast mõttest eraldi lauset ja näidata, kuidas ideed on seotud.
Examples:
I saw a bird in the garden. The bird was blue. → Ma nägin aias lindu. Lind oli sinine.
I need a pen. → Mul on pastakat vaja.
The pen on the desk is mine. → Laual olev pastakas on minu oma.
Books can teach us a lot. → Raamatud võivad meile palju õpetada.
Milk is good for children. → Piim on lastele kasulik.
Special cases / exceptions: Kõige tähtsam paar: because vastab küsimusele „miks?” ja annab põhjuse; so näitab tulemust. Ära kasuta neid samas rollis.
Common mistakes:
❌ It was late, because we went home. → ✅ We went home because it was late.
❌ It was raining, because we took an umbrella. → ✅ It was raining, so we took an umbrella.
Don't confuse with: Because = põhjus. So = tulemus. But = vastandus. Or = valik. And = lisamine.
Quick summary / memory hook:
and = lisame.
but = vastandame.
or = valime.
because = põhjus.
so = tulemus.

Lesson / Topic: Conjunctions: and, but, or, so, because
Core idea: Inglise keeles on sõnajärg üsna range. Lihtsas väites on tavaliselt Subject + Verb + Object: kes teeb → mida teeb → millele tegevus on suunatud.
Main rule / explanation: Põhimudel: Subject + Verb + Object. Koht ja aeg seisavad sageli põhiosa järel. Küsimustel on eraldi struktuur to be või auxiliary abil.
Form / structure: S + V + O: Tom reads books. S + be + adjective: Anna is tired. S + V + place + time: We study at home in the evening.
When / why we use it: Kasutame seda järjekorda tavalistes väidetes. Inglise sõnu ei saa lihtsalt vene keele sõnajärje järgi ümber tõsta.
Examples:
I like tea and coffee. → Mulle meeldib tee ja kohv.
The task is difficult, but it is possible. → Ülesanne on raske, kuid see on võimalik.
Do you want tea or juice? → Kas sa tahad teed või mahla?
It was raining, so we stayed home. → Sadas vihma, seega jäime koju.
We stayed home because it was raining. → Jäime koju, sest sadas vihma.
Special cases / exceptions: Küsimustes sõnajärg muutub: Do you play football? / Is the dog under the table? Ära kasuta väite tavalist sõnajärge lihtsalt küsimärgiga.
Common mistakes:
❌ Every day I football play. → ✅ I play football every day.
❌ Where you live? → ✅ Where do you live?
❌ She English speaks. → ✅ She speaks English.
Don't confuse with: English word order ja Question word order on erinevad mudelid. Kõigepealt määra, kas tegu on väite või küsimusega.
Quick summary / memory hook:
S + V + O.
Kes? → Subject.
Mida teeb? → Verb.
Mida/keda? → Object.
Place/time tulevad tavaliselt hiljem.
Küsimustel on oma skeem.

Core idea: Mõlemad sõnad võivad tähendada „see”, kuid this osutab millelegi või tutvustab seda, it aga viitab tavaliselt juba teadaolevale esemele või olukorrale.
Main rule / explanation: This kasutame, kui näitame, osutame millelegi või tutvustame seda praeguses olukorras. It kasutame, kui on juba selge, millisest esemest või olukorrast räägime.
Form / structure: This + noun / This is ... / It + verb or be ...
When / why we use it: Kui tutvustame või osutame esemele: This is my phone. Seejärel võime öelda: It is new. This aitab näidata, it jätkata juba mõistetud objektist rääkimist.
Examples:
Tom plays football after school. → Tom mängib pärast kooli jalgpalli.
My sister reads books every evening. → Mu õde loeb igal õhtul raamatuid.
We study English at home on Sundays. → Me õpime pühapäeviti kodus inglise keelt.
The dog is under the table. → Koer on laua all.
Special cases / exceptions: This võib seista nimisõna ees: this picture. It ei seisa nimisõna ees: mitte it picture. It kasutatakse ka ilma, aja ja mõne olukorra puhul: It's cold. / It's late.
Common mistakes:
❌ It is cold? → ✅ Is it cold?
❌ This is my phone. This is very fast. → ✅ This is my phone. It is very fast.
Don't confuse with: Ära aja this ja it segi varasema this/that/these/those teemaga. Siin on põhiküsimus: kas me näitame/tutvustame objekti või räägime juba teadaolevast objektist?
Quick summary / memory hook:
THIS = näitame / tutvustame.
IT = viitame juba teadaolevale.
This is my phone.
It is new.
This picture is nice.
I like it.

Core idea: Present Simple ja Present Continuous kirjeldavad mõlemad olevikku, kuid vastavad erinevatele küsimustele: kas tegu on tavalise/püsiva olukorraga või toimub tegevus praegu/ajutiselt?
Main rule / explanation: Present Simple — harjumuste, rutiini, faktide ja püsivate olukordade jaoks. Present Continuous — am/is/are + V-ing praegu toimuva või ajutise tegevuse jaoks.
Form / structure: S + V1/V-s. He/She/It + V-s/-es. S + am/is/are + V-ing.
When / why we use it: Present Simple: I work in Kyiv. = tavaline olukord. Present Continuous: I'm working in Kyiv this week. = ajutine olukord.
Examples:
She usually drives to work, but today she's taking the train. → Tavaliselt sõidab ta tööle autoga, kuid täna sõidab rongiga.
We use this software every day. → Me kasutame seda tarkvara iga päev.
We're testing a different system this month. → Sel kuul testime teistsugust süsteemi.
Special cases / exceptions: Vali ajavorm tähenduse, mitte ainult sõnade today/this week järgi. Today võib kirjeldada nii tavalist päeva kui ka praegu toimuvat tegevust.
Common mistakes:
❌ I am work every day. → ✅ I work every day.
❌ I work now. → ✅ I'm working now. (kui tegevus toimub praegu)
❌ He are testing it. → ✅ He is testing it.
Don't confuse with: Present Simple = routine/fact/stable. Present Continuous = now/temporary/in progress.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Tavaliselt/alati → Present Simple.
Praegu/ajutiselt → Present Continuous.
Simple: V1/V-s.
Continuous: am/is/are + V-ing.

Core idea: Present Perfect seob mineviku olevikuga. Räägime varasemast kogemusest, tulemusest või ajavahemikust, mis veel kestab.
Main rule / explanation: Vorm: have/has + V3. Kasutame kogemuse puhul ilma lõpetatud ajahetketa, hiljutise tulemuse ja veel kestva ajavahemiku korral.
Form / structure: Positive: I/you/we/they have + V3; he/she/it has + V3. Negative: haven't/hasn't + V3. Question: Have/Has + subject + V3?
When / why we use it: Experience: I've visited Poland. Result: I've lost my keys. Unfinished period: I've had three meetings today.
Examples:
We've completed the first stage. → Me oleme esimese etapi lõpetanud.
He has never used this tool. → Ta ei ole seda tööriista kunagi kasutanud.
Have you seen my notebook? → Kas sa oled mu vihikut näinud?
I've lost my keys. → Olen oma võtmed kaotanud. (ja praegu ei ole need minu käes)
Special cases / exceptions: Present Perfect ei sobi tavaliselt lõpetatud ajahetkega: yesterday, last Monday. Sellisel juhul kasutame Past Simple-it.
Common mistakes:
❌ I've seen him yesterday. → ✅ I saw him yesterday.
❌ She have finished. → ✅ She has finished.
❌ Did you have seen it? → ✅ Have you seen it?
Don't confuse with: Present Perfect = minevikul on seos now-ga. Past Simple = lõpetatud minevikuhetk.
Quick summary / memory hook:
have/has + V3.
Kogemus.
Tulemus praegu.
Lõpetamata ajavahemik.
Finished past time → tavaliselt Past Simple.
