Core idea: Põhiküsimus: kas meile on tähtis kogemus/seos olevikuga ilma lõpetatud ajata või konkreetne lõpetatud aeg minevikus?
Main rule / explanation: Present Perfect — kui täpne lõpetatud aeg ei ole oluline või olukorral on seos now-ga. Past Simple — kui sündmus kuulub lõpetatud minevikuaega või see aeg on nimetatud.
Form / structure: Present Perfect: have/has + V3. Past Simple: V2 / did + V1.
When / why we use it: Present Perfect: I've seen that film. = kogemus. Past Simple: I saw it last Friday. = konkreetne lõpetatud aeg.
Examples:
Have you ever worked abroad? → Kas sa oled kunagi välismaal töötanud?
Yes, I worked in Germany in 2023. → Jah, ma töötasin 2023. aastal Saksamaal.
I've visited London three times. → Ma olen Londonit kolm korda külastanud.
I visited London last year. → Ma külastasin Londonit eelmisel aastal.
Special cases / exceptions: Yesterday, two days ago, last week, last year ja teised selgelt lõpetatud perioodid nõuavad tavaliselt Past Simple-it.
Common mistakes:
❌ I've met her last week. → ✅ I met her last week.
❌ Did you ever visited Spain? → ✅ Have you ever visited Spain?
❌ I have saw it. → ✅ I have seen it.
Don't confuse with: Ever/never ja kogemus ilma finished time-ita viitavad sageli Present Perfectile. Nimetatud finished time → Past Simple.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Finished past time → Past Simple.
Experience/no finished time → Present Perfect.
Las tähendus otsustab, mitte üksik sõna.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Past Simple räägib minevikus lõpetatud sündmustest ja olukordadest.
Main rule / explanation: Regular verbs saavad tavaliselt lõpu -ed, irregular verbs kasutavad oma V2-vormi. Küsimustes ja eitustes kasutame did/didn't + V1.
Form / structure: Positive: S + V2. Negative: S + didn't + V1. Question: Did + subject + V1?
When / why we use it: Kasutame lõpetatud tegevuste ja olukordade puhul minevikus.
Examples:
We launched the project in May. → Me käivitasime projekti mais.
She didn't attend the meeting. → Ta ei osalenud koosolekul.
Did you send the invoice? → Kas sa saatsid arve?
They visited us last Sunday. → Nad külastasid meid eelmisel pühapäeval.
Special cases / exceptions: Pärast did/didn't on alati V1: Did he go? / He didn't go. Mitte V2.
Common mistakes:
❌ Did he went? → ✅ Did he go?
❌ She didn't attended. → ✅ She didn't attend.
❌ We launch the project yesterday. → ✅ We launched the project yesterday.
Don't confuse with: Ära aja jaatavat lauset segi küsimuse ja eitusega: V2 kasutatakse Past Simple-is ainult jaatuses.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Positive → V2.
Did/didn't → V1.
Past Simple = completed past.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Past Continuous näitab tegevust, mis oli mineviku kindlal hetkel pooleli. Past Simple näitab sageli lõpetatud sündmust, mis toimus selle protsessi ajal.
Main rule / explanation: Past Continuous = was/were + V-ing. Past Simple = V2. Jutustuses annab Past Continuous sageli tausta, Past Simple aga lühema sündmuse.
Form / structure: Past Continuous: I/he/she/it was + V-ing; you/we/they were + V-ing. Past Simple: V2.
When / why we use it: Tegevuse puhul, mis juba toimus: I was checking the figures when the phone rang. Selle katkestanud sündmuse puhul: the phone rang.
Examples:
I was checking the figures when the phone rang. → Ma kontrollisin numbreid, kui telefon helises.
They were discussing the plan when the manager arrived. → Nad arutasid plaani, kui juht saabus.
At 8 p.m. I was still working. → Kell 8 õhtul töötasin ma ikka veel.
Special cases / exceptions: Tavaliselt on lühike lõpetatud sündmus Past Simple-is ja kestev taust Past Continuous-is.
Common mistakes:
❌ I was check the data. → ✅ I was checking the data.
❌ The phone was ringing when I checked the figures. → ✅ The phone rang when I was checking the figures.
Don't confuse with: Past Continuous = protsess/taust. Past Simple = sündmus/lõpetatud tegevus.
Quick summary / memory hook:
was/were + V-ing = tegevus käis.
V2 = sündmus toimus.
Väga kasulik ühendus: was/were doing + when + V2.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Past Perfect näitab, et üks minevikusündmus toimus enne teist minevikusündmust.
Main rule / explanation: Vorm on kõigi isikute puhul sama: had + V3. Varasem sündmus on Past Perfectis, hilisem tavaliselt Past Simple-is.
Form / structure: Subject + had + V3. Negative: had not/hadn't + V3. Question: Had + subject + V3?
When / why we use it: Kui on oluline näidata kahe minevikusündmuse järjekorda: The meeting had started before I arrived.
Examples:
The meeting had started before I arrived. → Koosolek oli juba alanud enne, kui ma saabusin.
She had already left when I called. → Ta oli juba lahkunud, kui ma helistasin.
They had finished the work before lunch. → Nad olid töö enne lõunat lõpetanud.
Special cases / exceptions: Ära kasuta Past Perfecti automaatselt igas minevikulauses. Seda on vaja siis, kui „varem kui teine minevik” suhe on oluline.
Common mistakes:
❌ She had went home. → ✅ She had gone home.
❌ I had finished yesterday. (ilma teise minevikusündmuseta on see tavaliselt tarbetu) → ✅ I finished yesterday.
Don't confuse with: Past Perfect = „minevik enne minevikku”. Past Simple = hilisem minevik.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Earlier past → had + V3.
Later past → usually Past Simple.
had = märk „see juhtus varem”.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Will vs be going to: Future
Core idea: Will ja be going to räägivad mõlemad tulevikust, kuid näitavad tavaliselt erinevat vaadet: otsus praegu, juba olemasolev kavatsus või praegustel märkidel põhinev tulemus.
Main rule / explanation: Will kasutatakse sageli kõnehetkel tehtud otsuse, pakkumise, lubaduse ja ennustuse puhul. Going to — juba kujunenud plaani/kavatsuse ning praeguste märkide põhjal tehtud ennustuse puhul.
Form / structure: Will + V1. Be going to: am/is/are + going to + V1.
When / why we use it: Telefon heliseb → I'll answer it. = otsus praegu. I'm going to call him after lunch. = plaan on juba olemas.
Examples:
The phone is ringing. I'll answer it. → Telefon heliseb. Ma vastan.
I'm going to call him after lunch. → Ma kavatsen talle pärast lõunat helistada.
I'll help you with that. → Ma aitan sind sellega.
Look at those clouds — it's going to rain. → Vaata neid pilvi — kohe hakkab vihma sadama.
Special cases / exceptions: Mõlemad vormid võivad päriselus kattuda. Vali vorm tähenduse, mitte jäiga „üks vorm = üks kasutus” reegli järgi.
Common mistakes:
❌ I going to call him. → ✅ I am going to call him.
❌ She will to help. → ✅ She will help.
❌ It is going rain. → ✅ It is going to rain.
Don't confuse with: Will — otsus/pakkumine/lubadus/ennustus. Going to — varasem plaan või praegustel märkidel põhinev ennustus.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Will + V1.
be going to + V1.
Now decision → will.
Already planned / visible signs → going to.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Present Continuous võib rääkida tulevikust, kui sündmus on juba korraldatud: kohtumine, sõit, kokkulepe.
Main rule / explanation: Vorm jääb tavaliseks Present Continuousiks: am/is/are + V-ing. Tuleviku tähendus selgub tavaliselt kontekstist või tulevikuajamäärusest.
Form / structure: Subject + am/is/are + V-ing + future time.
When / why we use it: Eelnevalt korraldatud tulevaste sündmuste puhul: appointments, meetings, travel ja muud kindlad kokkulepped.
Examples:
I'm meeting the client at ten tomorrow. → Kohtun kliendiga homme kell kümme.
We're flying to Warsaw on Friday. → Lendame reedel Varssavisse.
I'm meeting Anna tomorrow. → Kohtun homme Annaga.
Special cases / exceptions: Ilma kontekstita mõistetakse Present Continuousit tavaliselt olevikuna. Tuleviku puhul aitavad tomorrow, on Friday, next week jne.
Common mistakes:
❌ I meeting the client tomorrow. → ✅ I'm meeting the client tomorrow.
❌ She is meet him on Friday. → ✅ She is meeting him on Friday.
Don't confuse with: Juba korraldatud plaan → Present Continuous. Will võib kõlada otsuse/ennustusena, going to aga kavatsusena.
Quick summary / memory hook:
am/is/are + V-ing.
Tulevik = tavaliselt juba arranged.
I'm meeting..., We're flying...
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Review of all verb tenses A2
Core idea: Tuleta meelde kogu A2 süsteem: erinevad ajavormid vastavad erinevatele küsimustele harjumuse, protsessi, lõpetatud mineviku, olevikuga seose ja tuleviku kohta.
Main rule / explanation: Present Simple — routine/fact. Present Continuous — now/temporary. Past Simple — completed past. Past Continuous — action in progress in past. Present Perfect — past connected with now/experience. Past Perfect — earlier past. Will/going to/Present Continuous — erinevad tulevikutähendused.
Form / structure: Present Simple: V1/V-s. Present Continuous: am/is/are + V-ing. Past Simple: V2. Past Continuous: was/were + V-ing. Present Perfect: have/has + V3. Past Perfect: had + V3. Future: will + V1 / be going to + V1 / am/is/are + V-ing.
When / why we use it: Vali ajavorm tähenduse järgi: routine, now, finished past, process in past, connection with now, earlier past või future meaning.
Examples:
I usually work from home, but I'm working at the office today. → Tavaliselt töötan kodus, kuid täna töötan kontoris.
I finished the report yesterday. → Lõpetasin eile aruande.
I've already sent it. → Olen selle juba saatnud.
I was checking the data when my manager called. → Kontrollisin andmeid, kui mu juht helistas.
Special cases / exceptions: Ära vali ajavormi ainult ühe märksõna, näiteks today või this week, järgi. Kõigepealt otsusta, mida kõneleja tahab näidata.
Common mistakes:
❌ Ära õpi „yesterday = alati Past Simple” kui ainsat reeglit ilma tähenduseta.
✅ Määra kõigepealt: habit, now, finished past, connection with now, earlier past, future arrangement.
Don't confuse with: See on kordamistund: võrdle vorme ja tähendusi, mitte ainult lõppe.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Routine → Present Simple.
Now/temporary → Present Continuous.
Finished past → Past Simple.
Past process → Past Continuous.
Past + now → Present Perfect.
Past before past → Past Perfect.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Have to, don’t have to, must, mustn’t
Core idea: Have to, must, don't have to ja mustn't räägivad reeglitest ja kohustusest, kuid ei tähenda sama.
Main rule / explanation: Have to — kohustus reegli, nõude või olukorra tõttu. Don't have to — kohustus puudub. Must — tugev vajadus. Mustn't — keeld.
Form / structure: Have to + V1. Don't have to + V1. Must + V1. Mustn't + V1.
When / why we use it: Väline reegel: We have to wear badges. Kohustuse puudumine: You don't have to come early. Tugev nõue: You must check the figures. Keeld: You mustn't share this password.
Examples:
We have to wear badges here. → Siin peame kandma töötõendeid.
You don't have to come early. → Sa ei pea vara tulema.
You must check the figures. → Sa pead numbrid üle kontrollima.
You mustn't share this password. → Sa ei tohi seda parooli jagada.
Special cases / exceptions: Kõige tähtsam erinevus: don't have to = ei pea tegema; mustn't = ei tohi teha.
Common mistakes:
❌ You don't have to go = „sul on keelatud minna”. → Ei: see tähendab „sa ei pea minema”.
❌ She must to leave. → ✅ She must leave.
Don't confuse with: Don't have to ≠ mustn't. Need on vastandlikud ideed: kohustuse puudumine ja keeld.
Quick summary / memory hook:
have to = peab.
don't have to = ei pea.
must = peab / on tingimata vaja.
mustn't = ei tohi.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Should annab nõu või näitab, et miski on mõistlik/ootuspärane. Shouldn't ütleb, et midagi ei tasu teha.
Main rule / explanation: Pärast should ja shouldn't kasutatakse V1.
Form / structure: Positive: should + V1. Negative: shouldn't + V1. Question: Should + subject + V1?
When / why we use it: Nõuande, soovituse või ootuse puhul: You should back up the file. Should I call the customer?
Examples:
You should back up the file. → Sa peaksid failist varukoopia tegema.
We shouldn't ignore this warning. → Me ei peaks seda hoiatust ignoreerima.
Should I call the customer? → Kas ma peaksin kliendile helistama?
Special cases / exceptions: Should ei tähenda ranget keeldu. See on nõuanne või mõistlik tegevus.
Common mistakes:
❌ You should to check it. → ✅ You should check it.
❌ She should checks it. → ✅ She should check it.
Don't confuse with: Should on tähenduselt nõrgem kui must: should = nõuanne; must = tugev vajadus.
Quick summary / memory hook:
should + V1 = peaks / tuleks.
shouldn't + V1 = ei peaks / ei tasuks.
Pärast should ei panda kunagi to-d.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Might räägib võimalusest, kuid ilma kindluseta: midagi võib juhtuda, aga võib ka mitte juhtuda.
Main rule / explanation: Vorm: might + V1. Eitus: might not + V1.
Form / structure: Positive: might + V1. Negative: might not + V1. Question forms depend on context; the core lesson is possibility.
When / why we use it: Kasutame, kui kõneleja ei ole tulemuses kindel.
Examples:
The meeting might finish early. → Koosolek võib lõppeda varem.
She might not join us today. → Võib-olla ei ühine ta meiega täna.
It might rain later. → Võib-olla sajab hiljem vihma.
Special cases / exceptions: Might väljendab tavaliselt väiksemat kindlust kui kindel väide.
Common mistakes:
❌ might to go → ✅ might go.
❌ She might goes. → ✅ She might go.
❌ He might not comes. → ✅ He might not come.
Don't confuse with: May väljendab samuti võimalust; järgmine õppetund võrdleb may ja might-i.
Quick summary / memory hook:
might + V1.
might not + V1.
Might = võimalik, kuid kindlust pole.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: May and might: What’s the difference?
Core idea: May ja might väljendavad võimalikkust; may võib väljendada ka luba.
Main rule / explanation: may/might + V1
Form / structure: may/might + V1
When / why we use it: Kasutame võimalikkuse või loa väljendamiseks.
Examples:
We may need more time. → Võib-olla vajame rohkem aega.
We might arrive late. → Võib-olla jõuame hilja.
May I come in? → Kas ma võin sisse tulla?
It may rain later. → Hiljem võib vihma sadada.
Special cases / exceptions: May ei väljenda ainult tulevikku; kontekst näitab, kas tegu on võimalikkuse või loaga.
Common mistakes:
❌ May I to come in? → ✅ May I come in?
❌ She may goes. → ✅ She may go.
❌ Might to rain. → ✅ Might rain.
Don't confuse with: May/might väljendavad võimalikkust; may võib väljendada luba. Might kõlab sageli veidi ebakindlamalt.
Quick summary / memory hook:
may/might + V1 = võimalikkus.
May I...? = luba.
Might = tavaliselt ettevaatlikum võimalikkus.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Used to, didn’t use to: Past habits and states
Core idea: Used to näitab varasemat harjumust või seisundit, mis oli varem tõsi, kuid nüüd enam ei ole.
Main rule / explanation: Jaatus: used to + V1. Eitus: didn't use to + V1. Küsimus: Did + subject + use to + V1?
Form / structure: Positive: used to + V1. Negative: didn't use to + V1. Question: Did you use to + V1?
When / why we use it: Vanade harjumuste ja seisundite puhul, mis on muutunud.
Examples:
We used to meet every Friday. → Varem saime igal reedel kokku.
She didn't use to drive. → Varem ei juhtinud ta autot.
Did they use to live here? → Kas nad elasid varem siin?
Special cases / exceptions: Pärast did/didn't kasutame use, mitte used.
Common mistakes:
❌ Did you used to work here? → ✅ Did you use to work here?
❌ She didn't used to like coffee. → ✅ She didn't use to like coffee.
Don't confuse with: Used to räägib minevikust, mis ei ole enam praegu tavaline või tõsi.
Quick summary / memory hook:
used to + V1 = varem oli nii.
didn't use to + V1 = varem ei olnud nii.
Did ... use to? = kas varem oli nii?
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: How to use the verb ‘go’ in English
Core idea: Go-l on mitu sagedast mudelit. Põhitähendus on kuhugi liikumine, kuid go esineb ka tegevuste nimedes ja mõnes plaanitud liikumise kontekstis.
Main rule / explanation: Go + place: go home, go to work. Go + V-ing tegevuste puhul: go shopping, go swimming. Go esineb ka plaanitud liikumise/osalemise kontekstis.
Form / structure: go + destination. go + V-ing (activities).
When / why we use it: Liikumine: I go to work. Tegevus: They went shopping. Plaan/liikumine: We're going to the conference.
Examples:
I go to work by bus. → Ma sõidan bussiga tööle.
They went shopping after lunch. → Pärast lõunasööki läksid nad ostlema.
Are you going to the gym? → Kas sa lähed jõusaali?
Special cases / exceptions: Õpi selliseid väljendeid tervikuna: eessõna või järgnev vorm võib muutuda.
Common mistakes:
❌ go to home → ✅ go home.
❌ go shop → ✅ go shopping.
❌ They went to shopping. → ✅ They went shopping.
Don't confuse with: Ära proovi go-d kõigis fraasides ühe eesti sõnaga tõlkida. Vaata kogu ühendit.
Quick summary / memory hook:
go home / go to work.
go shopping / go swimming.
Õpi go-ühendeid tervikuna.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: The different uses of the verb ‘get’
Core idea: Get on väga sage verb, millel on mitu tähendust. Täpne tähendus sõltub tugevalt kõrval olevatest sõnadest.
Main rule / explanation: Get võib tähendada become, receive/obtain ja kõnekeeles ka arrive.
Form / structure: get + adjective = become. get + noun = receive/obtain. get + place = arrive.
When / why we use it: Change: get tired, get better. Receive: get an email. Arrive: get home, get to work.
Examples:
I got an email from the client. → Ma sain kliendilt e-kirja.
She gets tired after long meetings. → Ta väsib pärast pikki koosolekuid.
What time did you get home? → Mis kell sa koju jõudsid?
I hope you get better soon. → Loodan, et saad varsti terveks.
Special cases / exceptions: Täpse tähenduse määrab kontekst. Get-il ei ole kõigis olukordades üht tõlget.
Common mistakes:
❌ get to home → ✅ get home.
❌ I get an angry. → ✅ I get angry.
❌ She gets a email. → ✅ She gets an email.
Don't confuse with: Õpi get-i koos ümbrusega: get tired, get an email, get home.
Quick summary / memory hook:
get + adjective → muutuma.
get + noun → saama.
get + place → saabuma/jõudma.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Do ja make tõlgitakse mõlemad sageli sõnaga „tegema”, kuid inglise keeles moodustavad nad erinevaid püsiväljendeid.
Main rule / explanation: Make on sageli seotud loomise, tootmise või tulemusega: make a plan, make a decision, make a mistake. Do on seotud töö, ülesannete ja tegevustega: do homework, do work, do exercise.
Form / structure: make + noun/collocation. do + activity/task/work collocation.
When / why we use it: Ära vaata ainult tõlget „tegema”, vaid õpi püsiväljendit tervikuna.
Examples:
Let's make a plan. → Teeme plaani.
I need to do some work. → Mul on vaja natuke tööd teha.
She made a mistake. → Ta tegi vea.
He does his homework every evening. → Ta teeb igal õhtul koduseid ülesandeid.
Special cases / exceptions: See on collocations-teema: universaalset reeglit „alati do” või „alati make” ei ole.
Common mistakes:
❌ make homework → ✅ do homework.
❌ do a decision → ✅ make a decision.
❌ do a mistake → ✅ make a mistake.
Don't confuse with: Õpi do/make koos nimisõnaga ühe püsiväljendina.
Quick summary / memory hook:
make a plan / decision / mistake.
do homework / work / exercise.
Õpi collocations.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Mõned verbid võivad korraga võtta inimese ja asja: kellelegi midagi anda, kellelegi midagi saata või kellelegi midagi näidata.
Main rule / explanation: Skeem 1: verb + person + thing. Paljude verbide puhul on võimalik ka verb + thing + to + person.
Form / structure: give someone something / send someone something / show someone something. Samuti: give something to someone / send something to someone.
When / why we use it: Kui tegevus annab või edastab eseme teisele inimesele.
Examples:
She sent me the report. → Ta saatis mulle aruande.
She sent the report to me. → Ta saatis aruande mulle.
Can you show us the new dashboard? → Kas sa saad meile uut armatuurlauda näidata?
Give me the file. → Anna mulle fail.
Special cases / exceptions: Kõik verbid ei võimalda mõlemat mudelit samal viisil. Õpi konkreetseid levinud ühendusi.
Common mistakes:
❌ She sent to me the report. → ✅ She sent me the report. / She sent the report to me.
❌ Show the new dashboard us. → ✅ Show us the new dashboard.
Don't confuse with: Peamine on mõista, kes saab ja mida saab. Ühes mudelis võib person seista enne thing-i.
Quick summary / memory hook:
verb + person + thing.
verb + thing + to + person.
give/send/show — põhinäited.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Dynamic verbs kirjeldavad tegevust või protsessi. Stative verbs kirjeldavad seisundit: teadmine, omamine, arvamus või eelistus.
Main rule / explanation: Dynamic verbs kirjeldavad sagedamini tegevust või protsessi ja võivad olla Continuous-is. Stative verbs kirjeldavad seisundit ja on sellises tähenduses tavaliselt Simple-is.
Form / structure: Dynamic: work, run, study → võivad olla working/running/studying. Stative: know, have (possession), understand → tavaliselt Simple.
When / why we use it: Kasutame seda teemat, kui tuleb otsustada, kas tegevust saab näidata praegu toimuvana või räägime seisundist, mida tavaliselt Continuous-is ei kasutata.
Examples:
I am running now. → Ma jooksen praegu.
I know the answer. → Ma tean vastust.
She has a bike. → Tal on jalgratas.
We understand the game. → Me saame mängust aru.
I am thinking about my holiday. → Ma mõtlen oma puhkuse peale.
Special cases / exceptions: Mõne verbi tüüp võib sõltuvalt tähendusest muutuda: think, have, see ja teised. Seetõttu vaata alati tähendust.
Common mistakes:
❌ I am knowing the answer. → ✅ I know the answer.
❌ I am having a car. → ✅ I have a car. (omamise tähenduses)
Don't confuse with: Ära tee reeglit „kui praegu, siis alati Continuous”. Kõigepealt kontrolli, kas verb on stative.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Dynamic = tegevus/protsess.
Stative = seisund.
Stative verb-e kasutame tavaliselt Simple-is.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Phrasal verbs: Transitive and intransitive, separable and inseparable
Core idea: Phrasal verb = verb + particle ja kogu ühendil võib olla tähendus, mis erineb verbi tavalisest tähendusest.
Main rule / explanation: Mõned phrasal verbs vajavad object-it (transitive). Mõnda saab jagada, teisi mitte. Seda tuleb õppida koos konkreetse phrasal verb-iga.
Form / structure: turn off the light / turn the light off — separable. look after the customer — inseparable.
When / why we use it: Vaata mitte ainult verbi, vaid kogu phrasal verb-i ja selle mudelit.
Examples:
Please turn off the computer. → Palun lülita arvuti välja.
Please turn the computer off. → Palun lülita arvuti välja.
We looked after the customer. → Me hoolitsesime kliendi eest.
Special cases / exceptions: Kõiki phrasal verbs-e ei saa lahutada. Asesõnaga separable-mudelis: turn it off, mitte turn off it.
Common mistakes:
❌ We looked the customer after. → ✅ We looked after the customer.
❌ Turn off it. → ✅ Turn it off.
Don't confuse with: Peab teadma mitte ainult tõlget, vaid ka: transitive/intransitive, separable/inseparable.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Õpi phrasal verb tervikuna.

Lesson / Topic: First conditional and future time clauses
Core idea: First Conditional näitab reaalset või võimalikku tulevikutingimust ja selle tulemust. Future time clauses räägivad samuti tulevikust, kuid after when/before/after ja sarnaste sõnade järel ei kasutata inglise keeles tavaliselt will-i.
Main rule / explanation: First Conditional: if + Present Simple, will + V1. Future time clause: when/before/after/as soon as/until + Present Simple, pealauses võib olla will.
Form / structure: If + Present Simple, will + V1. I'll + V1 + when + Present Simple.
When / why we use it: Kasutame võimaliku tulevikutingimuse ja selle tulemuse ning when, before, after, as soon as või until järel toimuvate tulevikutegevuste puhul.
Examples:
If I finish my homework, I'll play a game. → Kui ma lõpetan kodutöö, mängin mängu.
When Mum comes home, we'll have dinner. → Kui ema koju tuleb, sööme õhtust.
I'll call you when I arrive. → Helistan sulle, kui kohale jõuan.
If it rains, we'll stay at home. → Kui vihma sajab, jääme koju.
Special cases / exceptions: If-i järel on tingimusosas Present Simple. Tulevikutähendusega when/before/after/as soon as/until järel on samuti tavaliselt Present Simple.
Common mistakes:
❌ If we will finish early, we'll call you. → ✅ If we finish early, we'll call you.
❌ I'll send it when I will finish. → ✅ I'll send it when I finish.
Don't confuse with: Tingimus- või ajalauses ei kasutata will-i lihtsalt sellepärast, et räägime tulevikust.
Quick summary / memory hook:
First Conditional: if + Present Simple → will + V1.
Time clause: when/before/after/etc. + Present Simple.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Second Conditional räägib ebareaalsest, ebatõenäolisest või kujuteldavast olukorrast olevikus või tulevikus.
Main rule / explanation: Vorm: if + Past Simple, would + V1. Siin aitab Past Simple näidata kaugust tegelikkusest; see ei tähenda tingimata minevikku.
Form / structure: If + V2, would + V1. Tingimusosas on võimalik ka were: If I were you...
When / why we use it: Kasutame, kui kujutame ette ebareaalset, ebatõenäolist või hüpoteetilist olukorda praegu või tulevikus.
Examples:
If I had more time, I'd play football. → Kui mul oleks rohkem aega, mängiksin jalgpalli.
If we lived near the park, we'd go there every day. → Kui me elaksime pargi lähedal, käiksime seal iga päev.
If I were you, I'd wait. → Kui ma oleksin sinu asemel, ootaksin.
If she knew the answer, she'd tell us. → Kui ta teaks vastust, ütleks ta meile.
Special cases / exceptions: Korrektses ja ettevaatlikus keeles võib hüpoteetilises tingimuslauses kasutada were-vormi eri isikute puhul: If I were you.
Common mistakes:
❌ If I would have more time, I'd study. → ✅ If I had more time, I'd study.
❌ If I had more time, I learn another language. → ✅ If I had more time, I'd learn another language.
Don't confuse with: Ära aja Second Conditional'i Past-vormi segi tavalise minevikujutustusega.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Second Conditional: if + Past Simple → would + V1.
Kujuteldav/ebatõenäoline olevik või tulevik.

Lesson / Topic: Present and past simple passive: be + past participle
Core idea: Passive Voice keskendub tegevusele või tulemusele, mitte sellele, kes tegevuse teeb.
Main rule / explanation: Present Simple Passive = am/is/are + V3. Past Simple Passive = was/were + V3.
Form / structure: Present: am/is/are + V3. Past: was/were + V3.
When / why we use it: Kasutame, kui olulisem on, mis objektiga juhtus, mitte kes tegevuse tegi.
Examples:
The reports are checked every day. → Aruandeid kontrollitakse iga päev.
The data is stored on a server. → Andmeid hoitakse serveris.
The documents were signed last week. → Dokumendid allkirjastati eelmisel nädalal.
The report was checked yesterday. → Aruannet kontrolliti eile.
Special cases / exceptions: Passive sisaldab alati be + V3. Ainult V3 ei tee lausest passive-lauset.
Common mistakes:
❌ The reports checked every day. → ✅ The reports are checked every day.
❌ The report was check yesterday. → ✅ The report was checked yesterday.
Don't confuse with: Active: keegi teeb tegevuse. Passive: objekt või tulemus muutub sõnumi keskpunktiks.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Present passive → am/is/are + V3.
Past passive → was/were + V3.
be + V3 = võti.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Reported Speech annab edasi kellegi teise sõnad mitte otsese tsitaadina, vaid meie lause sees.
Main rule / explanation: Kui reporting verb on minevikus, nihkub algne aeg sageli ühe sammu võrra tagasi. Samuti võivad muutuda asesõnad ja ajaväljendid.
Form / structure: Direct: “I am busy.” → Reported: She said (that) she was busy. Direct: “I'll call tomorrow.” → Reported: Anna said she'd call the next day.
When / why we use it: Kasutame, kui räägime kellelegi edasi, mida teine inimene ütles.
Examples:
Tom said, 'I need help.' → Tom said that he needed help. → Tom ütles, et tal on abi vaja.
Anna said, 'I'll call tomorrow.' → Anna said she'd call the next day. → Anna ütles, et helistab järgmisel päeval.
Special cases / exceptions: Ära muuda iga aega mehaaniliselt. Backshift sõltub tähendusest ja kontekstist. Ka asesõnad ja ajaväljendid sõltuvad olukorrast.
Common mistakes:
❌ Tom said I am busy. (kui on vaja edasi anda minevikus öeldut) → ✅ Tom said he was busy.
❌ Anna said she'd call tomorrow. (kui „homme” ei ole enam sama päev) → ✅ Anna said she'd call the next day.
Don't confuse with: Direct speech = kõneleja täpsed sõnad. Reported speech = anname tema sõnumi edasi.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Sageli: reporting verb in past → tense backshift.
Jälgi pronouns ja time expressions.
Tähendus on tähtsam kui mehaanika.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Tegevuse eesmärgi väljendamiseks kasutatakse inglise keeles sageli to + V1 või for + noun.
Main rule / explanation: To + V1 näitab tegevuse eesmärki. For + noun/pronoun näitab kasutusotstarvet või eesmärki.
Form / structure: to + V1 = purpose of action. for + noun/pronoun = purpose/intended use.
When / why we use it: Kasutame, kui selgitame, miks keegi midagi teeb või milleks mingi ese mõeldud on.
Examples:
I went to the shop to buy milk. → Läksin poodi piima ostma.
I opened the book to read. → Avasin raamatu lugemiseks.
This bag is for school. → See kott on kooli jaoks.
This brush is for painting. → See pintsel on maalimiseks.
Special cases / exceptions: Eesmärgi puhul tuleb pärast to-d V1. Pärast for-i ei saa selles mudelis lihtsalt V1 panna: I went there to talk. For + noun/gerund kasutatakse otstarbe või kasutuse kohta.
Common mistakes:
❌ I went there for talk. → ✅ I went there to talk.
❌ I opened the file for check the figures. → ✅ I opened the file to check the figures.
Don't confuse with: Eesmärgi to + V1. Selle mudeli for + noun/pronoun.
Quick summary / memory hook:
to + V1 = tegevuse eesmärk.
for + noun = otstarve/kasutus.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Pärast üht verbi ei ole järgmise verbi vorm alati sama. Mõned verbid nõuavad to + V1, mõned V-ing-vormi.
Main rule / explanation: Infinitive: want to leave, decide to stay, hope to improve. Gerund: enjoy reading, avoid making, finish working. Mõni verb võimaldab mõlemat vormi, mõnikord erineva tähendusega.
Form / structure: Verb + to + V1. Verb + V-ing. Mõned verbs + either form.
When / why we use it: Kasutame, kui ühe verbi järel tuleb panna teine verb ja tuleb valida to + V1 või V-ing vahel.
Examples:
I want to swim. → Ma tahan ujuda.
She decided to stay. → Ta otsustas jääda.
We hope to win. → Loodame võita.
I enjoy reading. → Mulle meeldib lugeda.
He finished playing. → Ta lõpetas mängimise.
Special cases / exceptions: Esimese verbi järel olev vorm on osa verb pattern-ist. Seda tuleb õppida koos esimese verbiga, mitte valida ainult tõlke järgi.
Common mistakes:
❌ I enjoy to work here. → ✅ I enjoy working here.
❌ I decided going home. → ✅ I decided to go home.
❌ We hope finishing soon. → ✅ We hope to finish soon.
Don't confuse with: See on nagu sõnaraamatu mudel: want to do, enjoy doing, finish doing, decide to do.
Quick summary / memory hook:
want/decide/hope + to + V1.
enjoy/avoid/finish + V-ing.
Õpi verb patterns.

Lesson / Topic: Subject pronouns, object pronouns, possessive pronouns, possessive adjectives
Core idea: Inglise keeles on neli põhirühma: subject pronouns, object pronouns, possessive adjectives ja possessive pronouns.
Main rule / explanation: Subject teeb tegevuse: I, you, he... Object saab tegevuse või seisab pärast eessõna: me, him... Possessive adjective seisab nimisõna ees: my book. Possessive pronoun asendab nimisõnafraasi: mine.
Form / structure: Subject: I/you/he/she/it/we/they. Object: me/you/him/her/it/us/them. Possessive adjective: my/your/his/her/its/our/their. Possessive pronoun: mine/yours/his/hers/ours/theirs.
When / why we use it: Kasutame, kui on vaja näidata, kes teeb tegevuse, kellele see on suunatud või kellele miski kuulub.
Examples:
She helped me. → Ta aitas mind.
I saw them at school. → Ma nägin neid koolis.
This is my book. → See on minu raamat.
The book is mine. → Raamat on minu oma.
We gave her our ball. → Me andsime talle meie palli.
Special cases / exceptions: Possessive adjective vajab tavaliselt nimisõna: my book. Possessive pronoun seisab iseseisvalt: The book is mine.
Common mistakes:
❌ This book is my. → ✅ This book is mine.
❌ Give it to I. → ✅ Give it to me.
❌ That is her book; this one is her. → ✅ That is her book; this one is hers.
Don't confuse with: my = possessive adjective, mine = possessive pronoun. I = subject, me = object.
Quick summary / memory hook:
I → me → my → mine.
he → him → his → his.
she → her → her → hers.
we → us → our → ours.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Something/anything/nothing/everything ja sarnased sõnad võimaldavad rääkida asjadest, inimestest ja kohtadest ilma neid täpselt nimetamata.
Main rule / explanation: Something/someone/somewhere esinevad tavaliselt jaatavates lausetes. Anything/anyone/anywhere esinevad sageli küsimustes ja eitustes. Nothing sisaldab juba eitust.
Form / structure: some- = affirmative tendency. any- = questions/negatives. no- = negative meaning. every- = all.
When / why we use it: Kasutame, kui räägime inimesest, asjast või kohast seda täpselt nimetamata: keegi, miski, kusagil, mitte keegi, mitte miski jne.
Examples:
I want something to eat. → Ma tahan midagi süüa.
Did you see anyone? → Kas sa nägid kedagi?
We didn't find anything. → Me ei leidnud midagi.
Nobody called me. → Keegi ei helistanud mulle.
Everything is ready. → Kõik on valmis.
Special cases / exceptions: Tavalises inglise keeles ei panda nothing-iga veel üht eitust: Nothing happened, mitte Nothing didn't happen.
Common mistakes:
❌ I didn't see nothing. → ✅ I didn't see anything. / I saw nothing.
❌ Nobody didn't call. → ✅ Nobody called. / Nobody called me.
Don't confuse with: Any- ei tähenda alati sõna-sõnalt „midagi/kedagi”; seda kasutatakse sageli küsimustes ja eitustes.
Quick summary / memory hook:
some- → sageli positive.
any- → sageli question/negative.
no- → already negative.
every- → all.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Much, many, little, few, some, any: Quantifiers
Core idea: Quantifiers näitavad kogust ja peavad sobima nimisõna tüübiga.
Main rule / explanation: Many ja few käivad plural countable nimisõnadega. Much ja little — uncountable nimisõnadega. Some esineb sageli jaatavates lausetes; any sageli küsimustes ja eitustes.
Form / structure: many + plural countable. few + plural countable. much + uncountable. little + uncountable. some/any + appropriate noun.
When / why we use it: Kasutame, kui on vaja öelda, kui palju midagi on: palju, vähe, natuke, mõned.
Examples:
There are many books on the shelf. → Riiulil on palju raamatuid.
We don't have much time. → Meil ei ole palju aega.
I have a few friends here. → Mul on siin mõned sõbrad.
There is a little juice left. → Mahla on natuke alles.
Do you have any questions? → Kas sul on küsimusi?
Special cases / exceptions: Quantifier'i valik algab küsimusest: kas nimisõna on countable või uncountable?
Common mistakes:
❌ much options → ✅ many options.
❌ many information → ✅ much information.
❌ a few information → ✅ a little information.
Don't confuse with: See jätkab A1 koguste teemat, kuid siin peab kindlalt eristama countable/uncountable ja lähedasi quantifier'e.
Quick summary / memory hook:
many/few → plural countable.
much/little → uncountable.
some/any → vastavalt konstruktsioonile.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Too, too much, too many, enough
Core idea: Too tähendab „rohkem kui vaja/soovitatav”. Enough tähendab „nii palju või sellisel määral, kui vaja”.
Main rule / explanation: Too + adjective/adverb. Too much + uncountable noun. Too many + plural countable noun. Enough + noun, kuid adjective/adverb + enough.
Form / structure: too + adjective/adverb. too much + uncountable. too many + plural countable. enough + noun. adjective/adverb + enough.
When / why we use it: Kasutame, kui räägime sellest, et midagi on rohkem kui vaja, või et kogus/aste on piisav.
Examples:
The bag is too heavy. → Kott on liiga raske.
There are too many toys here. → Siin on liiga palju mänguasju.
We have too much homework. → Meil on liiga palju kodutööd.
We have enough time. → Meil on piisavalt aega.
The box is big enough. → Kast on piisavalt suur.
Special cases / exceptions: Enough'i asukoht on tähtis: enough time, kuid clear enough. Nimisõna puhul seisab enough enne nimisõna; adjective/adverb'i puhul pärast seda.
Common mistakes:
❌ enough clear → ✅ clear enough.
❌ too much errors → ✅ too many errors.
❌ too many work → ✅ too much work.
Don't confuse with: Too = üle normi. Enough = piisav kogus või aste.
Quick summary / memory hook:
too = üle normi.
enough = piisavalt.
enough time, but clear enough.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Most, most of ja the most näevad sarnased välja, kuid täidavad erinevat ülesannet.
Main rule / explanation: Most + plural/uncountable noun teeb üldise väite. Most of + determiner/pronoun räägib konkreetsest rühmast. The most on superlative.
Form / structure: Most + noun. Most of + the/my/these/us... The most + adjective.
When / why we use it: Üldiselt: Most customers prefer email. Konkreetsest rühmast: Most of our customers prefer email. Superlatiiv: the most useful feature.
Examples:
Most customers prefer email. → Enamik kliente eelistab e-posti.
Most of our customers prefer email. → Enamik meie kliente eelistab e-posti.
This is the most useful report. → See on kõige kasulikum aruanne.
Special cases / exceptions: Pärast most of-i on tavaliselt vaja determinerit/pronoomenit: the, my, these, us jne.
Common mistakes:
❌ Most of customers... → ✅ Most customers... / Most of the customers...
❌ This is most useful feature. → ✅ This is the most useful feature.
Don't confuse with: Most = üldine enamus. Most of = konkreetse rühma enamus. The most = superlatiiv.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Most + noun = generally.
Most of + specific group.
the most + adjective = superlative.

Lesson / Topic: Defining relative clauses: Who, which, that, where
Core idea: Defining relative clause täpsustab, millisest konkreetsest inimesest või asjast räägime.
Main rule / explanation: Who — inimeste puhul. Which/that — asjade puhul tavalistes defining clauses. Where — kohtade puhul.
Form / structure: person + who + clause. thing + which/that + clause. place + where + clause.
When / why we use it: Kasutame, kui on vaja täpsustada, millisest inimesest, asjast või kohast räägime.
Examples:
The girl who won the race is my friend. → Tüdruk, kes võistluse võitis, on minu sõber.
The dog that I saw was very big. → Koer, keda ma nägin, oli väga suur.
This is the park where we play. → See on park, kus me mängime.
The book that you gave me is funny. → Raamat, mille sa mulle andsid, on naljakas.
Special cases / exceptions: Ära lisa teist subject-it pärast who/which/that, kui suhtesõna on juba vajalik lauseosa.
Common mistakes:
❌ The analyst who she prepared the report... → ✅ The analyst who prepared the report...
❌ The file that you sent it... → ✅ The file that you sent...
Don't confuse with: Relative clause vastab küsimusele „milline inimene/asi/koht täpselt?”
Quick summary / memory hook:
who → people.
which/that → things.
where → places.

Lesson / Topic: So, neither: so am I, neither do I, etc.
Core idea: So ja neither võimaldavad lühidalt näidata, et oleme teise inimese väitega või eitusega nõus.
Main rule / explanation: Positive agreement: So + auxiliary + subject. Negative agreement: Neither + auxiliary + subject. Abiverb peab vastama esimesele lausele.
Form / structure: So am I. / So do I. / So can I. / So have I. Neither do I. / Neither have I.
When / why we use it: Kasutame, kui tahame lühidalt öelda „mina ka” või „mina ka mitte”, kasutades sama abiverbi.
Examples:
'I am happy.' — 'So am I.' → „Ma olen õnnelik.” — „Mina ka.”
'I like pizza.' — 'So do I.' → „Mulle meeldib pitsa.” — „Mulle ka.”
'I don't play chess.' — 'Neither do I.' → „Ma ei mängi malet.” — „Mina ka mitte.”
'She can swim.' — 'So can I.' → „Ta oskab ujuda.” — „Mina ka.”
Special cases / exceptions: Ära kasuta do-d automaatselt. Vaata algset lauset: be, do, have või modal.
Common mistakes:
❌ I am tired. — So do I. → ✅ So am I.
❌ He hasn't finished. — Neither do I. → ✅ Neither have I.
Don't confuse with: See ei ole uus ajavorm, vaid lühike nõustumisstruktuur.
Quick summary / memory hook:
So = positive agreement.
Neither = negative agreement.
Auxiliary must match.

Lesson / Topic: Auxiliary verbs: do, be and have
Core idea: Auxiliary verbs do, be ja have aitavad moodustada grammatilisi konstruktsioone. Mõnikord ei kanna nad peamist tähendust, vaid näitavad küsimust, eitust või ajavormi.
Main rule / explanation: Do/does/did aitavad tavaliste verbide küsimustes ja eitustes. Be moodustab Continuous-i ja Passive'i. Have/has/had moodustab Perfect-i.
Form / structure: Do: Do you work? / She doesn't work. Be: is working / was checked. Have: have finished / had left.
When / why we use it: Kasutame, kui on vaja mõista do, be ja have rolli küsimustes, eitustes, Continuous-is, Passive'is ja Perfect-is.
Examples:
Do you like cats? → Kas sulle meeldivad kassid?
She is reading. → Ta loeb praegu.
They have finished the game. → Nad on mängu lõpetanud.
He doesn't play tennis. → Ta ei mängi tennist.
We have seen this film. → Me oleme seda filmi näinud.
Special cases / exceptions: Auxiliary verb on osa grammatikakonstruktsioonist. Seda ei ole vaja iga kord eraldi sõnana tõlkida.
Common mistakes:
❌ She does working. → ✅ She is working.
❌ Did you worked? → ✅ Did you work?
❌ They have finish. → ✅ They have finished.
Don't confuse with: Do = questions/negatives with ordinary verbs. Be = continuous/passive. Have = perfect.
Quick summary / memory hook:
do → questions/negatives.
be → continuous/passive.
have → perfect.

Lesson / Topic: Comparative and superlative adjectives and adverbs
Core idea: Comparative võrdleb kahte objekti. Superlative tõstab ühe objekti rühmast esile. Sama erinevus töötab ka adverb'ide puhul.
Main rule / explanation: Comparative: faster, more carefully, better than. Superlative: the fastest, the most carefully, the best. Mõned vormid on ebareeglipärased.
Form / structure: Adjective/adverb + -er / more. Superlative: the + -est / the most. Irregular: good → better → the best; badly → worse → the worst.
When / why we use it: Kasutame, kui võrdleme kahte eset/tegevust või tõstame ühe esile kogu rühmast.
Examples:
My dog is faster than yours. → Minu koer on sinu omast kiirem.
This book is more interesting than that one. → See raamat on huvitavam kui too.
Anna runs faster than me. → Anna jookseb minust kiiremini.
This is the best cake. → See on parim kook.
He sings the most beautifully in the group. → Ta laulab rühmas kõige ilusamalt.
Special cases / exceptions: Ära sega adjective'i ja adverb'i mudeleid. Good → adjective; well → adverb. Mõnel sõnal on ebareeglipärane vorm.
Common mistakes:
❌ She works more quick. → ✅ She works more quickly.
❌ This is the better option of all three. → ✅ This is the best option of the three.
❌ He is more better. → ✅ He is better.
Don't confuse with: Comparative = 2. Superlative = 1 grupist. Vaata, kas kirjeldad noun'i või action'it.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Comparative → two.
Superlative → group.
Adjective and adverb may use different forms.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: No longer, any longer ja anymore näitavad, et miski ei ole enam tõsi.
Main rule / explanation: No longer tähendab „enam mitte”. Any longer/anymore esinevad tavaliselt eitavas lauses: not ... any longer / not ... anymore.
Form / structure: No longer + verb. Do/does not + verb + anymore/any longer.
When / why we use it: Kasutame, kui ütleme, et miski ei toimu enam või ei ole enam tõsi.
Examples:
I no longer play that game. → Ma ei mängi seda mängu enam.
We don't watch cartoons anymore. → Me ei vaata multikaid enam.
She doesn't live here any longer. → Ta ei ela siin enam.
He no longer wears glasses. → Ta ei kanna enam prille.
Special cases / exceptions: Sõnajärg on tähtis: no longer seisab tavaliselt enne põhiverbi, anymore/any longer aga tavaliselt pärast öeldist eitavas konstruktsioonis.
Common mistakes:
❌ I work no longer there. → ✅ I no longer work there.
❌ I no longer don't work there. → ✅ I no longer work there.
❌ I work there anymore. → ✅ I don't work there anymore.
Don't confuse with: Ära kasuta anymore't no longer'i vaba asendusena igas positsioonis. Vaata lause struktuuri.
Quick summary / memory hook:
no longer + verb.
not + verb + anymore/any longer.

Lesson / Topic: However, although, because, so, and time connectors
Core idea: Need sõnad seovad ideid erinevalt: contrast, reason, result või time.
Main rule / explanation: Although toob vastanduse ühe konstruktsiooni sisse. However seob vastandlikke ideid lausete või osade vahel. Because = põhjus. So = tulemus. When/while/before/after/as soon as/until = aeg.
Form / structure: Although + clause. Sentence. However, sentence. because + reason. so + result. Time connector + clause.
When / why we use it: Kasutame, kui seome ideid ja näitame vastandust, põhjust, tulemust või aega.
Examples:
Although it was raining, we went outside. → Kuigi sadas vihma, läksime õue.
It was raining. However, we went outside. → Sadas vihma. Kuid me läksime õue.
We stayed home because it was cold. → Jäime koju, sest oli külm.
It was late, so we went home. → Oli hilja, seega läksime koju.
When Mum arrives, we'll eat. → Kui ema saabub, sööme.
Special cases / exceptions: Although ja however ei ole sama grammatikaga. Ära pane however'it kohta, kus on vaja although-konstruktsiooni.
Common mistakes:
❌ Although it was late. However, we continued. (mitte ühes konstruktsioonis) → ✅ Although it was late, we continued.
❌ We stayed, so we needed more time. → ✅ We stayed because we needed more time. / We needed more time, so we stayed.
Don't confuse with: Määra kõigepealt seos: contrast, reason, result või time.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Although/however = contrast.
because = reason.
so = result.
time connectors = sequence.

Lesson / Topic: Prepositions of movement: Along, across, over, etc.
Core idea: Prepositions of movement näitavad liikumise teed, mitte ainult asukohta.
Main rule / explanation: Along — liikumine piki midagi. Across — ühelt poolelt teisele. Through — läbi sisemise ruumi. Over — üle või üle takistuse.
Form / structure: move/walk/run + along/across/through/over + noun.
When / why we use it: Kasutame, kui kirjeldame liikumisteed: piki midagi, läbi ruumi, ühelt poolelt teisele või üle takistuse.
Examples:
We walked along the river. → Me kõndisime mööda jõge.
We ran across the street. → Me jooksime üle tänava.
The train went through the tunnel. → Rong läks läbi tunneli.
The cat jumped over the box. → Kass hüppas üle kasti.
Special cases / exceptions: Vali eessõna liikumistrajektoori, mitte ainult ühe eestikeelse või venekeelse tõlke järgi.
Common mistakes:
❌ We walked through the street. (kui mõte on ühest tänavapoolelt teisele) → ✅ We walked across the street.
❌ The train went across the tunnel. → ✅ The train went through the tunnel.
Don't confuse with: Along = piki. Across = ühelt poolelt teisele. Through = läbi ruumi. Over = üle/takistusest üle.
Quick summary / memory hook:
along = piki.
across = ühelt poolelt teisele.
through = seest läbi.
over = üle/pealt.
