Lesson / Topic: On time vs In time, At the end vs In the end.
Core idea: On time ja in time on sarnased, kuid üks on seotud graafikuga ja teine sellega, kas jõudsime õigeks ajaks. At the end ja in the end erinevad samuti.
Main rule / explanation: On time = täpselt graafikujärgselt õigel ajal. In time = piisavalt vara, et mitte hiljaks jääda. At the end = perioodi/koha/sündmuse lõpus. In the end = lõpuks / lõpptulemusena.
Form / structure: on time = schedule. in time + for/to = before too late. at the end of + period/event. in the end = finally.
When / why we use it: Kasutame, kui on vaja eristada „graafikujärgselt õigel ajal”, „õigeks ajaks”, „lõpus” ja „lõppkokkuvõttes”.
Examples:
The school bus arrived on time. → Koolibuss saabus õigel ajal.
We arrived in time for the film. → Me jõudsime filmi jaoks piisavalt vara.
At the end of the story, the hero went home. → Loo lõpus läks kangelane koju.
In the end, we chose the blue team. → Lõpuks valisime sinise meeskonna.
Special cases / exceptions: Peamine vihje: schedule → on time. Enough early → in time. Final part → at the end. Final result/decision → in the end.
Common mistakes:
❌ The train arrived in time. (kui tähtis on graafik) → ✅ The train arrived on time.
❌ At the end, she accepted the offer. → ✅ In the end, she accepted the offer.
Don't confuse with: Ära tõlgi neid väljendeid sõna-sõnalt. Õpi neid valmis paaridena.
Quick summary / memory hook:
on time = graafiku järgi.
in time = mitte liiga hilja.
at the end = lõpus.
in the end = lõpuks.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Asking questions in English: Question forms
Core idea: Inglise küsimustel on oma struktuur. Tavaliselt seisab auxiliary või be subject'i ees.
Main rule / explanation: Yes/no questions: be/auxiliary + subject. Wh-questions: question word + auxiliary/be + subject + main verb. Modal questions: modal + subject + V1.
Form / structure: Are you ready? Do you work here? Did she call? Where do they live? Why is he late? Can you help?
When / why we use it: Kasutame, kui esitame tavalisi Yes/No- ja Wh-küsimusi ning peame abiverbi õigesti paigutama.
Examples:
Do you like music? → Kas sulle meeldib muusika?
Where does Sam live? → Kus Sam elab?
What are they doing? → Mida nad teevad?
Can you help me? → Kas sa saad mind aidata?
Why is the dog barking? → Miks koer haugub?
Special cases / exceptions: Tavalises direct question-is jääb auxiliary subject'i ette. Ära kopeeri tavalise väite sõnajärge.
Common mistakes:
❌ Where they live? → ✅ Where do they live?
❌ Why she is late? → ✅ Why is she late?
❌ What you need? → ✅ What do you need?
Don't confuse with: Leia kõigepealt auxiliary/be/modal. Seejärel subject. Siis main verb, kui see on vajalik.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Auxiliary/be before subject.
Wh-word comes first in Wh-questions.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Kui who/what on subject, ehitatakse küsimus teisiti: tavaliselt ei ole do/does/did vaja. Kui who/what on object, on vaja auxiliary't. Kõnekeelses inglise keeles läheb eessõna sageli lõppu.
Main rule / explanation: Subject question: Who called you? Object question: Who did you call? Preposition often at the end: Who did you speak to?
Form / structure: Subject question: Who/What + verb ...? Object question: Who/What + do/does/did + subject + V1 ...? + preposition at end if needed.
When / why we use it: Kasutame, kui who/what on tegevuse tegija või kui who/what on objekt ja küsimuses on eessõna.
Examples:
Who called you? → Kes sulle helistas?
Who did you call? → Kellele sa helistasid?
What happened? → Mis juhtus?
Who did you speak to? → Kellega sa rääkisid?
What are you looking at? → Mida sa vaatad?
Special cases / exceptions: Ära lisa did-i, kui who/what on juba subject: Who called? on tavaline neutraalne vorm. Formaalses keeles on võimalik To whom did you speak?, kuid everyday English-is on tavalisem Who did you speak to?
Common mistakes:
❌ Who did call you? → ✅ Who called you?
❌ What did happen? → ✅ What happened? (tavaline neutraalne variant)
❌ To who did you speak? → ✅ Who did you speak to? / To whom did you speak?
Don't confuse with: Küsi kõigepealt: kas who/what teeb tegevuse või saab selle? Kui teeb → tavaliselt ilma do/does/did.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Who/what as subject → usually no do/does/did.
Who/what as object → auxiliary needed.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Present Simple ja Present Continuous kirjeldavad mõlemad olevikku, kuid Simple näitab harjumuspärast või stabiilset olukorda, Continuous aga praegu toimuvat, ajutist või muutuvat tegevust.
Main rule / explanation: Present Simple — harjumused, päevakava, faktid ja püsivad seisundid. Present Continuous = am/is/are + V-ing millegi praegu toimuva, ajutise või muutuva protsessi kohta.
Form / structure: S + V1/V-s. S + am/is/are + V-ing.
When / why we use it: Võrdle: I work with sales data. / I'm working with sales data this week.
Examples:
I usually start work at eight. → Alustan tavaliselt tööd kell kaheksa.
Our office opens at nine. → Meie kontor avatakse kell üheksa.
I'm working from home this week. → Sel nädalal töötan kodust.
Special cases / exceptions: Stative verbs such as know, believe, understand, need and belong kasutatakse sageli Simple-vormis.
Common mistakes:
❌ I am know the answer. → ✅ I know the answer.
❌ He work from home this week. → ✅ He is working from home this week.
Don't confuse with: Kas tegu on routine/stable või temporary/in progress?
Quick summary / memory hook:
Simple = routine/fact/stable.
Continuous = now/temporary/changing.
Stative verbs → tavaliselt Simple.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Future forms – will, be going to, present continuous
Core idea: Kolm tulevikuvormi erinevad eelkõige tähenduse poolest: spontaanne otsus või lubadus, juba kujunenud kavatsus või kokkulepitud korraldus.
Main rule / explanation: Will — spontaanne otsus, pakkumine, lubadus või ennustus. Going to — juba tehtud kavatsus ja praegustel märkidel põhinev ennustus. Present Continuous — kokkulepitud sündmus.
Form / structure: will + V1. am/is/are + going to + V1. am/is/are + V-ing + future time.
When / why we use it: I'll call her. = decision/promise. I'm going to call her. = intention. I'm calling her at three. = arrangement.
Examples:
The phone is ringing. I'll answer it. → Telefon heliseb. Ma vastan.
We're going to change the process. → Me kavatseme protsessi muuta.
I'm meeting the client at three tomorrow. → Kohtun homme kell kolm kliendiga.
Special cases / exceptions: Vormid võivad osaliselt kattuda. Vali vorm kõneleja tähenduse, mitte ainult ühe ajamääruse põhjal.
Common mistakes:
❌ I will to call her. → ✅ I will call her.
❌ She going to change it. → ✅ She is going to change it.
Don't confuse with: Will = decision/promise/prediction. Going to = intention/evidence. Present Continuous = arranged event.
Quick summary / memory hook:
will → otsus/lubadus/ennustus.
going to → kavatsus/märkide põhine ennustus.
Present Continuous → kokkulepe.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Past Simple seob sündmuse lõpetatud minevikuga. Present Perfect seob minevikus toimunu olevikuga või räägib kogemusest ilma lõpetatud ajahetketa.
Main rule / explanation: Past Simple — completed event in finished past time. Present Perfect — experience, recent result or unfinished period connected with now.
Form / structure: Past Simple: V2 / did + V1. Present Perfect: have/has + V3.
When / why we use it: I visited Prague last year. = lõpetatud minevik. I've visited Prague three times. = kogemus.
Examples:
I worked in Germany in 2023. → Töötasin Saksamaal 2023. aastal.
I've worked abroad several times. → Olen töötanud välismaal mitu korda.
She has just finished the report. → Ta lõpetas just aruande.
Special cases / exceptions: Yesterday, last month, in 2020, two days ago kasutatakse tavaliselt koos Past Simple'iga. Ever, never, before, so far esinevad sageli Present Perfectiga ilma lõpetatud ajata.
Common mistakes:
❌ I've seen him yesterday. → ✅ I saw him yesterday.
❌ I have visited Rome in 2020. → ✅ I visited Rome in 2020.
Don't confuse with: Finished past time → Past Simple. Experience/current connection → Present Perfect.
Quick summary / memory hook:
finished time → Past Simple.
experience/result/unfinished period → Present Perfect.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Present perfect simple and present perfect continuous
Core idea: Present Perfect Simple näitab sagedamini tulemust, tegevuste arvu või saavutust. Present Perfect Continuous keskendub rohkem protsessile, kestusele või hiljutisele tegevusele.
Main rule / explanation: Simple = have/has + V3. Continuous = have/has been + V-ing.
Form / structure: Present Perfect Simple: have/has + V3. Present Perfect Continuous: have/has been + V-ing.
When / why we use it: I've written three emails. = result/number. I've been writing emails all morning. = activity/duration.
Examples:
I've cleaned the room. → Olen toa koristanud.
I've been cleaning the room. → Olen tuba koristanud.
She has written five messages. → Ta on kirjutanud viis sõnumit.
Special cases / exceptions: Stative verbs kasutatakse tavaliselt Simple-vormis: I've known her for years. Ära vali Continuous-vormi ainult sellepärast, et tegevus kestab kaua.
Common mistakes:
❌ I've been knowing her for years. → ✅ I've known her for years.
❌ I have been write emails. → ✅ I have been writing emails.
Don't confuse with: Simple → result/number/achievement. Continuous → activity/duration/recent process.
Quick summary / memory hook:
have/has + V3 = tulemus/arv.
have/has been + V-ing = protsess/kestus.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: During, for ja while on seotud ajaga, kuid nende järel tulevad erinevad konstruktsioonid.
Main rule / explanation: During + noun/period/event. For + length of time. While + clause with subject + verb.
Form / structure: during + noun. for + period of time. while + S + V.
When / why we use it: During the meeting. For two hours. While I was working.
Examples:
I fell asleep during the film. → Jäin filmi ajal magama.
We talked for an hour. → Rääkisime tund aega.
She called while I was driving. → Ta helistas, kui ma sõitsin.
Special cases / exceptions: Ära kasuta for-i otse täieliku kõrvallause ees.
Common mistakes:
❌ for I was working → ✅ while I was working.
❌ during two hours → ✅ for two hours.
Don't confuse with: During = mille ajal? For = kui kaua? While = samal ajal kui + lause.
Quick summary / memory hook:
during + noun.
for + duration.
while + clause.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Comparative and superlative adjectives and adverbs
Core idea: Comparative võrdleb kahte objekti, superlative toob rühmas esile kõige kõrgema või madalama tulemuse. See kehtib nii adjectives- kui ka adverb-vormide kohta.
Main rule / explanation: Comparatives: faster, more carefully, better than. Superlatives: the fastest, the most carefully. Määrsõnad kasutavad sageli more/most.
Form / structure: Comparative: -er / more + form + than. Superlative: the + -est / the most + form.
When / why we use it: Kasutame kahe objekti võrdlemiseks või ühe objekti valimiseks rühmast.
Examples:
This version is more stable than the old one. → See versioon on vanast stabiilsem.
She works more efficiently now. → Ta töötab nüüd tõhusamalt.
He is the most experienced analyst. → Ta on kõige kogenum analüütik.
Special cases / exceptions: Mõnel vormil on irregular patterns: well → better → best. Linking verbs järel on vaja adjective'i, tegevuse kirjeldamisel adverbi.
Common mistakes:
❌ She works more quick. → ✅ She works more quickly.
❌ He is most experienced analyst. → ✅ He is the most experienced analyst.
Don't confuse with: Küsi endalt: kas kirjeldan noun/person/state või action?
Quick summary / memory hook:
Comparative → two.
Superlative → group.
Adjective ≠ adverb.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: A/an, the ja artikli puudumine sõltuvad sellest, kas asi on konkreetne või üldine, kas kuulaja seda teab ja kas nimisõna on ainsuses loendatav.
Main rule / explanation: A/an — singular countable, kui asi pole konkreetne või seda mainitakse esimest korda. The — konkreetne või teadaolev asi. No article — sageli mitmuse ja loendamatute nimisõnade üldises tähenduses.
Form / structure: a/an + singular countable. the + specific noun. Ø + plural/uncountable general noun.
When / why we use it: I bought a laptop. The laptop was expensive. Laptops are useful.
Examples:
I bought a laptop yesterday. → Ostsin eile sülearvuti.
The laptop is on my desk. → Sülearvuti on minu laual.
Laptops are useful tools. → Sülearvutid on kasulikud tööriistad.
Technology changes quickly. → Tehnoloogia muutub kiiresti.
Special cases / exceptions: Artikli valik sõltub tähendusest ja kontekstist, mitte ainult tõlkest.
Common mistakes:
❌ I bought laptop. → ✅ I bought a laptop.
❌ A laptop was expensive. → ✅ The laptop was expensive.
Don't confuse with: a = üks, kuid mitte konkreetne. the = konkreetne/teadaolev. Ø = üldine mitmus või loendamatu nimisõna.
Quick summary / memory hook:
a/an = singular non-specific.
the = specific/known.
Ø = general plural/uncountable.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Another, other, others, the other, the others
Core idea: Another, other, others, the other ja the others erinevad arvu, nimisõna olemasolu ja konkreetsuse poolest.
Main rule / explanation: Another = veel üks. Other käib nimisõna ees. Others on asesõna. The other = teine kahest või konkreetne allesjäänud. The others = teadaoleva rühma ülejäänud liikmed.
Form / structure: another + singular noun. other + noun. others — ilma noun'ita. the other + singular. the others — ilma noun'ita.
When / why we use it: Some agreed; others disagreed. One file is correct; the other is broken.
Examples:
Can I have another question? → Kas ma saan veel ühe küsimuse?
We need other options. → Me vajame teisi variante.
Some agreed; others disagreed. → Mõned nõustusid, teised mitte.
The others are ready. → Ülejäänud on valmis.
Special cases / exceptions: Other omadussõnana vajab tavaliselt nimisõna: other ideas. Others asendab nimisõna juba ise.
Common mistakes:
❌ others ideas → ✅ other ideas.
❌ one file... another is broken → ✅ the other is broken.
Don't confuse with: Nimisõna olemasolu on oluline vihje: other + noun, others ilma noun'ita.
Quick summary / memory hook:
another = veel üks.
other + noun.
others = teised.
the other = teine.
the others = ülejäänud.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Can, could, be able to – ability and possibility
Core idea: Can, could ja be able to väljendavad võimet või võimalikkust, kuid neid kasutatakse erinevate aegade ja olukordade puhul.
Main rule / explanation: Can — present ability/possibility. Could — past general ability ja viisakad request'id. Be able to on kasulik siis, kui on vaja teist aega või konstruktsiooni.
Form / structure: can + V1. could + V1. be able to + V1.
When / why we use it: Can = võime praegu. Could = üldine võime minevikus või viisakas palve. Be able to võimaldab moodustada future/perfect vorme.
Examples:
I can drive. → Ma oskan autot juhtida.
I could swim at five. → Ma oskasin viieaastaselt ujuda.
Could you help me? → Kas te saaksite mind aidata?
I'll be able to join later. → Ma saan hiljem liituda.
Special cases / exceptions: Ühe konkreetse eduka minevikusündmuse puhul võib was/were able to rõhutada õnnestunud sooritust.
Common mistakes:
❌ I can to drive. → ✅ I can drive.
❌ I'll can join later. → ✅ I'll be able to join later.
Don't confuse with: Modal → V1. Tuleviku ja muude konstruktsioonide puhul kasutame be able to.
Quick summary / memory hook:
can = present ability.
could = past general ability/polite request.
be able to = flexible form.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: have to, must, should – obligation, prohibition, necessity, advice
Core idea: Have to, must ja should on seotud kohustuse ja nõuandega, kuid nende tugevus ja nõude allikas on erinevad.
Main rule / explanation: Have to — kohustus, mis tuleneb reeglist või olukorrast. Must — tugev vajadus. Should — nõuanne või ootus.
Form / structure: have to + V1. must + V1. should + V1. Negative: don't have to / mustn't / shouldn't.
When / why we use it: Have to tuleb sageli reeglist või olukorrast. Must väljendab tugevat kohustust. Should on nõuanne.
Examples:
We have to wear ID badges. → Me peame kandma töötajakaarte.
You must keep this information private. → Sa pead seda infot saladuses hoidma.
You should check the figures. → Sa peaksid numbrid üle kontrollima.
Special cases / exceptions: Don't have to = kohustus puudub. Mustn't = keeld. Shouldn't = soovitus mitte teha.
Common mistakes:
❌ You don't have to share it = „sul pole lubatud seda jagada”. → Ei: „sa ei pea seda jagama”.
❌ She must to check. → ✅ She must check.
Don't confuse with: Have to/must = obligation. Should = advice. Ära aja segi don't have to ja mustn't.
Quick summary / memory hook:
have to = kohustus.
must = tugev vajadus.
should = nõuanne.
don't have to ≠ mustn't.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Reflexive pronouns näitavad, et subject ja object on sama inimene või asi; mõnikord kasutatakse neid lihtsalt subject'i rõhutamiseks.
Main rule / explanation: Forms: myself, yourself, himself, herself, itself, ourselves, yourselves, themselves. By + reflexive võib tähendada üksinda.
Form / structure: subject + verb + reflexive. by + reflexive.
When / why we use it: Same person: She hurt herself. Emphasis: I did it myself. Alone: I did it by myself.
Examples:
She hurt herself. → Ta sai viga.
I did it myself. → Ma tegin selle ise.
We solved the problem ourselves. → Me lahendasime probleemi ise.
He travelled by himself. → Ta reisis üksi.
Special cases / exceptions: Ära kasuta reflexive pronoun'i tavalise object pronoun'i asemel lihtsalt selleks, et kõlada ametlikumalt.
Common mistakes:
❌ Please contact myself. → ✅ Please contact me.
❌ She told himself. → ✅ She told herself.
Don't confuse with: Reflexive = sama inimene mis subject või rõhutamine. Tavaline object pronoun = me/him/her.
Quick summary / memory hook:
myself/yourself/... = ise / iseennast.
by myself = üksi.
Ära asenda nendega tavalisi object pronouns'e.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: -ed ja -ing adjectives on verbidest moodustatud omadussõnad, kuid kirjeldavad erinevaid asju: inimese tunnet või selle tunde põhjust.
Main rule / explanation: -ed kirjeldab tavaliselt seda, mida inimene tunneb. -ing kirjeldab tavaliselt inimest või asja, mis seda tunnet tekitab.
Form / structure: -ed adjective: bored, interested, confused. -ing adjective: boring, interesting, confusing.
When / why we use it: The task is confusing; the employees are confused.
Examples:
I'm bored. → Mul on igav.
The film is boring. → Film on igav.
The task is confusing. → Ülesanne on segadust tekitav.
The employees are confused. → Töötajad on segaduses.
Special cases / exceptions: I am boring tähendab „ma olen igav / ma tekitan igavust”, mitte „mul on igav”.
Common mistakes:
❌ I am boring. → ✅ I am bored.
❌ The lesson is bored. → ✅ The lesson is boring.
Don't confuse with: -ed = feeling/result in a person. -ing = cause/quality of thing or situation.
Quick summary / memory hook:
-ed → kuidas ma ennast tunnen.
-ing → mis seda tunnet tekitab.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Past simple, past continuous, past perfect
Core idea: Minevikust rääkides võivad kolm vormi töötada koos: Past Simple näitab põhisündmusi, Past Continuous tausta või pooleliolevat tegevust ning Past Perfect midagi, mis toimus veel varem.
Main rule / explanation: Past Simple = completed event. Past Continuous = action in progress/background. Past Perfect = earlier event before another past event.
Form / structure: V2. was/were + V-ing. had + V3.
When / why we use it: The meeting started. People were talking. The manager had left before I arrived.
Examples:
The meeting started at nine. → Koosolek algas kell üheksa.
People were talking when the manager arrived. → Inimesed vestlesid, kui juht saabus.
The manager had left before I arrived. → Juht oli enne minu saabumist lahkunud.
Special cases / exceptions: Past Perfect näitab minevikusündmuste omavahelist järjekorda, mitte lihtsalt „väga ammu” toimunut.
Common mistakes:
❌ Every past sentence should be Past Perfect. → Ei: vaja on vaadata, milline sündmus toimus varem.
❌ I had went. → ✅ I had gone.
Don't confuse with: Timeline: earlier event → Past Perfect; background → Past Continuous; main completed event → Past Simple.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Past Perfect = varem.
Past Continuous = protsess/taust.
Past Simple = põhisündmus.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Review of all intermediate verb tenses (CEFR B1)
Core idea: See on peamiste intermediate verb tenses'ite süsteemne ülevaade. Peamine oskus on valida aeg tähenduse, mitte mehaanilise märksõnade loendi järgi.
Main rule / explanation: Present Simple — routine/fact/stable. Present Continuous — current/temporary. Past Simple — completed past. Past Continuous — past process. Past Perfect — earlier past. Present Perfect — past connected to now. Present Perfect Continuous — activity/duration to now. Future forms have different meanings.
Form / structure: V1/V-s; am/is/are + V-ing; V2; was/were + V-ing; had + V3; have/has + V3; have/has been + V-ing; will/going to/Present Continuous.
When / why we use it: Vaata suhet: usual, now, finished past, process in past, earlier past, connection with now, duration to now või future meaning.
Examples:
I usually work from home. → Töötan tavaliselt kodust.
I'm working at the office today. → Täna töötan kontoris.
I finished the report yesterday. → Lõpetasin aruande eile.
I've already sent it. → Olen selle juba saatnud.
I was checking the data when my manager called. → Kontrollisin andmeid, kui mu juht helistas.
Special cases / exceptions: Ära vali tense'i ainult ühe time expression'i järgi. Kõigepealt määra kindlaks meaning and relationship.
Common mistakes:
❌ today = alati Present Continuous. → Ei.
❌ yesterday = ainus valiku alus. → Vaata kogu konteksti.
Don't confuse with: See õppetund on süsteemi kaart, mitte uus eraldi tense.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Routine → Present Simple.
Now/temp → Present Continuous.
Finished past → Past Simple.
Past process → Past Continuous.
Past before past → Past Perfect.
Past + now → Present Perfect.
Activity/duration + now → Present Perfect Continuous.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: usually, used to, be used to, get used to
Core idea: Usually, used to, be used to ja get used to on sarnased, kuid tähistavad erinevaid ideid: praegune harjumus, vana harjumus või harjumise protsess.
Main rule / explanation: Usually — adverb of frequency. Used to + V1 — vana harjumus/seisund. Be used to + noun/-ing — olema harjunud. Get used to + noun/-ing — harjuma.
Form / structure: usually + verb. used to + V1. be used to + noun/V-ing. get used to + noun/V-ing.
When / why we use it: I usually work at home. = tavaliselt. I used to live there. = varem. I'm used to working late. = olen harjunud. I'm getting used to the new system. = harjun.
Examples:
I usually work at home. → Töötan tavaliselt kodust.
I used to live there. → Ma elasin varem seal.
I'm used to working late. → Olen harjunud hilja töötama.
I'm getting used to the new system. → Harjun uue süsteemiga.
Special cases / exceptions: Pärast be/get used to peab tulema noun või V-ing, mitte infinitive.
Common mistakes:
❌ I'm used to work late. → ✅ I'm used to working late.
❌ I used to working late. → ✅ I used to work late.
Don't confuse with: used to = varem. be used to = juba harjunud. get used to = harjumise protsess. usually = tavaliselt.
Quick summary / memory hook:
usually = now habit.
used to + V1 = past habit/state.
be used to + noun/-ing = accustomed.
get used to + noun/-ing = become accustomed.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Passive näitab tegevust või tulemust siis, kui tegija pole oluline, pole teada või pole peamine fookus.
Main rule / explanation: Passive = form of be + V3. Just be näitab tense'i: is done, was done, has been done, will be done.
Form / structure: Present: is/are + V3. Past: was/were + V3. Perfect: has/have been + V3. Future: will be + V3.
When / why we use it: Vali passive, kui tegevus või tulemus on tähtsam kui tegija. By + agent lisatakse siis, kui tegija on oluline.
Examples:
The data is stored securely. → Andmeid säilitatakse turvaliselt.
The documents were signed yesterday. → Dokumendid allkirjastati eile.
The results will be published tomorrow. → Tulemused avaldatakse homme.
The report was prepared by the finance team. → Aruande koostas finantsmeeskond.
Special cases / exceptions: Täielik passive ei moodustu ilma be + V3-ta.
Common mistakes:
❌ The report written yesterday. → ✅ The report was written yesterday.
❌ The results will published tomorrow. → ✅ The results will be published tomorrow.
Don't confuse with: Kõigepealt määra be-vormi tense, seejärel lisa V3.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Passive = be + V3.
Tense lives in be.
by + agent — kui tegija on oluline.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Active voice keskendub sellele, kes tegevuse teeb. Passive voice keskendub objektile või tulemusele, millele tegevus suunatakse.
Main rule / explanation: Active: subject performs action. Passive: subject receives action; object from active becomes grammatical subject.
Form / structure: Active: The analyst prepared the report. Passive: The report was prepared by the analyst.
When / why we use it: Actor/action important → active. Result/affected object important → passive.
Examples:
The company launched the product. → Ettevõte tõi toote turule.
The product was launched in June. → Toode toodi turule juunis.
The analyst prepared the report. → Analüütik koostas aruande.
The report was prepared by the analyst. → Aruande koostas analüütik.
Special cases / exceptions: Active → passive muutmisel tuleb subject ja object ümber tõsta, mitte lihtsalt be lisada.
Common mistakes: ❌ The analyst was prepared the report. → ✅ The report was prepared by the analyst.
Don't confuse with: Mõtle, kelle või mille tahad peamiseks fookuseks teha. Actor → active. Result/object → passive.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Active = kes tegi.
Passive = mis tehti.
Passive nõuab lause ümberkujundamist.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Modal verbs of deduction – must, might, could, can’t
Core idea: Modal deduction kasutab must, might, could ja can't mitte reeglite, vaid olemasolevate märkide põhjal tehtava loogilise järelduse jaoks.
Main rule / explanation: Must = tugev järeldus. Might/could = võimalik seletus. Can't = tugev järeldus, et miski pole võimalik.
Form / structure: must/might/could/can't + V1 või be.
When / why we use it: The lights are on, so they must be inside. = tugev järeldus. He might be asleep. = võimalikkus. This can't be the final version. = tugev võimatus.
Examples:
The lights are on, so they must be inside. → Tuled põlevad, seega peavad nad tõenäoliselt sees olema.
He might be asleep. → Võib-olla ta magab.
This can't be the final version. → See ei saa olla lõplik versioon.
Special cases / exceptions: Siin tähendab must deduction, mitte obligation. Tähenduse määrab kontekst.
Common mistakes:
❌ He must be inside = alati „ta peab sees olema”. → Siin võib see olla loogiline järeldus.
❌ He might to be asleep. → ✅ He might be asleep.
Don't confuse with: Kõigepealt küsi: kas tegu on reegli või tõendite põhjal tehtud järeldusega? Kui järeldusega, on tegu modal deduction'iga.
Quick summary / memory hook:
must = tugev järeldus.
might/could = võib-olla.
can't = ei saa olla.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: First Conditional ja future time clauses räägivad realistlikust tulevikust. Pärast when/before/after/as soon as/until kasutatakse kõrvallauses tavaliselt olevikuvormi, kuigi tähendus on tulevik.
Main rule / explanation: First Conditional: if + Present Simple, will + V1. Future time clause: connector + Present form; main clause can contain will.
Form / structure: If + Present Simple, will + V1. I'll + V1 + when/before/after/as soon as/until + Present Simple.
When / why we use it: Tingimus: If the client agrees, we'll start. Aeg: I'll call when I arrive.
Examples:
If the client agrees, we'll start Monday. → Kui klient nõustub, alustame esmaspäeval.
I'll send the link as soon as I finish. → Saadan lingi kohe, kui olen valmis.
I'll call when I arrive. → Helistan, kui kohale jõuan.
Special cases / exceptions: Ära pane will-i pärast when/before/after/as soon as/until lihtsalt sellepärast, et tähendus on tulevik.
Common mistakes:
❌ When I will arrive, I'll call. → ✅ When I arrive, I'll call.
❌ If the client will agree, we'll start. → ✅ If the client agrees, we'll start.
Don't confuse with: if-clause = condition. time clause = millal sündmus toimub. Mõlemad dependent clauses võivad tuleviku tähenduses kasutada Presenti.
Quick summary / memory hook:
if + Present → will + V1.
when/before/after/as soon as/until + Present → future meaning.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Second Conditional näitab hüpoteetilist, ebatõenäolist või kujuteldavat olukorda olevikus või tulevikus.
Main rule / explanation: Vorm: if + Past Simple, would + V1. Past-vorm näitab siin distantsi tegelikkusest.
Form / structure: If + V2, would + V1. Advice pattern: If I were you, I'd...
When / why we use it: Kasutame imaginary/unlikely situations puhul.
Examples:
If I had more time, I'd study German. → Kui mul oleks rohkem aega, õpiksin saksa keelt.
If she were here, she'd know what to do. → Kui ta oleks siin, teaks ta, mida teha.
If I were you, I'd wait. → Mina sinu asemel ootaksin.
Special cases / exceptions: If I were you on standardne püsivorm. Were võib esineda formaalsetes hüpoteetilistes lausetes.
Common mistakes:
❌ If I would have more time... → ✅ If I had more time...
❌ If she were here, she will help. → ✅ If she were here, she'd help.
Don't confuse with: Past form ≠ tingimata minevikuaeg. Siin näitab see hypothetical distance'i.
Quick summary / memory hook:
If + Past Simple → would + V1.
Imaginary/unlikely now/future.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: First ja Second Conditional erinevad selle poolest, kuidas kõneleja näeb tingimust: realistlik võimalus või hüpoteetiline/ebatõenäoline olukord.
Main rule / explanation: First = realistic possibility. Second = hypothetical/unlikely situation.
Form / structure: First: if + Present, will + V1. Second: if + Past, would + V1.
When / why we use it: Võrdle: If we have enough time, we'll finish. / If we had more time, we'd redesign it.
Examples:
If we have enough time, we'll finish today. → Kui meil on piisavalt aega, lõpetame täna.
If we had more time, we'd redesign it. → Kui meil oleks rohkem aega, kujundaksime selle ümber.
Special cases / exceptions: Ära kasuta Second Conditionalit automaatselt iga ebakindla olukorra puhul. Oluline on kõneleja vaatenurk.
Common mistakes:
❌ If it rains, we'd cancel. → ✅ If it rains, we'll cancel. (reaalselt võimalik tulevik → First Conditional.)
❌ If I knew it will rain, I would stay home. → ✅ If I knew it would rain, I would stay home. (hüpoteetiline tingimus.)
Don't confuse with: First = real/possible. Second = imagined/unlikely.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Kõigepealt määra meaning.
Real possibility → First.
Hypothetical/unlikely → Second.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Third Conditional räägib ebareaalsest minevikust: tingimus ei täitunud ja seetõttu ei juhtunud ka kujuteldav tulemus.
Main rule / explanation: If + Past Perfect, would have + V3.
Form / structure: If + had + V3, would have + V3.
When / why we use it: Kasutame imagined past condition'i ja result'i puhul.
Examples:
If we had checked the data, we would have found the error. → Kui oleksime andmeid kontrollinud, oleksime vea leidnud.
If she had left earlier, she would have caught the train. → Kui ta oleks varem lahkunud, oleks ta rongile jõudnud.
Special cases / exceptions: If-clause'is ei kasutata standardse Third Conditionali puhul would have'i.
Common mistakes:
❌ If we would have checked... → ✅ If we had checked...
❌ If she had left earlier, she would catch... → ✅ she would have caught...
Don't confuse with: Mõlemad tulemused kuuluvad minevikku ja tegelikkuses neid ei juhtunud.
Quick summary / memory hook:
if + had + V3 → would have + V3.
Imaginary past.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Reported Speech annab kellegi teise sõnad edasi ilma täpset otsest tsitaati kasutamata. Vajaduse korral muutuvad tense, pronouns ja time expressions.
Main rule / explanation: Pärast past reporting verb'i nihkub algne tense sageli tahapoole. Tänased/homsed ajamäärused ja asesõnad võivad muutuda. Reported questions kasutavad statement word order'it.
Form / structure: Direct → reported clause. Question: asked + question word + subject + verb.
When / why we use it: 'I work here.' → He said he worked there. 'Tomorrow' → the next day. She asked where I lived.
Examples:
Tom said, 'I need help.' → Tom ütles, et ta vajab abi.
Anna said, 'I'll call tomorrow.' → Anna ütles, et ta helistab järgmisel päeval.
She asked where I lived. → Ta küsis, kus ma elan.
Special cases / exceptions: Backshift ei ole kõigis kontekstides mehaaniline reegel. Tähendus ja olukord on tähtsamad kui automaatne muutmine.
Common mistakes: ❌ She asked where did I live. → ✅ She asked where I lived.
Don't confuse with: Reported question'is säilib statement'i sõnajärg: where I lived, mitte where did I live.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Annad sõnad edasi, mitte ei tsiteeri.
Jälgi tense'i, pronouns'e ja time words'e.
Reported question → statement order.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Gerund or infinitive – do, to do, doing
Core idea: Pärast erinevaid verbe kasutatakse erinevat pattern'it: to + V1, V-ing või mõlemat. Mõnikord muudab vormi valik ka tähendust.
Main rule / explanation: Mõned verbs võtavad infinitive'i, teised gerundi; mõned lubavad mõlemat. Verbid remember, stop ja try võivad pattern'i muutmisel tähendust muuta.
Form / structure: verb + to + V1. verb + V-ing. Mõned verbs + both with meaning difference.
When / why we use it: Võrdle: Remember to lock the door. / I remember locking the door. / Try to open it. / Try opening it.
Examples:
Remember to lock the door. → Ära unusta ust lukustada.
I remember locking the door. → Ma mäletan, et lukustasin ukse.
Try to open it. → Proovi see avada.
Try opening it. → Proovi see avada (võimaliku lahendusena).
Special cases / exceptions: Ära vali vormi ainult esimese verbi tõlke järgi. Vaata intended meaning'i.
Common mistakes:
❌ I remember to locking the door. → ✅ I remember locking the door.
❌ Try to opening it. → ✅ Try opening it.
Don't confuse with: Verb pattern on konkreetse verbi grammatika osa. Mõnikord muudab see tähendust.
Quick summary / memory hook:
remember + to do / doing ≠ sama tähendus.
stop/try võivad samuti tähendust muuta.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Much, many, a lot, little, few, some, any, no – quantifiers
Core idea: Quantifiers näitavad kogust ja nõuavad õiget nimisõna tüüpi. Oluline on eristada few/little ja a few/a little.
Main rule / explanation: Many, few, a lot of → plural countable. Much, little, a lot of → uncountable. Some esineb sageli jaatavates lausetes; any küsimustes ja eituses, kuid on ka erandeid. No + noun = negative.
Form / structure: many/few + plural countable. much/little + uncountable. a lot of + both. some/any/no + appropriate noun.
When / why we use it: Vali quantifier pärast seda, kui oled kindlaks määranud, kas noun on countable või uncountable, ja millist koguse varjundit vajad.
Examples:
We have few options. → Meil on vähe võimalusi.
There isn't much time. → Meil pole palju aega.
There are no seats left. → Vabu kohti pole jäänud.
I bought some fruit. → Ostsin veidi puuvilju.
Special cases / exceptions: Few/little tähendavad sageli „vähe, ebapiisavalt”. A few/a little kõlavad positiivsemalt: mingi kogus on olemas.
Common mistakes:
❌ little options → ✅ few options.
❌ many information → ✅ much information.
❌ I don't have no time. → ✅ I don't have any time.
Don't confuse with: Kõigepealt countable või uncountable. Seejärel amount/meaning.
Quick summary / memory hook:
many/few → countable plural.
much/little → uncountable.
a few/a little → väike, kuid olemasolev kogus.
no + noun = negative.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: All viitab kolmele või enamale rühmaliikmele tervikuna või loendamatule tervikule. Both viitab kahele.
Main rule / explanation: All employees / all the information. Both options / both of us. Both võib paikneda plural noun'i ees või subject pronoun'i järel.
Form / structure: all + plural/uncountable. both + plural referring to two.
When / why we use it: 2 → both. 3+ või uncountable whole → all.
Examples:
All the reports are ready. → Kõik aruanded on valmis.
Both answers are possible. → Mõlemad vastused on võimalikud.
They both understand the problem. → Nad mõlemad saavad probleemist aru.
Both of us agree. → Me mõlemad oleme nõus.
Special cases / exceptions: Both käib põhitähenduses ainult kahe kohta. All on kolme või enama või loendamatu terviku jaoks.
Common mistakes: ❌ Both options, if there are five options. → ✅ All options.
Don't confuse with: Loenda rühma liikmed: 2 → both; 3+ / whole mass → all.
Quick summary / memory hook:
both = 2.
all = 3+ or whole mass.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Both, either ja neither käivad kahe võimaluse või objekti kohta: mõlemad, kumb tahes kahest või mitte kumbki kahest.
Main rule / explanation: Both = the two together. Either = one of two. Neither = not one and not the other.
Form / structure: both + plural. either + singular noun. neither + singular noun.
When / why we use it: Kasutame siis, kui on täpselt kaks võimalust või objekti.
Examples:
Both solutions work. → Mõlemad lahendused toimivad.
Either solution will work. → Kumbki kahest lahendusest sobib.
Neither solution works. → Kumbki kahest lahendusest ei toimi.
Special cases / exceptions: Basic meaning'us ei kasutata either/neither'it kolme või enama liikmega rühma kohta.
Common mistakes:
❌ Either of five options... → Põhitähenduses on vaja teist quantifier'it.
❌ Neither options works. → ✅ Neither option works.
Don't confuse with: See on kahe elemendi loogika: both = 2, either = 1 kahest, neither = 0 kahest.
Quick summary / memory hook:
2 items:
both = 2 together.
either = 1 of 2.
neither = 0 of 2.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Any, no ja none võivad väljendada puudumist või määramata kogust, kuid neid kasutatakse erinevates konstruktsioonides.
Main rule / explanation: Any + noun võib kontekstist sõltuvalt tähendada one/some/whichever. No + noun muudab lause eitavaks. None on pronoun, mis asendab noun phrase'i.
Form / structure: any + noun. no + noun. none without noun.
When / why we use it: There aren't any tickets. / There are no tickets. / None came.
Examples:
There aren't any tickets. → Pileteid pole.
There are no tickets. → Pileteid pole.
I invited five people, but none came. → Kutsusin viis inimest, kuid keegi ei tulnud.
Special cases / exceptions: Standard English'is välditakse double negative'it: I don't have any, mitte I don't have none.
Common mistakes:
❌ I don't have none. → ✅ I don't have any. / I have none.
❌ None tickets are left. → ✅ No tickets are left.
Don't confuse with: no vajab noun'i. none asendab noun phrase'i.
Quick summary / memory hook:
any + noun.
no + noun.
none = pronoun.
No double negatives.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: So, such, such a, so much, so many
Core idea: So, such, so much ja so many võimendavad määra või kogust, kuid nende järel kasutatakse erinevaid konstruktsioone.
Main rule / explanation: So + adjective/adverb. Such + noun phrase. So much + uncountable. So many + plural countable.
Form / structure: so + adj/adv. such + noun phrase. so much + uncountable. so many + plural countable.
When / why we use it: Võrdle so ja such järel olevat vormi: so difficult; such a difficult task.
Examples:
It was so cold. → Oli nii külm.
It was such a cold day. → See oli nii külm päev.
We had so much work. → Meil oli nii palju tööd.
There were so many emails. → E-kirju oli nii palju.
Special cases / exceptions: Pärast so ei saa panna otse a + noun phrase'i: mitte so a difficult task.
Common mistakes:
❌ so a difficult task → ✅ such a difficult task.
❌ so many work → ✅ so much work.
❌ such cold → ✅ so cold / such a cold day.
Don't confuse with: Kui kohe järgneb adjective/adverb → so. Kui järgneb noun phrase → such. Koguse puhul → so much/many.
Quick summary / memory hook:
so + adj/adv.
such + noun phrase.
so much + uncountable.
so many + plural countable.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Defining relative clause on vajalik noun'i tuvastamiseks. Non-defining lisab täiendavat infot ja eraldatakse komadega.
Main rule / explanation: Defining = essential identifying information, no commas. Non-defining = extra information, commas. Who — people; which — things. That on tavaliselt defining.
Form / structure: Defining: noun + who/which/that + clause. Non-defining: noun, who/which + clause,.
When / why we use it: Võrdle: The report that you sent... ja My laptop, which is three years old,...
Examples:
The report that you sent is useful. → Aruanne, mille sa saatsid, on kasulik.
My laptop, which is three years old, still works well. → Mu sülearvuti, mis on kolm aastat vana, töötab endiselt hästi.
The employee who joined yesterday needs access. → Töötaja, kes eile liitus, vajab juurdepääsu.
Special cases / exceptions: Ära pane essential identifying information'i ümber komasid. That'i ei kasutata tavaliselt standardsetes non-defining clauses'ites.
Common mistakes:
❌ My laptop, that is three years old,... → ✅ My laptop, which is three years old,...
❌ The employee, who joined yesterday, needs access. (kui clause identifies employee) → ✅ The employee who joined yesterday needs access.
Don't confuse with: Defining = „milline täpselt?”. Non-defining = lisamärkus.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Defining = essential, no commas.
Non-defining = extra, commas.
who → people; which → things.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Question tags: Aren't you? don't you?
Core idea: Question tag muudab väite lühikeseks kinnitavaks küsimuseks: „eks ole?” / „kas pole?”
Main rule / explanation: Positive statement saab tavaliselt negative tag'i. Negative statement saab positive tag'i. Kasutame sama auxiliary/modal'i ja sama subject pronoun'i.
Form / structure: Positive + negative tag. Negative + positive tag. Auxiliary/modal must match; with ordinary present/past use do/does/did.
When / why we use it: You're ready, aren't you? You don't know, do you?
Examples:
You're ready, aren't you? → Sa oled valmis, eks?
You don't know, do you? → Sa ei tea, eks?
She can drive, can't she? → Ta oskab autot juhtida, eks?
They weren't late, were they? → Nad ei hilinenud, eks?
Special cases / exceptions: Tag peab sobima põhilause tense'i, auxiliary/modal'i ja subject pronoun'iga.
Common mistakes:
❌ She can drive, doesn't she? → ✅ She can drive, can't she?
❌ They weren't late, weren't they? → ✅ They weren't late, were they?
Don't confuse with: Kõigepealt leia põhilause auxiliary/modal, seejärel tee polarity vastupidiseks.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Positive → negative tag.
Negative → positive tag.
Match auxiliary + tense + pronoun.

Lesson / Topic: Clauses of contrast, purpose and reason
Core idea: Contrast-, purpose- ja reason-klauslid vastavad eri küsimustele: millele vaatamata? milleks? miks?
Main rule / explanation: Although/even though väljendavad ootamatut vastandust. To/in order to/so that väljendavad eesmärki. Because/since/as juhatavad sisse põhjuse.
Form / structure: although/even though + clause. to/in order to + V1. so that + clause. because/since/as + clause.
When / why we use it: Võrdle goal ja cause: We left early to avoid traffic. / We changed the plan because the weather was bad.
Examples:
Although it was late, we continued. → Kuigi oli hilja, jätkasime.
We left early to avoid traffic. → Lahkusime vara, et liiklust vältida.
We changed the plan because the weather was bad. → Muutsime plaani, sest ilm oli halb.
Special cases / exceptions: Purpose ja reason ei ole sama asi: purpose = goal; reason = cause.
Common mistakes:
❌ We left early because catch the train. → ✅ We left early to catch the train.
❌ We left early to the weather was bad. → ✅ We left early because the weather was bad.
Don't confuse with: Küsi: what was the goal? → purpose. Why did it happen? → reason. Unexpected contrast? → although/even though.
Quick summary / memory hook:
contrast = although/even though.
purpose = to/in order to/so that.
reason = because/since/as.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Mõned verbs moodustavad kindla ühenduse konkreetse preposition'iga. See preposition on verb pattern'i osa.
Main rule / explanation: Jäta verb + preposition meelde tervikuna: depend on, listen to, wait for, belong to.
Form / structure: verb + preposition + noun/pronoun/V-ing as appropriate.
When / why we use it: Ära tõlgi preposition'it eraldi — õpi kogu chunk tervikuna.
Examples:
It depends on the price. → See sõltub hinnast.
Please listen to me. → Palun kuula mind.
We're waiting for the client. → Me ootame klienti.
This bag belongs to Anna. → See kott kuulub Annale.
Special cases / exceptions: Preposition'it ei saa sageli vene keelest üks-ühele loogiliselt tõlkida.
Common mistakes:
❌ listen me → ✅ listen to me.
❌ depend of → ✅ depend on.
❌ wait the client → ✅ wait for the client.
Don't confuse with: Ära õpi ainult verbi. Õpi verb + preposition ühe leksikaal-grammatilise üksusena.
Quick summary / memory hook:
depend on.
listen to.
wait for.
belong to.
Õpi chunk tervikuna.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Paljud adjectives nõuavad samuti kindlat preposition'it. See on püsikonstruktsiooni osa.
Main rule / explanation: Levinud patterns: interested in, good at, afraid of, responsible for.
Form / structure: adjective + preposition + noun/pronoun/V-ing as appropriate.
When / why we use it: Õiget preposition'it ei saa sageli vene tõlke põhjal ette ennustada.
Examples:
She's interested in analytics. → Talle pakub analytics huvi.
He's good at explaining complex ideas. → Ta oskab keerukaid ideid hästi selgitada.
I'm responsible for this report. → Mina vastutan selle aruande eest.
She is afraid of making mistakes. → Ta kardab vigu teha.
Special cases / exceptions: Õpi kogu väljendit, mitte ainult adjective'i eraldi.
Common mistakes:
❌ interested on → ✅ interested in.
❌ good in explaining → ✅ good at explaining.
❌ responsible of → ✅ responsible for.
Don't confuse with: Preposition belongs to the adjective pattern.
Quick summary / memory hook:
interested in.
good at.
afraid of.
responsible for.
Õpi whole phrase.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Had better ja It's time väljendavad tugevat nõuannet või seda, et praegu on juba aeg midagi teha.
Main rule / explanation: Had better + V1 = tugev nõuanne võimaliku negatiivse tagajärje vihjega. It's time + Past Simple = praegu on juba aeg.
Form / structure: had better + V1. had better not + V1. It's time + subject + Past Simple.
When / why we use it: You'd better save the file. = parem salvesta. It's time we started. = meil on juba aeg alustada.
Examples:
You'd better save the file. → Sul oleks parem fail salvestada.
You'd better not miss the train. → Sul oleks parem rongist mitte maha jääda.
It's time we started. → Meil on juba aeg alustada.
Special cases / exceptions: Pärast had better tuleb V1 ilma to-ta. Past Simple pärast It's time'i ei tähenda tingimata minevikku.
Common mistakes:
❌ You'd better to leave. → ✅ You'd better leave.
❌ It's time we start. → ✅ It's time we started.
Don't confuse with: Had better on tugevam kui tavaline should. It's time + Past Simple näitab, et tegevus peaks juba toimuma.
Quick summary / memory hook:
had better + V1.
had better not + V1.
It's time + Past Simple.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: for, since, from – what's the difference?
Core idea: For, since ja from näitavad kestust või ajavahemiku algust, kuid vastavad erinevatele küsimustele.
Main rule / explanation: For = duration. Since = starting point continuing to now/another reference time. From = starting point, often with an endpoint or range.
Form / structure: for + length. since + starting point. from + starting point (+ to/until).
When / why we use it: For vastab küsimusele „kui kaua?”. Since — „mis ajast?”. From moodustab sageli ajavahemiku.
Examples:
I've lived here for five years. → Olen siin elanud viis aastat.
I've worked here since 2021. → Olen siin töötanud alates 2021. aastast.
The office is open from nine to five. → Kontor on avatud üheksast viieni.
Special cases / exceptions: Ära aja segi duration'i ja starting point'i.
Common mistakes:
❌ I've lived here since five years. → ✅ I've lived here for five years.
❌ I've worked here for 2021. → ✅ I've worked here since 2021.
Don't confuse with: for = amount of time. since = starting point. from = starting point/range.
Quick summary / memory hook:
for = how long.
since = from when.
from = starting point, often + to.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: B1 Phrasal verbs 1 – Exercises and explanation
Core idea: Phrasal verbs ühendavad verbi ja particle'i ning saavad sageli tähenduse, mida ei saa üksikute sõnade tähendustest kokku panna.
Main rule / explanation: Õpi phrasal verb koos selle tähenduse ja grammar pattern'iga. Siin on olulised get up, find out, look for, turn on, carry on.
Form / structure: verb + particle. Pattern sõltub konkreetsest phrasal verb'ist.
When / why we use it: Vaata kogu phrase'i ja konteksti.
Examples:
I found out about the change yesterday. → Sain eile muutusest teada.
Please turn on the monitor. → Palun lülita monitor sisse.
We need to look for a solution. → Me peame lahendust otsima.
Please carry on. → Palun jätka.
Special cases / exceptions: Ära tõlgi iga sõna eraldi: look for ≠ lihtsalt look + for.
Common mistakes:
❌ Turn on = alati „pöörama”. → Ei: context'is tähendab turn on = sisse lülitama.
❌ look + for = tavaline sõnaühend. → Ei, look for = otsima.
Don't confuse with: Üks particle muudab algse verbi tähendust.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Õpi whole phrasal verb.
get up.
find out.
look for.
turn on.
carry on.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: B1 Phrasal verbs 2 – Exercises and explanation
Core idea: B1 tasemel on oluline teada mitte ainult phrasal verb'i tähendust, vaid ka seda, kas object võib verbi ja particle'i vahel paikneda.
Main rule / explanation: Mõned phrasal verbs on separable: pick the file up / pick up the file. Teised on inseparable: look after the child. Pronoun'iga seisab separable object tavaliselt verbi ja particle'i vahel.
Form / structure: separable: pick + object + up / pick up + object. With pronoun: pick it up. Inseparable: look after + object.
When / why we use it: Õpi meaning + object pattern + separability.
Examples:
Please pick up the documents. → Palun võta dokumendid üles.
Please pick the documents up. → Palun võta dokumendid üles.
She looks after the new employee. → Ta hoolitseb uue töötaja eest.
Pick it up. → Võta see üles.
Special cases / exceptions: Separable phrasal verb'ide puhul paikneb pronoun tavaliselt verbi ja particle'i vahel.
Common mistakes:
❌ pick up it → ✅ pick it up.
❌ look the child after → ✅ look after the child.
Don't confuse with: Pattern is part of vocabulary: separable or inseparable.
Quick summary / memory hook:
separable → pick it up.
inseparable → look after it.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: B1 Phrasal verbs 3 – Exercises and explanation
Core idea: Phrasal verbs moodustavad tähendusrühmi ning sama verb võib erinevate particle'itega saada erineva tähenduse.
Main rule / explanation: Võrdle whole phrase'i ja konteksti: take off, take up, take over — kolm erinevat konstruktsiooni.
Form / structure: verb + particle = separate lexical item; meaning depends on combination.
When / why we use it: Ära kanna ühe phrasal verb'i tähendust üle teisele, millel on sama verb.
Examples:
The plane took off. → Lennuk tõusis õhku.
She took up a new hobby. → Ta hakkas tegelema uue hobiga.
The new manager took over the project. → Uus juht võttis projekti enda kontrolli alla.
Special cases / exceptions: Sama verb + teine particle = uus väljend.
Common mistakes:
❌ take up = õhku tõusma. → Ei: take off = õhku tõusma.
❌ take over = hobiga alustama. → Ei: take up = millegagi tegelema hakkama.
Don't confuse with: Kontekst ja particle määravad meaning'i.
Quick summary / memory hook:
take off = õhku tõusma.
take up = millegagi tegelema hakkama.
take over = kontrolli üle võtma.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Would rather ja would sooner väljendavad eelistust erinevate võimaluste vahel.
Main rule / explanation: Would rather + V1 ühe subject'i puhul. Kui tegevuse teeb teine inimene: I'd rather you + Past Simple. Would sooner on sarnase tähendusega ja kõlab sageli formaalsemalt.
Form / structure: would rather + V1. would rather + person + Past Simple. would sooner + V1.
When / why we use it: Same subject: I'd rather stay. Different subject: I'd rather you came tomorrow.
Examples:
I'd rather stay. → Ma jääksin pigem.
I'd rather you came tomorrow. → Ma eelistaksin, et sa tuleksid homme.
I'd sooner wait. → Ma pigem ootaksin.
Special cases / exceptions: Sama subject'i puhul ei panda would rather'i järel to-d.
Common mistakes:
❌ I'd rather to stay. → ✅ I'd rather stay.
❌ I'd rather you come tomorrow. → ✅ I'd rather you came tomorrow.
Don't confuse with: Same subject → rather + V1. Different subject → rather + person + Past Simple.
Quick summary / memory hook:
would rather = eelistaksin.
would sooner = sarnane, formaalsem.
Pärast rather → V1.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Compound adjectives with numbers: A two-day trip
Core idea: Arv + nimisõna võivad moodustada compound adjective'i teise nimisõna ees: two-day, five-minute, ten-page.
Main rule / explanation: Enne noun'i kirjutatakse compound adjective tavaliselt sidekriipsudega ning compound'i sees olev noun jääb singular-vormi.
Form / structure: number + singular noun + hyphens + main noun.
When / why we use it: Number+noun unit toimib ühe adjective'ina enne põhinimisõna.
Examples:
We had a three-hour meeting. → Meil oli kolmetunnine koosolek.
a five-minute break. → viieminutiline paus.
a ten-page report. → kümneleheküljeline aruanne.
a two-day trip. → kahepäevane reis.
Special cases / exceptions: Compound'i sees olev noun jääb singular-vormi: two-day, mitte two-days.
Common mistakes:
❌ a two-days trip → ✅ a two-day trip.
❌ a five-minutes break → ✅ a five-minute break.
Don't confuse with: Võrdle: The trip lasted two days. / It was a two-day trip.
Quick summary / memory hook:
number + singular noun.
tavaliselt hyphens before main noun.
two-day, five-minute, ten-page.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Inglise keeles on küsimustel erinevad struktuurid sõltuvalt sellest, milline info on teadmata ja mida tahame rõhutada.
Main rule / explanation: Yes/No questions algavad tavaliselt auxiliary/modal'iga. Wh-questions algavad question word'iga. Kui who/what on ise subject, pole do/does/did tavaliselt vaja. Preposition liigub everyday English'is sageli lõppu.
Form / structure: Yes/No: auxiliary/modal + subject + verb. Wh: question word + auxiliary/be + subject + verb. Subject question: Who/What + verb. Preposition: Who are you talking to?
When / why we use it: Vali struktuur küsimuse tüübi ja selle järgi, kes tegevuse teeb.
Examples:
Do you work here? → Kas sa töötad siin?
Are they waiting for us? → Kas nad ootavad meid?
Where do you work? → Kus sa töötad?
Who called you? → Kes sulle helistas?
Who did you call? → Kellele sa helistasid?
Who are you talking to? → Kellega sa räägid?
Special cases / exceptions: Formaalsemas stiilis võib preposition olla enne whom/which: To whom are you speaking? Everyday English'is on tavalisem Who are you speaking to?
Common mistakes:
❌ Where you work? → ✅ Where do you work?
❌ Who did call you? → ✅ Who called you? (kui who = subject)
❌ What are you looking? → ✅ What are you looking for?
Don't confuse with: Kõigepealt küsi: mis on teadmata — subject, object, place, time jne? See annab vihje struktuurile.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Yes/No → auxiliary/modal first.
Wh-question → question word first.
Who/what as subject → usually no do/does/did.
Preposition often goes to the end.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Indirect question on viisakam ja vähem otsene viis info küsimiseks. See on eriti kasulik tööl, teeninduses ja formaalsetes vestlustes.
Main rule / explanation: Pärast sissejuhatavat fraasi kasutatakse embedded question'is tavalist väitlause sõnajärge. Yes/No küsimustes kasutatakse if või whether.
Form / structure: Could you tell me + statement order? / Do you know + statement order? / ... if/whether + statement order.
When / why we use it: Direct: Where is the meeting room? Indirect: Could you tell me where the meeting room is?
Examples:
Could you tell me where the meeting room is? → Kas te saaksite öelda, kus koosolekuruum on?
Do you know where she works? → Kas te teate, kus ta töötab?
Could you tell me if the report is ready? → Kas te saaksite öelda, kas aruanne on valmis?
Do you know whether they have approved it? → Kas te teate, kas nad on selle heaks kiitnud?
Special cases / exceptions: Kasulikud sissejuhatavad fraasid: Could you tell me...? Do you know...? Would you mind telling me...? I'd like to know...? I wonder... Sisseehitatud küsimus on juba iseenesest viisakas.
Common mistakes:
❌ Do you know where does she work? → ✅ Do you know where she works?
❌ Could you tell me where is the office? → ✅ Could you tell me where the office is?
Don't confuse with: Ära aja segi direct question'i sõnajärge ja embedded question'i sõnajärge.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Indirect question = polite.
Pärast intro → normal statement order.
Yes/No → if/whether.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Auxiliary verbs aitavad moodustada küsimusi, eitusi, rõhutamist ja erinevaid aegu. Peamised auxiliaries on be, have ja do. Ka modal verbs toimivad auxiliary'dena.
Main rule / explanation: BE moodustab Continuous'i ja Passive'i. HAVE moodustab Perfect'i. DO aitab Present/Past Simple'i küsimustes ja eitustes ning võib väljendada rõhutust.
Form / structure: be + V-ing / V3. have + V3. do/does/did + V1. Modals + V1.
When / why we use it: She is working. / She has finished. / Do you understand? / I do understand your point.
Examples:
She is working. → Ta töötab.
Has she finished? → Kas ta on lõpetanud?
She doesn't understand. → Ta ei saa aru.
I do understand your point. → Ma saan su mõttest tõesti aru.
He did send the email. → Ta tõepoolest saatis meili.
Special cases / exceptions: Ära lisa do-d, kui lauses on juba teine auxiliary: Is she working? / Have they finished? Samuti jääb põhiverb pärast do/does/did V1-vormi.
Common mistakes:
❌ Does she is working? → ✅ Is she working?
❌ Do they have finished? → ✅ Have they finished?
❌ Did you went? → ✅ Did you go?
Don't confuse with: Auxiliary kannab grammatilist infot; main verb jääb tavaliselt konstruktsioonile sobivasse põhivormi.
Quick summary / memory hook:
be → continuous/passive.
have → perfect.
do → questions/negatives/emphasis.
modal → ability/advice/obligation + V1.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: The + comparative, the + comparative näitab, et kaks muutust on omavahel seotud: mida rohkem/vähem esimene muutub, seda rohkem/vähem muutub teine.
Main rule / explanation: Mõlemad osad sisaldavad tavaliselt comparative-vormi: the faster..., the easier... / the more..., the less... Kasutada saab adjectives'e ja adverbs'e.
Form / structure: the + comparative, the + comparative
When / why we use it: Näita proportsionaalset seost kahe muutuse vahel.
Examples:
The more you practise, the more confident you become. → Mida rohkem harjutad, seda enesekindlamaks muutud.
The earlier we start, the sooner we can finish. → Mida varem alustame, seda varem saame lõpetada.
The more carefully you check the data, the fewer errors you make. → Mida hoolikamalt andmeid kontrollid, seda vähem vigu teed.
Special cases / exceptions: See ei ole tavaline ühe asja võrdlemine teisega. Standardmudeli mõlemad osad algavad the-ga.
Common mistakes:
❌ More you learn, more you notice. → ✅ The more you learn, the more you notice.
❌ The more you practise, more confident you become. → ✅ The more you practise, the more confident you become.
Don't confuse with: Tavaline comparative: This solution is cheaper. Seotud muutus: The cheaper the solution, the more popular it becomes.
Quick summary / memory hook:
the more..., the more...
the less..., the easier...
Mõlemad osad — comparative.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Present Perfect Simple ja Continuous seovad mineviku olevikuga, kuid Simple näitab sagedamini tulemust või kogust ning Continuous kestust ja tegevust.
Main rule / explanation: Simple = have/has + V3. Continuous = have/has been + V-ing. Stative verbs ei kasutata tavaliselt Continuous'is.
Form / structure: Present Perfect Simple: have/has + V3. Present Perfect Continuous: have/has been + V-ing.
When / why we use it: I have finished the report. = result. I have been working on the report all morning. = process/duration.
Examples:
I have finished the report. → Olen aruande lõpetanud.
She has visited London three times. → Ta on Londonis kolm korda käinud.
I have been working on the report all morning. → Olen terve hommiku aruande kallal töötanud.
She has been studying since nine. → Ta on alates üheksast õppinud.
Special cases / exceptions: Know, believe, understand, own, belong, need, want ja mõnda muud stative verb'i ei kasutata tavaliselt Continuous'is.
Common mistakes:
❌ I have been knowing her for years. → ✅ I have known her for years.
❌ She has been work since nine. → ✅ She has been working since nine.
Don't confuse with: Simple → result/achievement/number/experience. Continuous → activity/duration/recent process.
Quick summary / memory hook:
have/has + V3 = result.
have/has been + V-ing = activity/duration.
for = period; since = starting point.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Mõnda adjective'i saab kasutada ilma noun'ita, et tähistada tervet inimrühma: the rich, the poor, the elderly, the unemployed.
Main rule / explanation: Pärast the-d on adjective'il sellises konstruktsioonis plural meaning ja see tähistab inimesi rühmana. Ühe inimese kohta on vaja tavalist noun phrase'i.
Form / structure: the + adjective = group of people. a/an + adjective + person/man/woman jne = individual.
When / why we use it: Kasutame seda, kui räägime tervest inimrühmast adjective + the abil, mitte ühest konkreetsest inimesest.
Examples:
The rich are not always happy. → Rikkad ei ole alati õnnelikud.
The elderly often need accessible services. → Eakad vajavad sageli juurdepääsetavaid teenuseid.
a rich person → rikas inimene
a/an elderly woman → eakas naine
Special cases / exceptions: Kõiki adjectives'e ei saa automaatselt noun'iks muuta. Mõnda sellist vormi tuleb õppida valmis pattern'ina.
Common mistakes:
❌ The rich is not always happy. → ✅ The rich are not always happy.
❌ an unemployed (inimese kohta) → ✅ an unemployed man/person.
Don't confuse with: Võrdle: The rich = inimrühm. Rich people = tavaline phrase noun'iga.
Quick summary / memory hook:
the + adjective → group of people.
Plural meaning → use plural verb.
Ühe inimese jaoks on vaja noun'i.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Kui mitu adjectives kirjeldavad ühte noun'i, kasutatakse inglise keeles tavaliselt kindlat loomulikku järjekorda.
Main rule / explanation: Kasulik skeem: opinion → size → age → shape → colour → origin → material → purpose → noun. Kõiki kategooriaid pole korraga vaja.
Form / structure: opinion → size → age → shape → colour → origin → material → purpose → noun
When / why we use it: Kasutame loomulikku järjekorda, kui kõrvuti on kaks või rohkem adjectives'i.
Examples:
a beautiful small old round wooden table → ilus väike vana ümmargune puidust laud
a large modern office → suur moodne kontor
an old French wooden chair → vana prantsuse puidust tool
a black leather jacket → must nahktag
Special cases / exceptions: Loomulikus kõnes piisab sageli 2–3 adjectives'ist. Material ja purpose on tavaliselt noun'ile lähedal.
Common mistakes:
❌ two expensives cars → ✅ two expensive cars.
❌ Ära kanna adjective'ide järjekorda vene keelest otse üle.
Don't confuse with: Pole vaja tohutuid nimekirju pähe õppida; oluline on liikumine üldisest hinnangust konkreetsemate omaduste ning noun'i lähedal oleva material/purpose'i poole.
Quick summary / memory hook:
opinion → size → age → shape → colour → origin → material → purpose → noun.
Adjectives ei muutu mitmuses.

Lesson / Topic: So, such, so much, so many
Core idea: So ja such tugevdavad tähendust, kuid nõuavad erinevaid konstruktsioone. So much ja so many näitavad suurt kogust.
Main rule / explanation: So + adjective/adverb. Such + noun phrase. So much + uncountable. So many + plural countable.
Form / structure: so + adj/adv. such + a/an + adj + singular noun. such + plural/uncountable noun. so much + uncountable. so many + plural countable.
When / why we use it: It was so difficult. / It was such a difficult task. / We had so much time. / There were so many questions.
Examples:
The service was so slow. → Teenindus oli nii aeglane.
They are such helpful people. → Nad on nii abivalmid inimesed.
It was such an interesting idea. → See oli nii huvitav idee.
We had so much time. → Meil oli nii palju aega.
There were so many customers. → Kliente oli nii palju.
Special cases / exceptions: Singular countable noun'i puhul: such a/an + adjective + noun. Plural/uncountable puhul: such + noun ilma a/an'ita.
Common mistakes:
❌ so a difficult task → ✅ such a difficult task.
❌ such an expensive → ✅ such an expensive car.
❌ so many money → ✅ so much money.
Don't confuse with: Pärast so vaata adjective'i/adverbi. Pärast such vaata noun phrase'i.
Quick summary / memory hook:
so + adjective/adverb.
such + noun phrase.
so much + uncountable.
so many + plural countable.

Core idea: Narrative tenses aitavad jutustada lugu: mis juhtus järjest, mis oli pooleli, mis toimus varem ja kui kaua miski kestis enne minevikuhetke.
Main rule / explanation: Past Simple — main sequence. Past Continuous — background/in progress. Past Perfect — earlier event. Past Perfect Continuous — duration/activity before a past point.
Form / structure: V2. was/were + V-ing. had + V3. had been + V-ing.
When / why we use it: Kombineeri aegu, et lugeja mõistaks sündmuste omavahelist seost.
Examples:
I arrived, opened the door and sat down. → Jõudsin kohale, avasin ukse ja istusin maha.
I was driving home when I saw the accident. → Sõitsin koju, kui nägin õnnetust.
When I arrived, the meeting had already started. → Kui kohale jõudsin, oli koosolek juba alanud.
She was tired because she had been working all night. → Ta oli väsinud, sest oli terve öö töötanud.
Special cases / exceptions: Past Perfect ei ole automaatselt vajalik iga varasema tegevuse puhul. Kasuta seda, kui relationship with another past point on oluline.
Common mistakes:
❌ Every earlier action must be Past Perfect. → Ei.
❌ She had been work all night. → ✅ She had been working all night.
Don't confuse with: Mõtle timeline'ile: main event, background, earlier event, duration before earlier point.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Past Simple = main sequence.
Past Continuous = background.
Past Perfect = earlier.
Past Perfect Continuous = duration before past point.

Lesson / Topic: Position of adverbs and adverb phrases
Core idea: Adverb'i asukoht sõltub selle tüübist. Frequency, manner, time ja place phrases paiknevad tavaliselt eri kohtades.
Main rule / explanation: Frequency adverbs on tavaliselt enne main verb'i, kuid pärast be-d. Manner on sageli pärast verb'i/object'i. Time/place phrases on sageli lõpus. Mõnda adverb'i saab rõhutamiseks algusesse tõsta.
Form / structure: frequency + main verb. be + frequency. verb/object + manner. sentence + time/place phrase.
When / why we use it: Kõigepealt määra adverb'i funktsioon, seejärel vali loomulik asukoht.
Examples:
She usually works from home. → Ta töötab tavaliselt kodust.
She is usually on time. → Ta on tavaliselt õigel ajal.
He spoke clearly. → Ta rääkis selgelt.
We met in the office yesterday. → Kohtusime eile kontoris.
Yesterday, we discussed the problem. → Eile arutasime probleemi.
Special cases / exceptions: Pole reeglit „adverb on alati pärast verb'i”. Asukoht sõltub tüübist ja struktuurist.
Common mistakes:
❌ She always is late. → ✅ She is always late.
❌ He spoke the problem carefully. → Tavaliselt: He explained the problem carefully.
Don't confuse with: Frequency → enne main verb'i, pärast be-d. Manner → sageli verb'i/object'i järel. Time/place → sageli lõpus.
Quick summary / memory hook:
always/usually/often → before main verb.
With be → after be.
Manner → often after verb/object.
Time/place → often at end.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Future Continuous näitab tegevust, mis on konkreetsel tulevikuhetkel pooleli. Future Perfect näitab, et tegevus on selleks hetkeks lõpetatud.
Main rule / explanation: Future Continuous = will be + V-ing. Future Perfect = will have + V3. Erinevus: activity in progress vs completed before a point.
Form / structure: will be + V-ing. will have + V3.
When / why we use it: At 10 tomorrow, I will be presenting. By Friday, we will have finished the project.
Examples:
At 10 tomorrow, I will be presenting the results. → Homme kell kümme esitlen tulemusi.
Will you be using the meeting room this afternoon? → Kas sa kasutad täna pärastlõunal koosolekuruumi?
By Friday, we will have finished the project. → Reedeks oleme projekti lõpetanud.
By the end of the year, she will have worked here for five years. → Aasta lõpuks on ta siin töötanud juba viis aastat.
Special cases / exceptions: At = konkreetne hetk Future Continuous'i puhul. By = tähtaeg või hiliseim punkt Future Perfect'i puhul.
Common mistakes:
❌ By Friday, we will finish the report. (kui on vaja rõhutada, et töö on tähtajaks lõpetatud) → ✅ By Friday, we will have finished the report.
❌ will have finishing → ✅ will have finished.
Don't confuse with: At six, I will be working. = process at six. By six, I will have finished. = finished before six.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Future Continuous → will be doing at a time.
Future Perfect → will have done by a time.

Lesson / Topic: Review of all upper-intermediate verb tenses (CEFR B2.1)
Core idea: B1+ tasemel sõltub tense'i valik tähendusest, ajalisest seosest ja kõneleja vaatenurgast. Oluline pole „kõige raskem aeg”, vaid vajalik relationship between time and meaning.
Main rule / explanation: Present Simple — routine/fact/state. Present Continuous — temporary/developing. Past Simple — completed past. Past Continuous — past activity. Past Perfect — earlier past. Past Perfect Continuous — duration before past point. Present Perfect Simple/Continuous — connection/duration to now. Future forms carry different meanings.
Form / structure: Present Simple. Present Continuous. Past Simple. Past Continuous. Past Perfect. Past Perfect Continuous. Present Perfect Simple. Present Perfect Continuous. will/going to/Present Continuous/Future Continuous/Future Perfect.
When / why we use it: Kasuta kogu süsteemi valikuks, mitte üksikute valemite kogumina.
Examples:
I usually work from home. → Töötan tavaliselt kodust.
I'm working on a new process this week. → Sel nädalal töötan uue protsessi kallal.
I was checking the data when she called. → Kontrollisin andmeid, kui ta helistas.
I had finished before the meeting. → Olin enne koosolekut lõpetanud.
I've been working all morning. → Olen terve hommiku töötanud.
By Friday, I'll have finished. → Reedeks olen lõpetanud.
Special cases / exceptions: Üks time expression ei vali alati automaatselt tense'i. Vaata kõigepealt meaning'it ja perspective'i.
Common mistakes:
❌ Tense'i valimine ainult sõnade today/yesterday/next week järgi.
✅ Kõigepealt määra: routine, process, result, duration, earlier event, arrangement, deadline jne.
Don't confuse with: Põhiküsimus: „Millist ajalist seost ma tahan näidata?”
Quick summary / memory hook: Mitte „milline aeg on keerulisem?”, vaid „millist time and meaning relationship'i tahan näidata?”
