Lesson / Topic: Used to, be used to, get used to
Core idea: Used to, be used to ja get used to kirjeldavad kolme erinevat ideed: minevikuharjumus, praegune harjumuspärasus ja harjumise protsess.
Main rule / explanation: Used to + V1 = past habit/state no longer true. Be used to + noun/-ing = accustomed. Get used to + noun/-ing = become accustomed.
Form / structure: used to + V1. be used to + noun/V-ing. get used to + noun/V-ing.
When / why we use it: Kõigepealt määra, kas jutt on minevikust, praegusest harjumusest või harjumise protsessist.
Examples:
I used to work there. → Ma töötasin seal varem.
We used to live in the city. → Me elasime varem linnas.
I am used to working late. → Olen harjunud hilja töötama.
You will get used to working with the new system. → Sa harjud uue süsteemiga töötama.
Special cases / exceptions: Be/get used to puhul on to preposition, seega tuleb pärast seda verb -ing-vormis: I am used to getting up early.
Common mistakes:
❌ I am used to get up early. → ✅ I am used to getting up early.
❌ I used to working there. → ✅ I used to work there.
Don't confuse with: Used to drive = varem juhtisin. Be used to driving = olen praegu juhtimisega harjunud.
Quick summary / memory hook:
used to + V1 = past habit/state.
be used to + noun/-ing = familiar now.
get used to + noun/-ing = become familiar.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Would and used to – past habits and repeated actions
Core idea: Used to ja would võivad kirjeldada korduvaid minevikutegevusi, kuid used to kirjeldab ka varasemaid seisundeid.
Main rule / explanation: Would sobib hästi korduvate minevikutegevuste jutustamisel. Used to sobib nii repeated actions kui ka past states puhul.
Form / structure: used to + V1. would + V1 repeated past action'i puhul.
When / why we use it: Repeated action: When I was a child, I would visit my grandparents every weekend. Past state: I used to live in Kyiv.
Examples:
When I was a child, I used to visit my grandparents every weekend. → Kui olin laps, käisin igal nädalavahetusel vanavanemaid vaatamas.
When I was a child, I would visit my grandparents every weekend. → Kui olin laps, käisin igal nädalavahetusel neil külas.
I used to live in Kyiv. → Ma elasin varem Kiievis.
Special cases / exceptions: Would ei sobi tavaliselt past states'ide puhul: live, be, know jne. Ühe üksiku sündmuse puhul ei sobi ei used to ega would.
Common mistakes:
❌ I would live in Kyiv when I was a child. → ✅ I used to live in Kyiv.
❌ I would visit them last Sunday. → ✅ I visited them last Sunday.
Don't confuse with: Would ei tähenda siin lihtsalt „tulevikku” ega conditional'it. Siin tähistab see iseloomulikku korduvat minevikutegevust.
Quick summary / memory hook:
used to = repeated action + past state.
would = repeated past action.
Single event → Past Simple.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Gerund ja infinitive on erinevad verb pattern'id. Mõni verb nõuab -ing-vormi, mõni to + V1-vormi ja mõni lubab mõlemat tähenduse muutumisega.
Main rule / explanation: Gerund patterns: avoid/enjoy/suggest/finish + V-ing. Infinitive patterns: decide/hope/plan/want + to + V1. Mõnel verb'il on mõlemad mudelid.
Form / structure: verb + V-ing. verb + to + V1. Some verbs + both.
When / why we use it: Esimese verbi järel olev vorm on selle grammar pattern'i osa.
Examples:
I enjoy reading. → Mulle meeldib lugeda.
We decided to leave. → Otsustasime lahkuda.
She suggested taking a taxi. → Ta soovitas takso võtta.
I stopped smoking. → Lõpetasin suitsetamise.
I stopped to smoke. → Peatusin, et suitsetada.
Special cases / exceptions: Pärast preposition'it kasutame -ing-vormi: interested in learning, thank you for helping.
Common mistakes:
❌ I enjoy to work here. → ✅ I enjoy working here.
❌ She suggested to take a taxi. → ✅ She suggested taking a taxi.
❌ interested in to learn → ✅ interested in learning.
Don't confuse with: Ära vaata ainult verbi tõlget; vaata, millist vormi see verb nõuab ja kas vorm muudab tähendust.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Verb pattern = osa sõnaühikust.
preposition → V-ing.
enjoy/suggest/finish → V-ing.
decide/hope/plan/want → to + V1.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Past modal deduction aitab teha järelduse selle kohta, mis tõenäoliselt minevikus juhtus.
Main rule / explanation: Must have + V3 = tugev järeldus. May/might/could have + V3 = võimalik seletus. Can't have + V3 = tugev järeldus, et miski on võimatu või ei juhtunud.
Form / structure: must have + V3. may/might/could have + V3. can't have + V3.
When / why we use it: Kasutame evidence'i põhjal mineviku kohta järeldusi tehes, mitte permission'i või ability'i puhul.
Examples:
They must have forgotten the meeting. → Nad vist unustasid koosoleku.
She might have missed the bus. → Võimalik, et ta jäi bussist maha.
He could have misunderstood the message. → Võimalik, et ta sai sõnumist valesti aru.
They can't have finished already. → Ei saa olla, et nad on juba lõpetanud.
Special cases / exceptions: Must have tähendab siin deduction'it, mitte obligation'it. Pärast have tuleb V3.
Common mistakes:
❌ She might has left. → ✅ She might have left.
❌ He must go = past deduction. → Ei, see on obligation; past deduction: He must have gone.
Don't confuse with: Võrdle must go = peab minema ja must have gone = ta pidi tõenäoliselt minema.
Quick summary / memory hook:
must have + V3 = strong deduction.
might/could have + V3 = possibility.
can't have + V3 = strong impossibility.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Likely, unlikely, bound, definitely, probably – probability
Core idea: Tõenäosuse väljendamiseks on inglise keeles mitu võimalust: probably, definitely, likely, unlikely ja be bound to.
Main rule / explanation: Probably = tõenäoliselt. Definitely = kindlasti. Likely/unlikely = tõenäoline/ebatõenäoline. Be bound to = väga kindlalt oodatav.
Form / structure: will probably + V1. be probably + place/adjective. definitely + clause. be likely/unlikely to + V1. be bound to + V1.
When / why we use it: Paiguta adverb loomulikult ja vali konstruktsioon tähenduse järgi.
Examples:
She will probably arrive soon. → Ta saabub tõenäoliselt varsti.
He is probably at home. → Ta on tõenäoliselt kodus.
We will definitely need more time. → Meil läheb kindlasti rohkem aega vaja.
It is likely to rain. → Tõenäoliselt hakkab vihma sadama.
They are unlikely to agree. → Nad tõenäoliselt ei nõustu.
The new system is bound to create questions. → Uus system tekitab peaaegu kindlasti küsimusi.
Special cases / exceptions: Likely võib esineda kahes mudelis: It is likely that prices will rise. / Prices are likely to rise. Tõenäosuse tugevus sõltub kontekstist.
Common mistakes:
❌ She will probably comes. → ✅ She will probably come.
❌ They are likely agree. → ✅ They are likely to agree.
Don't confuse with: Probably/definitely on adverbs. Likely/unlikely/bound to on adjective-based structures.
Quick summary / memory hook:
probably = tõenäoliselt.
definitely = kindlasti.
likely = tõenäoline.
unlikely = ebatõenäoline.
bound to = väga tõenäoline/ootuspärane.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Would rather ja would prefer väljendavad mõlemad eelistust, kuid nende järel kasutatakse erinevaid struktuure.
Main rule / explanation: Would rather + V1. Teise inimese tegevuse puhul: I'd rather you + Past Simple. Would prefer + noun või to-infinitive.
Form / structure: would rather + V1. would rather + person + Past Simple. would prefer + noun / to + V1. rather than + base/infinitive pattern in comparison.
When / why we use it: Kasutame, kui võrdleme kahte võimalikku valikut ja ütleme, kumba eelistame.
Examples:
I'd rather stay. → Ma eelistaksin jääda.
I'd rather you came tomorrow. → Ma eelistaksin, et sa tuleksid homme.
I'd prefer tea. → Ma eelistaksin teed.
I'd prefer to stay home. → Ma eelistaksin koju jääda.
I'd prefer to work from home rather than travel. → Eelistaksin töötada kodust, mitte sõita.
Special cases / exceptions: Sama subject'i puhul ei kasutata would rather'i järel to-d. Past form pärast you-d ei tähenda siin tingimata minevikku.
Common mistakes:
❌ I'd rather to stay. → ✅ I'd rather stay.
❌ I'd prefer stay. → ✅ I'd prefer to stay.
Don't confuse with: rather + V1. prefer + noun/to-infinitive.
Quick summary / memory hook:
would rather + V1.
would prefer + noun/to + V1.
Different subject after rather → Past Simple.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Verbs of the senses: look, sound, feel, etc.
Core idea: Look, sound, smell, taste ja feel võivad kirjeldada muljet, mille miski meie meeltele jätab. Sellises tähenduses seisab nende järel sageli adjective.
Main rule / explanation: Sense verb'i järel kasutatakse sageli adjective'i: look tired, sound interesting, smell great, taste strange, feel soft. Like toob sisse võrdluse.
Form / structure: subject + sense verb + adjective. sense verb + like + noun.
When / why we use it: Kasutame objekti meelelist muljet kirjeldades või millegagi võrreldes.
Examples:
You look tired. → Sa näed väsinud välja.
That sounds interesting. → See kõlab huvitavalt.
The food smells great. → Toit lõhnab hästi.
This tastes strange. → See maitseb imelikult.
The fabric feels soft. → Kangas tundub katsudes pehme.
Special cases / exceptions: Ära aja segi look = seem/appearance ja look at = suunama pilgu. Soup tastes good, mitte tastes well, kui räägime maitsest.
Common mistakes:
❌ The soup tastes well. → ✅ The soup tastes good.
❌ She looks at tired. → ✅ She looks tired.
Don't confuse with: Sense verb + adjective kirjeldab subject'i. Sense verb + like toob võrdluse: It looks like rain.
Quick summary / memory hook:
look/sound/smell/taste/feel + adjective.
+ like + noun for comparison.
look at ≠ look.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Passive Voice'i saab moodustada peaaegu kõigis põhivormides. Põhimõte jääb samaks: be-vorm + V3.
Main rule / explanation: Be-vorm muutub, kuid main lexical verb jääb V3-vormi: is checked, was sent, is being tested, has been fixed, will be fixed, must be reported.
Form / structure: Present Simple: am/is/are + V3. Past Simple: was/were + V3. Present Continuous: am/is/are being + V3. Past Continuous: was/were being + V3. Present Perfect: has/have been + V3. Past Perfect: had been + V3. Future: will be + V3. Modal: modal + be + V3.
When / why we use it: Vali passive tense vastavalt tegevuse ajale, säilitades be + V3.
Examples:
The reports are checked every morning. → Aruandeid kontrollitakse igal hommikul.
The system is being tested. → Süsteemi testitakse praegu.
The problem has been fixed. → Probleem on parandatud.
The problem had been fixed before the meeting. → Probleem oli enne koosolekut parandatud.
The issue must be reported. → Probleemist tuleb teatada.
Special cases / exceptions: by + agent lisatakse siis, kui tegija on oluline: The software was developed by a small team. Kui tegija pole teada, on ilmne või ebaoluline, jäetakse ta ära.
Common mistakes:
❌ The system is test. → ✅ The system is being tested.
❌ The problem will fixed. → ✅ The problem will be fixed.
Don't confuse with: Kõigepealt määra tense, seejärel pane õige be-vorm ja V3.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Passive core = be + V3.
Tense on be-vormis.
Modal passive = modal + be + V3.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Zero and first conditional and future time clauses
Core idea: Zero Conditional kirjeldab üldtõdesid, reegleid, routines'e ja ennustatavaid tulemusi. First Conditional kirjeldab realistlikku tulevikuvõimalust.
Main rule / explanation: Zero: if/when + Present Simple, Present Simple. First: if + Present Simple, will + V1. Future time clauses with when/as soon as/before/after/until/once use Present rather than will.
Form / structure: Zero: If + Present, Present. First: If + Present, will + V1. Time clause: when/as soon as/etc. + Present.
When / why we use it: Kasutame üldtõdede, ennustatavate tulemuste ja realistlike tulevikutingimuste/-järjestuste jaoks.
Examples:
If you heat ice, it melts. → Kui kuumutad jääd, see sulab.
When the system detects an error, it sends an alert. → Kui süsteem tuvastab vea, saadab see teate.
If it rains, we will stay inside. → Kui sajab, jääme sisse.
As soon as she arrives, we'll start. → Kohe, kui ta saabub, alustame.
Special cases / exceptions: Future time clause'is ei kasutata will-i tavaliselt: When I finish, I will call you. Result clause võib sisaldada will'i, modaalverbi või käsku.
Common mistakes:
❌ When I will finish, I will call you. → ✅ When I finish, I will call you.
❌ If you heat ice, it will melt. → Üldtõe puhul on standardsem If you heat ice, it melts.
Don't confuse with: Zero = general/predictable result. First = realistic future possibility.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Zero: Present → Present.
First: Present → will.
Future time clause → Present, not will.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Second and third conditionals – unreal conditionals
Core idea: Second Conditional näitab ebareaalset/hüpoteetilist olevikku või tulevikku. Third Conditional kirjeldab ebareaalset minevikku ja selle kujuteldavat tulemust.
Main rule / explanation: Second: if + Past Simple, would + V1. Third: if + Past Perfect, would have + V3. Could/might võivad asendada would'i, kui vaja on ability/possibility tähendust.
Form / structure: Second: If + V2, would + V1. Third: If + had + V3, would have + V3.
When / why we use it: Kasutame hypothetical/unreal situations puhul: Second — now/future, Third — past.
Examples:
If I had more time, I would learn another language. → Kui mul oleks rohkem aega, õpiksin veel üht keelt.
If we had left earlier, we would have caught the train. → Kui oleksime varem lahkunud, oleksime rongile jõudnud.
If I had more time, I could help. → Kui mul oleks rohkem aega, saaksin aidata.
Special cases / exceptions: Ära pane would'i if-clause'i: If I had known..., mitte If I would have known.... Second Conditional'i Past vorm ei pea tähistama minevikku.
Common mistakes:
❌ If I would have known... → ✅ If I had known...
❌ If I had more time, I would have helped yesterday. → Third Conditional: If I had had more time, I would have helped.
Don't confuse with: Vaata aega: unreal now/future → Second; unreal past → Third.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Second → if + Past, would + V1.
Third → if + Past Perfect, would have + V3.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Wishes and regrets – I wish / if only
Core idea: I wish ja if only näitavad, et tahame olukorra olevikus või minevikus teistsuguseks. Vorm sõltub ajast ja sellest, mida tahame muuta.
Main rule / explanation: Present wish: wish + Past Simple. Past regret: wish + Past Perfect. Annoying situation/change in behaviour: wish + would.
Form / structure: wish + V2. wish + had + V3. wish + would + V1.
When / why we use it: Kasutame siis, kui tahame, et olevik oleks teistsugune, kahetseme minevikku või soovime kellegi käitumise/olukorra muutumist.
Examples:
I wish I knew the answer. → Kahju, et ma vastust ei tea.
If only I had more time. → Kui mul oleks ainult rohkem aega.
I wish I had studied harder. → Kahju, et ma rohkem ei õppinud.
I wish you would stop interrupting. → Ma sooviksin, et sa lõpetaksid vahelesegamise.
Special cases / exceptions: Wish + would käib tavaliselt teise inimese käitumise või olukorra kohta, mida kõneleja tahab muuta. Unreal present'i puhul ei panda lihtsalt Present Simple'it.
Common mistakes:
❌ I wish I know the answer. → ✅ I wish I knew the answer.
❌ I wish I had more time yesterday. → Past regret: I wish I had had more time.
Don't confuse with: Present unreal → Past Simple. Past regret → Past Perfect. Want behaviour/situation to change → would.
Quick summary / memory hook:
wish + Past = tahan, et olevik oleks teistsugune.
wish + had + V3 = kahetsus mineviku pärast.
wish + would = tahan muutust.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Participles -ing ja -ed võivad toimida adjectives'ina. Põhierinevus on tunde põhjus/efekt või inimese tunne/kogemus.
Main rule / explanation: -ing kirjeldab tavaliselt seda, mis tunnet tekitab või milline effect on millelgi. -ed kirjeldab tavaliselt seda, mida inimene tunneb või kogeb.
Form / structure: -ing adjective: boring, confusing, interesting. -ed adjective: bored, confused, interested.
When / why we use it: Kasutame participles'e adjective'idena, et kirjeldada tunde allikat/efekti või inimese kogemust.
Examples:
The film was boring. → Film oli igav.
I was bored. → Mul oli igav.
The instructions were confusing. → Juhised olid segadust tekitavad.
I was confused by the instructions. → Juhised ajasid mind segadusse.
The news was shocking. → Uudis oli šokeeriv.
We were shocked. → Me olime šokeeritud.
Special cases / exceptions: Ära vali -ed-vormi automaatselt ainult sellepärast, et subject on inimene. Küsi: feeling/experience või cause/source?
Common mistakes:
❌ The news was shocked. → ✅ The news was shocking.
❌ I was confusing. → ✅ I was confused.
Don't confuse with: -ing = source/cause/effect. -ed = experience/feeling.
Quick summary / memory hook:
-ing → tekitab tunnet.
-ed → tunneb/kogeb.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Passive with reporting verbs võimaldab infot edasi anda siis, kui allikas on üldine, teadmata või sõnumi seisukohast ebaoluline.
Main rule / explanation: Kaks põhiskeemi: It is said/believed/expected that... ja person/thing + is said/believed/expected + to-infinitive. Infinitive'i aeg näitab relationship'it.
Form / structure: It is + V3 reporting verb + that-clause. Subject + is/are + V3 reporting verb + to + V1 / to have + V3.
When / why we use it: It is believed that the company will expand. / The company is believed to be expanding. / He is believed to have left.
Examples:
It is believed that the company will expand. → Arvatakse, et ettevõte laieneb.
The company is believed to be expanding. → Arvatakse, et ettevõte laieneb.
The CEO is expected to announce the decision soon. → Eeldatakse, et tegevjuht teatab otsusest peagi.
He is believed to have left the country. → Arvatakse, et ta on riigist lahkunud.
Special cases / exceptions: Simple infinitive võib kirjeldada praegust olukorda; perfect infinitive to have + V3 näitab varasemat tegevust.
Common mistakes:
❌ He is believed to has stolen the money. → ✅ He is believed to have stolen the money.
❌ The company is said expanding. → ✅ The company is said to be expanding.
Don't confuse with: Vaata, kus on fookus: general source → It is said that...; person/thing → is said to...
Quick summary / memory hook:
It is said/believed/expected that...
Subject is said/believed/expected to + V1/be + V-ing/to have + V3.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Have something done tähendab, et korraldad teenuse, kuid töö teeb keegi teine.
Main rule / explanation: Pattern: have + object + V3. Tense muutub have-vormis. Konstruktsioon võib kirjeldada ka ebameeldivat sündmust, mis inimesega juhtus.
Form / structure: have + object + V3. I had my car repaired. I am having my hair cut. I will have my laptop repaired.
When / why we use it: Kasutame siis, kui me ei tee tööd ise, vaid korraldame, et keegi teine selle ära teeks.
Examples:
I had my car repaired. → Lasin oma auto parandada.
She is having her hair cut. → Tal lõigatakse praegu juukseid.
We had the office cleaned. → Lasime kontori koristada.
He had his phone stolen. → Tema telefon varastati.
Special cases / exceptions: Kontekst näitab, kas teenus telliti või juhtus inimesega ebameeldiv sündmus.
Common mistakes:
❌ I repaired my car. = someone else did it for me. → Ei: see tähendab, et parandasin ise.
✅ I had my car repaired. = remondi tegi keegi teine.
Don't confuse with: Võrdle active: I repaired my car. Causative: I had my car repaired.
Quick summary / memory hook:
have + object + V3 = korraldasin, et tegevus tehakse objektiga.
Tense changes in have.
Võib kirjeldada ka ebameeldivat sündmust.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Reporting verbs ei edasta ainult kõne fakti, vaid ka viisi või eesmärki: agree, promise, admit, deny, suggest, advise ja teised nõuavad erinevaid pattern'eid.
Main rule / explanation: Erinevad verbs vajavad erinevaid konstruktsioone: verb + to-infinitive, verb + -ing, verb + object + to-infinitive või that-clause.
Form / structure: Verb + to: agree/promise/refuse/offer + to V1. Verb + -ing: admit/deny/suggest/recommend + V-ing. Verb + object + to: advise/encourage/remind/warn + object + to V1. Some + that-clause.
When / why we use it: Õpi reporting verb koos selle pattern'iga, mitte üksinda.
Examples:
She agreed to help. → Ta nõustus aitama.
He admitted making a mistake. → Ta tunnistas, et tegi vea.
They suggested taking a taxi. → Nad soovitasid takso võtta.
She advised me to wait. → Ta soovitas mul oodata.
He explained that the plan had changed. → Ta selgitas, et plaan oli muutunud.
Special cases / exceptions: Suggest on eriti oluline: standard pattern on suggest + V-ing: She suggested taking a taxi.
Common mistakes:
❌ She suggested to take a taxi. → ✅ She suggested taking a taxi.
❌ He advised to wait. → ✅ He advised me to wait. (selles mudelis on vaja object'it)
Don't confuse with: Verbi tähendus ei ütle alati grammar pattern'it ette. Pattern tuleb verbiga koos õppida.
Quick summary / memory hook:
agree/promise/refuse/offer + to.
admit/deny/suggest/recommend + -ing.
advice/encourage/remind/warn + object + to.
explain/claim/admit + that-clause.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Clauses of contrast näitavad ootamatut erinevust. Purpose clauses selgitavad eesmärki: miks või milleks me midagi teeme.
Main rule / explanation: Although/even though/whereas/while toovad contrast'i. To + V1, in order to, so as to + V1 väljendavad purpose'it. So that + clause. Despite/in spite of tavaliselt + noun/V-ing.
Form / structure: although/even though/whereas/while + clause. to/in order to/so as to + V1. so that + clause. despite/in spite of + noun/V-ing.
When / why we use it: Vali konstruktsioon idee tüübi järgi: contrast, purpose või negative purpose.
Examples:
Although it was expensive, we bought it. → Kuigi see oli kallis, ostsime selle.
Whereas the first option is cheap, the second is faster. → Kui esimene variant on odav, on teine kiirem.
I called to confirm the booking. → Helistasin, et broneeringut kinnitada.
We checked the address so as not to make a mistake. → Kontrollisime aadressi, et mitte viga teha.
I wrote it down so that I wouldn't forget. → Panin selle kirja, et ma ei unustaks.
Special cases / exceptions: Although/even though nõuavad clause'i. Despite/in spite of võtavad tavaliselt noun'i või -ing-vormi: Despite being tired...
Common mistakes:
❌ Although it was late, but we continued. → But pole vajalik.
❌ Despite it was late... → ✅ Although it was late... / Despite being tired...
Don't confuse with: Kõigepealt otsusta: unexpected contrast? → although/whereas. goal? → to/in order to/so that. noun/-ing after despite.
Quick summary / memory hook:
contrast → although/even though/whereas/while.
purpose → to/in order to/so as to/so that.
despite/in spite of + noun/-ing.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Whatever, whenever, wherever, whoever ja however võivad avada clause'e, mille tähendus on avatud või piiramatu: ükskõik milline asi, inimene, koht või aeg.
Main rule / explanation: Whatever = anything that. Whoever = any person who. Wherever = any place where. Whenever = any time that. However + adjective/adverb = no matter how.
Form / structure: whatever/whoever/wherever/whenever + clause. however + adjective/adverb + clause.
When / why we use it: Kasutame, kui konkreetne variant pole oluline või tähendus on „ükskõik milline/kes/kus/millal/kui palju”.
Examples:
Take whatever you need. → Võta kõik, mida vajad.
Whoever finishes first can leave. → Kes esimesena lõpetab, võib lahkuda.
We can meet wherever you prefer. → Võime kohtuda ükskõik kus, kus sulle sobib.
Call me whenever you need help. → Helista mulle alati, kui abi vajad.
However difficult it is, we will continue. → Ükskõik kui raske see on, jätkame.
Special cases / exceptions: However tähendab siin „ükskõik kui / olenemata sellest, kui palju”. Ära aja seda segi however = „siiski/aga”.
Common mistakes:
❌ However alone in However difficult it is... = „however” kui „siiski”. → Siin tähendab however = no matter how.
❌ Wherever + noun only. → Järgnev osa peab moodustama clause'i või asukohaidee.
Don't confuse with: However difficult = no matter how difficult. However üksinda linking adverb'ina = but/nevertheless.
Quick summary / memory hook:
whatever = anything that.
whoever = any person who.
wherever = any place where.
whenever = any time.
however + adj/adv = no matter how.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Quantifiers – all, most, both, either, neither, any, no, none
Core idea: Need quantifiers aitavad rääkida tervikkogusest, enamusest, kahest variandist, ühest kahest, mitte kummastki ja määramata valikust.
Main rule / explanation: All = whole group. Most = majority. Both = two together. Either = one of two. Neither = not one/not the other. Any sõltub kontekstist. No + noun. None stands alone.
Form / structure: all + noun. most + noun / most of + determiner. both + plural / both of. either/neither + singular or of + plural pronoun. no + noun. none without noun.
When / why we use it: Kasutame, et võrrelda terve rühma kogust, enamust ja valikuvõimalusi.
Examples:
All the employees attended. → Kõik töötajad tulid kohale.
Most people agreed. → Enamik inimesi nõustus.
Both options are possible. → Mõlemad variandid on võimalikud.
Either option is acceptable. → Kumbki kahest variandist sobib.
Neither option works. → Kumbki kahest variandist ei tööta.
You can choose any option. → Sa võid valida ükskõik millise variandi.
No employees were available. → Ükski töötaja polnud saadaval.
None of the employees were available. → Ükski töötajaist polnud saadaval.
Special cases / exceptions: None ei seisa vahetult noun'i ees: none of the students, kuid no students. Most of + specific group kasutab determiner'it.
Common mistakes:
❌ none students → ✅ no students / none of the students.
❌ Both of three options → ✅ Both of the two options / all three options.
Don't confuse with: Kõigepealt loenda rühm ja määra, kas vajad konkreetset rühma.
Quick summary / memory hook:
all = whole.
most = majority.
both = 2 together.
either = 1 of 2.
neither = 0 of 2.
no + noun.
none = pronoun.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Standard English kasutab lauses tavaliselt üht negatiivset elementi. Anything/anyone/anywhere ja ever aitavad eitust moodustada ilma teise negative'ita.
Main rule / explanation: Pärast not kasutatakse sageli anything, anyone, anywhere, ever. Sõnadel nobody/nothing/nowhere on juba negatiivne tähendus ja need ei vaja tavaliselt not-i.
Form / structure: not + any/ever forms. või positive clause + no/nobody/nothing/nowhere.
When / why we use it: Kasutame, et moodustada eitavaid lauseid standardse skeemi järgi ilma kahe negatiivse elemendita.
Examples:
I don't know anything. → Ma ei tea midagi.
She didn't see anyone. → Ta ei näinud kedagi.
We haven't been anywhere. → Me pole kusagil käinud.
I know nothing. → Ma ei tea midagi.
Nobody called. → Keegi ei helistanud.
Special cases / exceptions: Mõnes non-standard variety's esineb double negative, kuid standard formal English'is seda tavaliselt välditakse.
Common mistakes:
❌ I don't know nothing. → ✅ I don't know anything. / I know nothing.
❌ Nobody didn't call. → ✅ Nobody called.
❌ I don't hardly know him. → ✅ I hardly know him.
Don't confuse with: Kui sõna on juba negative (nothing, nobody, nowhere, rarely/hardly), ära lisa ilma erilise põhjuseta veel not-i.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Standard English → one negative element.
not + anything/anyone/anywhere.
nothing/nobody/nowhere already negative.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Already, still, yet – What's the difference?
Core idea: Already, still ja yet näitavad erinevat suhet oodatud ajaga: mis on juba juhtunud, mis jätkub või mis pole veel juhtunud.
Main rule / explanation: Already = sooner than expected/before now. Still = situation continues. Yet = expected event has not happened, usually in questions/negatives.
Form / structure: have + already + V3. still + main verb / after be. yet often at end.
When / why we use it: Kasutame, et näidata: tegevus on juba toimunud, olukord jätkub või oodatud sündmus pole veel toimunud.
Examples:
I've already finished. → Olen juba lõpetanud.
Is she already here? → Kas ta on juba siin?
I still work there. → Ma töötan seal endiselt.
She is still working. → Ta töötab ikka veel.
Have you finished yet? → Kas sa oled juba lõpetanud?
I haven't finished yet. → Ma pole veel lõpetanud.
Special cases / exceptions: Position is part of the pattern: already on sageli auxiliary ja main verb'i vahel; still enne main verb'i, kuid pärast be-d; yet sageli lõpus.
Common mistakes:
❌ I yet haven't finished. → Neutraalne standard: I haven't finished yet.
❌ I yet live here. → ✅ I still live here.
Don't confuse with: Still = continues. Yet = expected change has not happened. Already = happened sooner/before now.
Quick summary / memory hook:
already = juba.
still = endiselt/ikka veel.
yet = veel / juba? küsimustes ja eitustes.
Position matters.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Needn't, don't need to, didn't need to, needn't have
Core idea: Needn't, don't need to, didn't need to ja needn't have on sarnased, kuid kirjeldavad erinevaid olukordi seoses vajaduse puudumisega.
Main rule / explanation: Don't need to / needn't = no necessity now. Didn't need to = no necessity in the past; see ei ütle iseenesest, kas tegevus toimus. Needn't have + V3 = tegevus toimus, kuid polnud vajalik.
Form / structure: don't need to + V1. needn't + V1. didn't need to + V1. needn't have + V3.
When / why we use it: Kasutame, et täpselt eristada praegust ja minevikulist vajaduse puudumist ning juba tehtud tarbetut tegevust.
Examples:
You don't need to come early. → Sa ei pea vara tulema.
You needn't wait. → Sa ei pea ootama.
We didn't need to book a room. → Meil polnud vaja tuba broneerida.
You needn't have bought so much food. → Sa ei oleks pidanud nii palju toitu ostma (aga ostsid).
Special cases / exceptions: Peamine erinevus: didn't need to ei ütle, kas inimene tegevuse ära tegi; needn't have näitab selgelt, et tegevus toimus ja oli tarbetu.
Common mistakes:
❌ We didn't need to buy food = kindlasti ostsime. → Ei, see pole öeldud.
❌ You needn't have bought food = ei ostnud. → Ei, ostsid, aga asjatult.
Don't confuse with: Vaata outcome'i: kas tegevus toimus? Kui jah ja see oli tarbetu → needn't have + V3.
Quick summary / memory hook:
don't need to / needn't = no necessity now.
didn't need to = no past necessity; outcome unspecified.
needn't have + V3 = done, but unnecessary.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Pretty, Rather, Quite, Fairly – Adverbs of degree
Core idea: Pretty, rather, quite ja fairly on degree adverbs. Need tugevdavad adjective'i/adverbi, kuid nende tugevus ja varjund sõltuvad kontekstist.
Main rule / explanation: Fairly tähendab sageli moderately. Pretty on kõnekeelne „üsna”. Rather võib tähendada quite ja anda mõnikord oodatust tugevama või ebameeldiva varjundi. Quite sõltub adjective'ist ja context'ist.
Form / structure: fairly + adj. pretty + adj. rather + adj. quite + adj/adv.
When / why we use it: Vali sõna konteksti, tone'i ja adjective'i järgi, mitte täpse matemaatilise skaala järgi.
Examples:
The task was fairly easy. → Ülesanne oli üsna lihtne.
The task was pretty difficult. → Ülesanne oli päris keeruline.
It's rather expensive. → See on üsna/küllaltki kallis.
The room is quite large. → Tuba on üsna suur.
quite impossible / quite certain → täiesti võimatu / täiesti kindel.
Special cases / exceptions: Quite võib eri adjectives'idega anda erineva tugevuse. Need sõnad on paindlikud ning intonation/context mõjutavad varjundit.
Common mistakes: ❌ Arvata, et fairly = täpselt 50%, pretty = täpselt 70% jne. → Ei, täpset matemaatilist skaalat pole.
Don't confuse with: Need on degree adverbs, kuid nende exact strength sõltub context'ist ja adjective'ist.
Quick summary / memory hook:
fairly = mõõdukalt.
pretty = informal quite.
rather = quite, mõnikord ootamatu/ebameeldiv.
quite = flexible, context-dependent.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: When I do vs When I have done – Future time clauses
Core idea: Future time clause'ites kasutatakse pärast when, once, as soon as, after, before ja until tavaliselt Presenti, kuid mõnikord on vaja Present Perfect'i, et rõhutada esimese tegevuse täielikku lõpetamist.
Main rule / explanation: Present Simple näitab tavaliselt tuleviku sündmuste neutraalset järjestust. Present Perfect rõhutab, et esimene tegevus on enne teist täielikult lõpetatud.
Form / structure: When I finish the report, I'll send it. / When I have finished the report, I'll send it.
When / why we use it: Kasuta Present Simple'it neutraalse järjestuse puhul. Kasuta Present Perfect'i, kui completion on oluline. Main clause võib sisaldada will'i.
Examples:
When I finish the report, I'll send it. → Kui ma aruande lõpetan, saadan selle.
When I have finished the report, I'll send it. → Kui ma olen aruande valmis saanud, saadan selle.
As soon as we have received the data, we will start the analysis. → Niipea, kui oleme andmed kätte saanud, alustame analüüsi.
Special cases / exceptions: Ära kasuta will-i standardse future time clause'i sees: When I will finish... on vale. Present saab tulevikutähenduse connector'i tõttu.
Common mistakes:
❌ When I will finish, I'll send it. → ✅ When I finish, I'll send it.
❌ When I have finish... → ✅ When I have finished...
Don't confuse with: finish = neutraalne sequence. have finished = rõhutatud completion before next event.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Future time clause → Present, not will.
Present Simple = sequence.
Present Perfect = completion emphasized.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Do or Make – Which is it?
Core idea: Do ja make võivad mõlemad tähendada „tegema”, kuid inglise keel valib nende vahel kindlate püsivate sõnaühenduste järgi.
Main rule / explanation: Do kasutatakse sageli activities, tasks, work and actions puhul. Make kasutatakse creating, producing, preparing või tulemuse põhjustamise puhul. Paljud combinations tuleb õppida collocation'idena.
Form / structure: do + collocation. make + collocation.
When / why we use it: Õpi sagedasi kombinatsioone, mitte ära tõlgi vene verbi „tegema” otse.
Examples:
do homework. → teha kodutööd.
do research. → teha uuringut.
do exercise. → teha harjutusi.
do your best. → anda endast parim.
make a decision. → teha otsus.
make a mistake. → teha viga.
make a plan. → teha plaan.
make money. → teenida raha.
make an appointment. → leppida kokku kohtumine.
make progress. → teha edusamme.
do someone a favour. → teha kellelegi teene.
do damage. → tekitada kahju.
Special cases / exceptions: On erandeid, seega safest approach on õppida sagedasi kombinatsioone collocation'idena.
Common mistakes:
❌ do a decision → ✅ make a decision.
❌ make homework → ✅ do homework.
❌ make a research → ✅ do research.
Don't confuse with: Ära tõlgi „tegema” sõna-sõnalt. Mõtle kõigepealt collocation'ile.
Quick summary / memory hook:
do = activities/tasks/work/actions.
make = create/produce/prepare/result.
Peamine — collocations.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Have võib olla tavaline põhiverb või auxiliary. Roll sõltub kogu konstruktsioonist.
Main rule / explanation: Main verb'ina võib have tähendada omamist, kogemust või tegevust: I have a car. Auxiliary'na moodustab have Perfect'i: I have finished.
Form / structure: Main verb: have + noun. Questions/negatives: do/does/did + have. Auxiliary: have/has/had + V3.
When / why we use it: Do you have a minute? / I don't have enough information. / I have finished the report. / She had already left.
Examples:
I have a car. → Mul on auto.
She has breakfast at seven. → Ta sööb hommikusööki kell seitse.
Do you have a minute? → Kas teil on hetk aega?
I don't have enough information. → Mul pole piisavalt infot.
I have solved the problem. → Olen probleemi lahendanud.
They will have completed the work by Friday. → Reedeks on nad töö lõpetanud.
Special cases / exceptions: Kui have on juba Perfect'i auxiliary, do-d ei kasutata: Have you finished? Have kuulub perfect construction'i ja sellele järgneb V3.
Common mistakes:
❌ Do you have finished? → ✅ Have you finished?
❌ Did she has a meeting? → ✅ Did she have a meeting?
❌ I have solved the problem = main verb. → Siin on have auxiliary, solved = V3.
Don't confuse with: Vaata sõna pärast have'i: noun → sageli main verb; V3 → Perfect auxiliary.
Quick summary / memory hook:
have + noun = main verb.
have/has/had + V3 = Perfect auxiliary.
Do with have ainult siis, kui have on main verb.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Clauses of contrast, purpose, reason and result
Core idea: Linking structures näitavad, kuidas üks idee teisega seotud on: contrast, purpose, reason või result.
Main rule / explanation: Contrast: although/even though/whereas/while. Purpose: to/in order to/so that. Reason: because/since/as. Result: so/therefore/as a result/such...that/so...that.
Form / structure: although + clause. to + V1. because + clause. so/therefore + result. such...that / so...that.
When / why we use it: Vali linking structure loogilise seose järgi, mitte tõlke järgi.
Examples:
Although the task was difficult, we completed it. → Kuigi ülesanne oli raske, lõpetasime selle.
We changed the process to reduce errors. → Muutsime protsessi, et vigu vähendada.
We stayed inside because it was raining. → Jäime sisse, sest sadas vihma.
The system was overloaded, so the service became slow. → Süsteem oli üle koormatud, seetõttu muutus teenus aeglaseks.
It was so busy that we had to wait. → Nii kiire oli, et pidime ootama.
Special cases / exceptions: Pärast although/even though tuleb clause. Pärast despite/in spite of tuleb noun või V-ing. Purpose ja result vastavad erinevatele küsimustele.
Common mistakes:
❌ Although it was expensive, but we bought it. → ✅ Although it was expensive, we bought it.
❌ Despite it was expensive... → ✅ Despite the high price... / Despite being expensive...
Don't confuse with: Purpose = miks/ milleks? Reason = miks? Result = mis juhtus selle tagajärjel? Contrast = mis on ootamatult erinev?
Quick summary / memory hook:
although/even though = contrast.
to/in order to/so that = purpose.
because/since/as = reason.
so/therefore/as a result = result.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Kui inimese sugu pole teada, pole oluline või seda ei täpsustata, kasutatakse tänapäevases standardses inglise keeles sageli singular they.
Main rule / explanation: They/them/their võivad viidata ühele inimesele: someone, every applicant, a customer. See aitab vältida his or her kordamist.
Form / structure: someone/every + noun + they/them/their. Singular they hoiab kogu tekstis grammatika ühtlasena.
When / why we use it: Kasutame, kui räägime inimesest, kelle gender ei ole teada, oluline või määratletud.
Examples:
If a customer has a question, they can contact support. → Kui kliendil on küsimus, saab ta võtta ühendust toega.
Someone left their phone here. → Keegi jättis siia oma telefoni.
Every applicant should check their email. → Iga kandidaat peaks oma meili üle kontrollima.
Special cases / exceptions: Pronoun peab lauses ja tekstis jääma consistent.
Common mistakes:
❌ Every applicant should check his or her email, then they should reply. → Parem järjepidevalt: Every applicant should check their email, then they should reply.
❌ Someone left her phone here. (kui gender on teadmata) → ✅ Someone left their phone here.
Don't confuse with: Singular they ei tähenda, et jutt peab käima mitmest inimesest.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Singular they = one person with unknown/irrelevant gender.
they/them/their säilitavad plural pronoun'i grammar'i, kuid võivad viidata ühele inimesele.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Reflexive pronouns viitavad tagasi subject'ile: I hurt myself. Reciprocal pronouns näitavad vastastikust tegevust: They helped each other.
Main rule / explanation: Reflexive: myself, yourself, himself, herself, itself, ourselves, yourselves, themselves. Reciprocal: each other / one another.
Form / structure: subject + verb + reflexive. subject + verb + each other/one another.
When / why we use it: Reflexive — subject ja object on sama inimene. Reciprocal — kaks või enam inimest tegutsevad üksteise suhtes.
Examples:
I hurt myself. → Ma vigastasin ennast.
She introduced herself. → Ta tutvustas ennast.
I did it myself. → Ma tegin selle ise.
They helped each other. → Nad aitasid üksteist.
The two teams respect one another. → Kaks meeskonda austavad üksteist.
Special cases / exceptions: Reflexive võib anda ka emphasis'e. Ära kasuta reflexive'i ainult sellepärast, et see tundub formaalsem.
Common mistakes:
❌ Please contact myself. → ✅ Please contact me.
❌ They looked at themselves. (kui mõte on „teineteisele otsa”) → ✅ They looked at each other.
Don't confuse with: themselves = igaüks vaatab iseendale; each other = nad vaatavad teineteisele.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Reflexive = back to subject.
Reciprocal = one another.
Emphasis: I did it myself.

Core idea: There ja it võivad mõlemad olla subject position'is, kuid annavad eri infot. There teavitab olemasolust/ilmumisest, it viitab olukorrale, ilmale, ajale, kaugusele või toimib preparatory subject'ina.
Main rule / explanation: There introduces existence/occurrence. It refers to a situation, weather, time, distance or can be preparatory subject: It's important to check the data.
Form / structure: There is/are + noun. It + be/adjective/time/weather/etc. It + adjective + to-infinitive.
When / why we use it: Kasutame, et eristada olemasolu/occurrence'i, olukorra hindamist, ilma, aega, kaugust või tegevust.
Examples:
There is a problem with the system. → Süsteemiga on probleem.
There are several reasons for the delay. → Viivituseks on mitu põhjust.
It's difficult to explain. → Seda on raske selgitada.
It's raining. → Sajab vihma.
It's five o'clock. → Kell on viis.
It's important to check the data. → Andmeid on oluline kontrollida.
Special cases / exceptions: Ära aja segi There is a problem = probleem on olemas ja It is a problem = see on probleem. Preparatory it võimaldab panna real subject'i hiljem.
Common mistakes:
❌ It is a problem. (kui tahame lihtsalt öelda, et probleem on olemas) → ✅ There is a problem.
❌ There is difficult to explain. → ✅ It's difficult to explain.
Don't confuse with: On midagi olemas? → there. Hindame olukorda/tegevust/ilma/aega/kaugust? → it.
Quick summary / memory hook:
there = existence/occurrence.
it = situation/weather/time/distance/preparatory subject.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Advanced narrative tenses organiseerivad loo: põhisündmused, taust, varasemad sündmused, minevikuhetkele eelnev kestus, vanad harjumused ja korduvad tegevused.
Main rule / explanation: Past Simple = main events. Past Continuous = background. Past Perfect = earlier event. Past Perfect Continuous = duration/activity before past point. Used to = old habits/states. Would = repeated past actions.
Form / structure: V2. was/were + V-ing. had + V3. had been + V-ing. used to + V1. would + V1 repeated action'i puhul.
When / why we use it: Kombineeri vorme, et timeline ja korduva tegevuse iseloom oleks lugejale selge.
Examples:
I opened the email and called the client. → Avasin meili ja helistasin kliendile.
I was driving when the message arrived. → Sõitsin, kui sõnum saabus.
They had already left when I arrived. → Nad olid juba lahkunud, kui ma saabusin.
She had been waiting for an hour when the bus came. → Ta oli bussi saabudes tund aega oodanud.
I used to live there. → Ma elasin seal varem.
Every summer, we would visit the coast. → Igal suvel käisime rannikul.
Special cases / exceptions: Would ei kirjelda tavaliselt past states'e: I used to be shy, mitte I would be shy. Past Perfect pole automaatselt vajalik iga varasema tegevuse puhul.
Common mistakes:
❌ I would be shy as a child. → ✅ I used to be shy as a child.
❌ She had left before he arrived — sellest piisab; kõiki minevikutegevusi pole vaja Past Perfecti panna.
Don't confuse with: Kõigepealt loo timeline, siis vali tense. Harjumuste puhul: used to/would.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Past Simple = main story.
Past Continuous = background.
Past Perfect = earlier.
Past Perfect Continuous = duration.
used to = past habit/state.
would = repeated past action.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Get on äärmiselt sage verb, millel on palju tähendusi. Seda ei saa tõlkida ainult ühe eesti sõnaga.
Main rule / explanation: Get + adjective = become. Get + noun = obtain/receive. Get + place = arrive. Get + object + adjective = cause something to become. Get + object + V3 = arrange/cause. Get + -ing = start. Lisaks on palju phrasal verbs.
Form / structure: get + adjective/noun/place. get + object + adjective/V3. get + -ing. get + particle.
When / why we use it: Get'i tähenduse määravad kogu konstruktsioon ja kontekst.
Examples:
I get tired after work. → Ma väsin pärast tööd.
I got a message. → Sain sõnumi.
What time did you get home? → Mis kell sa koju jõudsid?
Let's get moving. → Hakkame liikuma.
Get the report checked. → Korralda aruande kontroll.
Get the room ready. → Pane ruum valmis.
Special cases / exceptions: Context on hädavajalik. Get in get up/get through/get along ja teistel phrasal verb'idel on oma tähendus.
Common mistakes:
❌ Õppida get = ainult „saama”. → Õpi whole phrase.
❌ get to home → ✅ get home.
Don't confuse with: Vaata, mis tuleb get'i järel ja kas seal on particle. See määrab sageli meaning'i.
Quick summary / memory hook:
get + adjective = become.
get + noun = receive/obtain.
get + place = arrive.
get + object + adj/V3 = cause/arrange.
get + -ing = start.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Discourse markers näitavad ideede loogilist seost ja muudavad kõne või teksti selgemaks.
Main rule / explanation: Adding: also, moreover, in addition, besides. Contrast: however, nevertheless, on the other hand. Result: therefore, consequently, as a result. Example: for example, for instance. Sequence: first, then, meanwhile, finally. Conclusion: overall, in conclusion.
Form / structure: Marker + clause/sentence, position depends on marker and style. Kirjas on punctuation oluline.
When / why we use it: Vali marker loogika järgi: addition, contrast, result, example, sequence või conclusion.
Examples:
The plan is expensive. However, it may be effective. → Plaan on kallis. Kuid see võib olla tõhus.
Therefore, we changed the schedule. → Seetõttu muutsime ajakava.
For example, the first option is faster. → Näiteks on esimene variant kiirem.
Overall, the results are positive. → Kokkuvõttes on tulemused positiivsed.
Special cases / exceptions: Mõned markers'id on formaalsemad kui teised. However on tavaline nii kõnes kui kirjas; moreover võib kõlada formaalsemalt. Need ei ole alati otsesed sünonüümid.
Common mistakes:
❌ Kasutada therefore'i kui however'i lihtsat sünonüümi. → Need näitavad erinevaid loogilisi seoseid.
❌ The plan is expensive however it may work. → Kirjas: The plan is expensive. However, it may work.
Don't confuse with: Kõigepealt määra loogiline seos, siis vali marker.
Quick summary / memory hook:
adding → also/moreover.
contrast → however/nevertheless.
result → therefore/as a result.
example → for example.
sequence → first/finally.
conclusion → overall/in conclusion.

Lesson / Topic: Speculation and deduction – modal verbs and expressions
Core idea: Modal verbs ja expressions näitavad kindluse astet: tugev järeldus, võimalikkus, võimatus või tõenäosus.
Main rule / explanation: Must = strong logical conclusion. Might/may/could = possibility. Can't = strong impossibility. Past deduction: modal + have + V3. Samuti likely/unlikely/bound to/probably.
Form / structure: must/might/may/could/can't + V1/be. Past: modal + have + V3. likely/unlikely/bound to + V1.
When / why we use it: Kasutame, kui ei räägi kindlast faktist, vaid sellest, kui kindlad me oletuses oleme.
Examples:
They must be at home. → Nad on ilmselt kodus.
They might be at home. → Võib-olla on nad kodus.
That can't be the right address. → See ei saa olla õige aadress.
They must have forgotten. → Nad vist unustasid.
She might have missed the train. → Võib-olla jäi ta rongist maha.
Special cases / exceptions: Must võib tähendada obligation'it või deduction'it. Kontekst määrab: You must leave now. / You must have left already.
Common mistakes:
❌ She might has left. → ✅ She might have left.
❌ He must leave = deduction. → Ei, see on obligation; deduction: He must have left.
Don't confuse with: Kõigepealt küsi: rule/obligation või evidence-based conclusion?
Quick summary / memory hook:
must = strong deduction.
might/may/could = possibility.
can't = impossible.
Past deduction = modal + have + V3.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Inversion with negative adverbials – adding emphasis
Core idea: Formaalses ja emphatic English'is võib lause alguses olev negative/restrictive adverbial põhjustada inversion'i: auxiliary liigub subject'i ette.
Main rule / explanation: Pärast Never, Rarely, Seldom, Hardly, Not only, Under no circumstances, At no time ja sarnaseid väljendeid kasutatakse inversion'it. Kui auxiliary puudub, lisatakse do/does/did.
Form / structure: Never + auxiliary + subject + verb. Rarely do we... Not only did she...
When / why we use it: Kasutame tugeva emphasis'e ja formaalsema stiili jaoks.
Examples:
Never had I seen such a result. → Ma polnud kunagi sellist tulemust näinud.
Rarely do we see such results. → Harva näeme selliseid tulemusi.
Not only did she solve the problem, but she also explained it clearly. → Ta mitte ainult ei lahendanud probleemi, vaid selgitas seda ka selgelt.
Special cases / exceptions: See on formal/emphatic structure, mitte tavaline kõnekeelne sõnajärg.
Common mistakes:
❌ Never I have seen... → ✅ Never have I seen...
❌ Rarely we see... → ✅ Rarely do we see...
Don't confuse with: Lause alguses olev negative/restrictive expression → kontrolli, kas inversion on vajalik.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Never/Rarely/Seldom + auxiliary + subject.
No auxiliary? → use do/does/did.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Distancing – expressions and passive of reporting verbs
Core idea: Distancing võimaldab infot edasi anda nii, et kõneleja ei esita seda isiklikult kontrollitud faktina.
Main rule / explanation: Kasutatakse It is said/believed, It appears/seems, According to, Apparently ja passive reporting konstruktsioone. Need on levinud journalism'is, academic writing'us ja professional reports'ides.
Form / structure: It is said that... / It appears that... / The company is believed to... / According to... / Apparently,...
When / why we use it: Kasutame siis, kui infoallikas on olemas, kuid kõneleja tahab väitest distantseeruda.
Examples:
It is believed that the company will expand. → Arvatakse, et ettevõte laieneb.
The company is believed to be expanding. → Arvatakse, et ettevõte laieneb.
He is thought to have left. → Arvatakse, et ta lahkus.
Apparently, the figures are incorrect. → Ilmselt on näitajad valed.
Special cases / exceptions: Distancing ei tohiks tekitada valet kindlustunnet. Sõnastus peab peegeldama available evidence'i.
Common mistakes:
❌ Kasutada It is definitely believed... ilma aluseta. → Distancing'i mõte on näidata allikat või ebakindlust.
❌ He is thought has left. → ✅ He is thought to have left.
Don't confuse with: Distancing = „annan info/allika edasi, kuid ei väida seda otsese enda faktina”.
Quick summary / memory hook:
It is said/believed...
It appears/seems...
According to...
Apparently...
The company is believed to...
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Wish, rather, if only, it's time – Unreal uses of past tenses
Core idea: Wish, if only, would rather ja it's time kasutavad minevikuvorme, et näidata ebareaalsust, kahetsust või seda, et praegu on aeg olukorda muuta.
Main rule / explanation: Present unreal: wish/if only + Past Simple. Past regret: + Past Perfect. Would rather about another person + Past Simple. It's time + Past Simple can refer to now/near future.
Form / structure: wish + V2. wish + had + V3. would rather + person + Past Simple. it's time + Past Simple.
When / why we use it: Kasutame unreal present'i, minevikukahetsuse, teise inimese eelistamise või praeguse kiire vajaduse väljendamiseks.
Examples:
I wish I knew the answer. → Kahju, et ma vastust ei tea.
If only I had more time. → Kui mul oleks ainult rohkem aega.
I wish I had prepared better. → Kahju, et ma paremini ei valmistunud.
I'd rather you didn't tell them yet. → Ma eelistaksin, et sa neile veel ei räägiks.
It's time we left. → Meil on juba aeg lahkuda.
Special cases / exceptions: Past vorm ei tähenda siin tingimata minevikuaega. See näitab distance from reality't.
Common mistakes:
❌ I wish I know the answer. → ✅ I wish I knew the answer.
❌ It's time we leave. → ✅ It's time we left.
Don't confuse with: Ära tõlgi Past-vormi siin automaatselt minevikuna. Vaata funktsiooni: unreal, regret, preference, urgency.
Quick summary / memory hook:
wish + Past = unreal present.
wish + Past Perfect = past regret.
would rather + person + Past.
It's time + Past.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Mõned verbs võtavad object'i, millele järgneb infinitive või -ing. Vorm sõltub konkreetsest verb pattern'ist.
Main rule / explanation: want/expect/allow/encourage + object + to V1. catch/find/keep + object + V-ing. make/let + object + bare infinitive. Remember võib pattern'i järgi tähendust muuta.
Form / structure: verb + object + to V1. verb + object + V-ing. make/let + object + V1.
When / why we use it: Õpi kogu pattern: verb + object + järgmine verbivorm.
Examples:
The manager encouraged us to apply. → Juht julgustas meid kandideerima.
I found him working late. → Avastasin, et ta töötab hilja.
The manager made us wait. → Juht sundis meid ootama.
They let us leave early. → Nad lubasid meil varem lahkuda.
I remember meeting her. → Ma mäletan, et kohtasin teda.
I remembered to call her. → Ma ei unustanud talle helistada.
Special cases / exceptions: Remember + -ing = minevikusündmuse mäletamine. Remember + to V1 = vajaliku tulevase tegevuse meelespidamine. Bare infinitive esineb selles mustris make/let järel.
Common mistakes:
❌ She encouraged me apply. → ✅ She encouraged me to apply.
❌ They made us to wait. → ✅ They made us wait.
❌ I remember to meeting her. → ✅ I remember meeting her.
Don't confuse with: Kõigepealt määra first verb, object ja object'i järel kasutatav pattern.
Quick summary / memory hook:
want/expect/allow/encourage + object + to.
catch/find/keep + object + -ing.
make/let + object + V1.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Unless, even if, provided, as long as, etc. – Other expressions in conditionals
Core idea: Unless, even if, provided/providing ja as long as väljendavad erinevaid tingimuse tüüpe.
Main rule / explanation: Unless = if not. Even if = tulemus ei muutu hoolimata tingimusest. Provided/providing ja as long as = tingimus peab olema täidetud.
Form / structure: unless + Present. even if + Present. provided/providing/as long as + clause.
When / why we use it: Future meaning'uga tingimuslause dependent clause'is kasutatakse tavaliselt Presenti, mitte will-i.
Examples:
Unless you hurry, you'll miss the train. → Kui sa ei kiirusta, jääd rongist maha.
Even if it rains, we'll go. → Isegi kui sajab, läheme.
You can borrow it provided that you return it tomorrow. → Sa võid selle laenata tingimusel, et tagastad selle homme.
You can stay as long as you keep the room clean. → Sa võid jääda seni, kuni hoiad toa puhtana.
Special cases / exceptions: Ära kasuta will-i pärast unless/if future condition clause'is: Unless it rains, we'll go.
Common mistakes:
❌ Unless it will rain, we'll go. → ✅ Unless it rains, we'll go.
❌ Even if it will be difficult, we'll continue. → ✅ Even if it is difficult, we'll continue.
Don't confuse with: Unless = negatiivne tingimus. Even if = tingimus ei muuda tulemust. Provided/as long as = nõutud tingimus.
Quick summary / memory hook:
unless = if not.
even if = despite condition.
provided/as long as = only if condition is satisfied.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: All conditionals – mixed conditionals, alternatives to if, inversion
Core idea: Conditionals võivad kombineeruda ja if'ile on olemas alternatiivsed väljendid. Formaalses inglise keeles on võimalik ka inversion ilma if-ita.
Main rule / explanation: Mixed conditional seob erinevaid ajaperioode. Alternatives: unless, provided, as long as, on condition that, supposing, assuming. Formal inversion: Had I known..., Were I..., Should you...
Form / structure: Mixed: If + past perfect, would + present/base. Or If + past, would have + V3. Inversion: Had/Were/Should + subject...
When / why we use it: Vali konstruktsioon tingimuse ja tulemuse aja ning stiili järgi.
Examples:
If I had studied engineering, I would have a different job now. → Kui oleksin inseneriks õppinud, oleks mul praegu teistsugune töö.
If I weren't so busy, I would have joined you yesterday. → Kui ma poleks nii hõivatud, oleksin eile sinuga liitunud.
Had I known, I would have acted differently. → Kui ma oleksin teadnud, oleksin teisiti käitunud.
Were I in your position, I would wait. → Kui ma oleksin sinu olukorras, ootaksin.
Should you need assistance, contact support. → Kui vajate abi, võtke toega ühendust.
Special cases / exceptions: Inversion eemaldab if'i ja tõstab auxiliary subject'i ette. Hoia intended time relationship selge.
Common mistakes:
❌ Had I knew... → ✅ Had I known...
❌ Were I was in your position... → ✅ Were I in your position...
❌ Should you will need assistance... → ✅ Should you need assistance...
Don't confuse with: Kõigepealt määra condition'i ja result'i aeg. Siis vali mixed conditional või formal inversion.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Mixed = different time periods.
Formal inversion:
Had I known...
Were I...
Should you...
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Mixed conditionals ühendavad ebareaalse tingimuse ja tulemuse, mis kuuluvad eri ajaperioodidesse.
Main rule / explanation: Past condition → present result: If + Past Perfect, would + V1/state now. Present condition → past result: If + Past, would have + V3.
Form / structure: Past→present: If + had + V3, would + V1. Present→past: If + V2, would have + V3.
When / why we use it: Kõigepealt määra, millal on imaginary cause ja millal imaginary result.
Examples:
If I had taken that job, I would live abroad now. → Kui oleksin siis selle töö vastu võtnud, elaksin nüüd välismaal.
If I were more organised, I wouldn't have missed the deadline yesterday. → Kui oleksin organiseeritum, poleks ma eile tähtaega ületanud.
Special cases / exceptions: Ära vali pattern'it ainult meeldejäetud valemi järgi. Määra kaks time period'i.
Common mistakes:
❌ If I had taken the job, I would have lived abroad now. → Past cause + present result: tavaliselt I would live abroad now.
❌ If I were more organised, I wouldn't miss the deadline yesterday. → Past result: wouldn't have missed.
Don't confuse with: Cause ja result võivad kuuluda erinevatesse aegadesse.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Past cause → present result.
Present condition → past result.
Kõigepealt aeg, siis vorm.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Modal verbs – permission, obligation, prohibition, necessity
Core idea: Modal verbs võivad väljendada permission'i, obligation'it, prohibition'it ja necessity puudumist. Tähendus sõltub modal/semi-modal'i valikust.
Main rule / explanation: Must = strong obligation. Have to = often external rule. Mustn't = prohibition. Don't have to/needn't = no necessity. Can/may = permission. Be allowed to = permission across tenses.
Form / structure: must/have to/mustn't/don't have to/needn't + V1. can/may + V1. be allowed to + V1.
When / why we use it: Kasutame obligation'i, prohibition'i, no necessity või permission'i väljendamiseks, ka erinevates aegades.
Examples:
You must wear a badge. → Te peate kandma töötajakaarti.
We have to submit the form by Friday. → Peame vormi reedeks esitama.
You mustn't share this password. → Te ei tohi seda parooli jagada.
You don't have to attend. → Te ei pea osalema.
You may leave early. → Te võite varem lahkuda.
We weren't allowed to enter. → Meil ei lubatud siseneda.
Special cases / exceptions: Mustn't ja don't have to pole vastandid: üks on prohibition, teine optional action.
Common mistakes:
❌ You mustn't go = „sa ei pea minema”. → Ei: „sul on keelatud minna”.
❌ You don't have to go = „sul on keelatud”. → Ei: „sa ei pea minema”.
Don't confuse with: Kõigepealt määra: obligation, prohibition, no necessity või permission?
Quick summary / memory hook:
must = obligation.
have to = external requirement.
mustn't = prohibited.
don't have to/needn't = optional.
can/may = permission.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Sense verbs kirjeldavad meelte kaudu saadud muljet. Nende järel võib olla adjective, like + noun või object + bare infinitive/-ing.
Main rule / explanation: look/sound/smell/taste/feel + adjective. Verb + like + noun. See/hear/watch/notice/feel + object + V1 või V-ing näitab terviktegevust või käimasolevat tegevust.
Form / structure: subject + sense verb + adjective. sense verb + like + noun. see/hear/watch + object + V1/V-ing.
When / why we use it: Vali V1, kui tajud tegevust tervikuna; V-ing, kui märkad protsessi selle toimumise ajal.
Examples:
The plan sounds reasonable. → Plaan kõlab mõistlikult.
It looks like a mistake. → See näeb välja nagu viga.
I saw him cross the street. → Nägin teda üle tänava minemas.
I saw him crossing the street. → Nägin teda tänavat ületamas.
The soup tastes good. → Supp maitseb hästi.
Special cases / exceptions: Sense verb'i järel on subject'i kirjeldamisel vaja adjective'i, mitte adverb'i: tastes good, mitte tastes well. Object + V-ing rõhutab käimasolevat tegevust.
Common mistakes:
❌ The soup tastes well. → ✅ The soup tastes good.
❌ I saw him to cross the street. → ✅ I saw him cross the street.
Don't confuse with: Kõigepealt määra: kas kirjeldad subject'i, teed võrdlust või kirjeldad tajutud tegevust?
Quick summary / memory hook:
sense verb + adjective.
+ like + noun.
object + V1 = whole action.
object + V-ing = action in progress.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Gerundil ja infinitive'il on keerukad vormid, mis näitavad täpsemalt aega ja voice'i.
Main rule / explanation: Perfect gerund = having + V3. Perfect infinitive = to have + V3. Passive infinitive = to be + V3. Perfect passive infinitive = to have been + V3.
Form / structure: having + V3. to have + V3. to be + V3. to have been + V3.
When / why we use it: Kasutame keerukamat vormi, kui on oluline varasem tegevus või passive meaning.
Examples:
He admitted having made a mistake. → Ta tunnistas, et oli vea teinud.
She seems to have forgotten. → Tundub, et ta unustas.
The report needs to be checked. → Aruanne tuleb üle kontrollida.
The documents appear to have been lost. → Tundub, et dokumendid on kaduma läinud.
Special cases / exceptions: Vormi valik sõltub time relationship'ist ja voice'ist, mitte ainult main verb'ist.
Common mistakes:
❌ He admitted to have made a mistake. → ✅ He admitted having made a mistake.
❌ He is believed to has left. → ✅ He is believed to have left.
❌ The report needs checking vs needs to be checked: mõlemad pattern'id võivad esineda, kuid siin on source'is fookus passive infinitive'il.
Don't confuse with: earlier action → perfect form. Receiver of action → passive form.
Quick summary / memory hook:
having + V3 = earlier gerund action.
to have + V3 = earlier infinitive action.
to be + V3 = passive.
to have been + V3 = earlier passive.

Core idea: Inglise keeles on mitu tulevikuvormi ning igal neist on tüüpiline funktsioon.
Main rule / explanation: Will: predictions/decisions/promises. Going to: prior intentions/evidence. Present Continuous: arrangements. Present Simple: schedules. Future Continuous: activity in progress. Future Perfect: completed before a future point.
Form / structure: will + V1. be going to + V1. am/is/are + V-ing. Present Simple. will be + V-ing. will have + V3.
When / why we use it: Vali future form tähenduse järgi: decision, intention, arrangement, timetable, ongoing future activity või completion by a point.
Examples:
I'll call you later. → Helistan sulle hiljem.
We're going to launch a new version. → Kavatseme uue versiooni välja lasta.
I'm meeting the client tomorrow. → Kohtun homme kliendiga.
The train leaves at eight. → Rong väljub kell kaheksa.
I'll be working at nine. → Kell üheksa töötan.
I'll have finished by nine. → Kella üheksaks olen lõpetanud.
Special cases / exceptions: Pole üht universaalset future form'i. Kõigepealt määra meaning: decision, intention, arrangement, timetable, ongoing future activity või deadline.
Common mistakes:
❌ Every future sentence must use will. → Ei.
❌ The train will leave at eight. → See võib olla prediction, kuid timetable'i puhul on tavalisem: The train leaves at eight.
Don't confuse with: Future ≠ üks grammatika, vaid mitu erineva tähendusega vormi.
Quick summary / memory hook:
will → decision/prediction/promise.
going to → intention/evidence.
Present Continuous → arrangement.
Present Simple → timetable.
Future Continuous → in progress.
Future Perfect → completed by point.

Core idea: Tulevikku saab väljendada ka erikonstruktsioonidega ilma tavalise will'ita. Need erinevad timing'u, certainty ja style'i poolest.
Main rule / explanation: Be due to = scheduled/expected. Be about to = very near future. Be set to = expected/planned. Be on the verge of + V-ing = almost happening. Be likely/expected to = probability/expectation.
Form / structure: be due to + V1. be about to + V1. be set to + V1. be on the verge of + V-ing. be likely/expected to + V1.
When / why we use it: Vali expression future meaning'i tüübi järgi.
Examples:
The train is due to arrive at six. → Rong peaks saabuma kell kuus.
The meeting is about to start. → Koosolek algab kohe.
The company is set to release a new product. → Ettevõte peaks uue toote välja laskma.
The system is on the verge of crashing. → Süsteem on kokkujooksmise äärel.
Prices are likely to rise. → Tõenäoliselt hinnad tõusevad.
Special cases / exceptions: About to = very near future. Kõik future expressions'id pole omavahel vahetatavad.
Common mistakes: ❌ The train is about to arrive at six. (see võib kõlada nagu „kohe-kohe”, mitte timetable) → Timetable'i puhul on parem due to arrive.
Don't confuse with: Kõigepealt määra: schedule, immediate future, planned/expected event või probability.
Quick summary / memory hook:
due to = scheduled.
about to = very soon.
set to = expected/planned.
on the verge of = almost happening.
likely/expected to = probability/expectation.

Core idea: Future in the past kirjeldab midagi, mis oli tulevik võrreldes mingi varasema minevikuhetkega.
Main rule / explanation: Was/were going to = past intention. Would = future from past viewpoint. Was/were about to = immediate future from past viewpoint. Was/were due to = scheduled future from past viewpoint.
Form / structure: was/were going to + V1. would + V1. was/were about to + V1. was/were due to + V1.
When / why we use it: Peamine on past viewpoint: At 9 a.m. I knew that I would finish by noon.
Examples:
I was going to call you, but I forgot. → Kavatsesin sulle helistada, kuid unustasin.
He said he would help. → Ta ütles, et aitab.
We were about to leave when she arrived. → Olime just lahkumas, kui ta saabus.
The train was due to arrive at noon. → Rong pidi keskpäeval saabuma.
Special cases / exceptions: Would ei ole siin conditional; see tähendab tulevikku mineviku vaatenurgast. Ära vaheta seda automaatselt will'iks pärast past reporting verb'i.
Common mistakes: ❌ He said he will help. → ✅ He said he would help.
Don't confuse with: Võrdle vaatenurka now vs then: I will finish. / I knew I would finish.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Future from past viewpoint:
was going to.
would.
was about to.
was due to.

Lesson / Topic: Ellipsis and substitution – Omitting or replacing words
Core idea: Ellipsis tähendab kontekstist arusaadavate sõnade ärajätmist. Substitution asendab korduvat struktuuri teise sõna või väljendiga.
Main rule / explanation: Ellipsis jätab understood material'i välja. Substitution kasutab näiteks one, ones, do, so, neither, et kordust vältida.
Form / structure: want to / promise to / me to etc. võivad jätta arusaadavad sõnad ütlemata. so/neither/do/one/ones asendavad korduvat materjali.
When / why we use it: Kasutame, et kõne kõlaks loomulikumalt ja väldiks juba arusaadava kordamist.
Examples:
I can help if you want me to. → Ma saan aidata, kui sa tahad, et ma aitaksin.
She didn't call, although she promised to. → Ta ei helistanud, kuigi lubas.
I need a new laptop. So does Anna. → Mul on uut sülearvutit vaja. Annal samuti.
I don't like the first option, but I like the second one. → Mulle ei meeldi esimene variant, kuid teine meeldib.
Special cases / exceptions: Ellipsis töötab ainult siis, kui puuduv info on kontekstist taastatav. Ära jäta sõnu välja, kui tekib ambiguity.
Common mistakes:
❌ I chose the blue report because the blue report was clearer. → ✅ I chose the blue report because it was clearer.
❌ Jätta välja sõnad, mida ei saa kontekstist taastada. → ✅ Jäta välja ainult see, millest kuulaja kergesti aru saab.
Don't confuse with: Küsi: kas listener saab missing words ilma oletamata taastada?
Quick summary / memory hook:
Ellipsis = omit understood words.
Substitution = replace repeated material.
Context must make meaning clear.

Core idea: Inglise keel moodustab compound noun'e ja kasutab possessive 's-i omanduse, suhte ja mõne ajaühendi väljendamiseks.
Main rule / explanation: Compound noun: software developer, data analysis, customer service. Possessive 's: singular owner, plural possessive with apostrophe, irregular plural with 's.
Form / structure: noun + noun. singular noun + 's + noun. plural ending -s + apostrophe. irregular plural + 's.
When / why we use it: Määra, kas esimene noun kirjeldab teise tüüpi/otstarvet või näitab kuuluvust, suhet või aega.
Examples:
software developer → tarkvaraarendaja.
data analysis → andmeanalüüs.
the manager's office → juhi kabinet.
the employees' room → töötajate ruum.
the children's books → laste raamatud.
today's meeting → tänane koosolek.
two weeks' holiday → kahenädalane puhkus.
Special cases / exceptions: Plural noun, mis lõpeb -s-iga, saab ainult apostrophe'i: students'. Irregular plural saab 's: children's.
Common mistakes:
❌ the students's projects → ✅ the students' projects.
❌ the children books → ✅ the children's books.
Don't confuse with: Compound noun = type/purpose. Possessive = relationship/ownership/time expression.
Quick summary / memory hook:
noun+noun = compound noun.
's = singular/irregular possessive.
s' = regular plural possessive.

Core idea: Cleft sentences jagavad info osadeks, et üks element saaks erilise emphasis'e.
Main rule / explanation: It-cleft: It was + focus + who/that... Wh-cleft: What + clause + be + focus. Esile saab tõsta inimese, asja, aja, koha või põhjuse.
Form / structure: It was X who/that + clause. What + clause + is/was + focus.
When / why we use it: Kasutame, kui on oluline mingi element parandada, täpsustada või eriti esile tõsta.
Examples:
It was John who called me. → See oli John, kes mulle helistas.
It was the deadline that caused the problem. → Just deadline tekitas probleemi.
What I need is more time. → Mida ma vajan, on rohkem aega.
What she wanted was a clear answer. → Mida ta tahtis, oli selge vastus.
Special cases / exceptions: Cleft on vajalik siis, kui tahame spetsiaalselt esile tõsta inimest, asja, kohta, aega või põhjust.
Common mistakes:
❌ It was John who called me yesterday. (kui pole põhjust rõhutada) → ✅ John called me yesterday.
❌ What I need is more time? → ✅ What I need is more time. (see on cleft-structure, mitte küsimus.)
Don't confuse with: Küsi: millist elementi tahan rõhutada? Kui ühtegi, võib tavaline lause olla parem.
Quick summary / memory hook:
It-cleft = It was X who/that...
Wh-cleft = What ... is/was X.
Peamine funktsioon = emphasis.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Relative clauses täpsustavad noun'i. Defining määrab täpselt, kellest või millest on jutt; non-defining lisab infot ja kasutab komasid.
Main rule / explanation: Defining võib kasutada who/which/that/where/whose. Non-defining kasutab who/which/whose, mitte standardset that. Object relative pronoun võib mõnikord ära jääda.
Form / structure: Defining: noun + who/which/that + clause. Non-defining: noun, who/which/whose + clause,.
When / why we use it: Kasutame defining/non-defining relative clause'e noun'i identifitseerimiseks või lisainfo andmiseks.
Examples:
The report that you sent is useful. → Aruanne, mille sa saatsid, on kasulik.
The report, which you sent yesterday, is useful. → Aruanne, mille sa eile saatsid, on kasulik.
The office where I work is nearby. → Kontor, kus ma töötan, on lähedal.
The report (that) I sent was approved. → Aruanne, mille ma saatsin, kiideti heaks.
Special cases / exceptions: Object relative pronoun võib ära jääda: the report (that) I sent. Subject pronoun'i tavaliselt ära jätta ei saa: the person who called.
Common mistakes:
❌ My manager, that lives nearby,... → ✅ My manager, who lives nearby,...
❌ The person called me. (kui who = relative clause'i subject) → ✅ The person who called me.
Don't confuse with: Defining = essential, no commas. Non-defining = extra, commas.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Defining → identifies.
Non-defining → extra information.
that only standard defining.
Object relative can sometimes be omitted.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Participle clauses muudavad laused lühemaks ja seovad seotud tegevusi või kirjeldusi.
Main rule / explanation: Present participle (-ing) võib näidata samaaegset või seotud tegevust. Past participle võib anda passive/background description'i. Perfect participle having + V3 näitab varasemat tegevust.
Form / structure: -ing clause. V3 clause. Having + V3 clause.
When / why we use it: Kasutame participle clause'e, et muuta seotud tegevused või kirjeldused lühemaks.
Examples:
Walking home, I saw an old friend. → Koduteel kõndides nägin vana sõpra.
The people working on the project are experienced. → Projekti kallal töötavad inimesed on kogenud.
Built in 1920, the building is still in use. → 1920. aastal ehitatud hoone on endiselt kasutusel.
Having finished the report, she sent it to the client. → Pärast aruande lõpetamist saatis ta selle kliendile.
Special cases / exceptions: Participle clause'i subject peab tavaliselt kattuma main clause'i subject'iga. Muidu tekib dangling participle.
Common mistakes:
❌ Walking down the street, the rain started. → Jääb mulje, nagu kõndinuks vihm mööda tänavat.
✅ Walking down the street, I got caught in the rain.
Don't confuse with: Kontrolli: kes teeb participle clause'i action'i? See peab olema main clause'i subject.
Quick summary / memory hook:
-ing = related/current action.
V3 = passive/background description.
Having + V3 = earlier action.
Avoid dangling participle.
