Lesson / Topic: Zero, first, second, and third conditionals
Core idea: Neli peamist conditional pattern'it näitavad erinevaid reaalsuse ja aja seoseid.
Main rule / explanation: Zero = general truth. First = real future possibility. Second = unreal/unlikely present/future. Third = unreal past. Mixed forms connect different periods.
Form / structure: Zero: If + Present, Present. First: If + Present, will + V1. Second: If + Past, would + V1. Third: If + Past Perfect, would have + V3.
When / why we use it: Vali conditional pattern aja ja reality kombinatsiooni järgi.
Examples:
If you heat water to 100°C, it boils. → Kui kuumutad vee 100 °C-ni, see keeb.
If it rains, we'll stay home. → Kui sajab, jääme koju.
If I had more time, I would travel more. → Kui mul oleks rohkem aega, reisiksin rohkem.
If we had left earlier, we would have caught the train. → Kui oleksime varem lahkunud, oleksime rongile jõudnud.
Special cases / exceptions: Valik sõltub reality'st ja ajast, mitte lihtsalt sõnast if. Mixed conditionals ühendavad ajaperioode.
Common mistakes:
❌ „On if → alati Second Conditional”. → Ei.
❌ Every hypothetical sentence is Third. → Third on konkreetselt unreal past.
Don't confuse with: Kõigepealt määra: general, real future, unreal now/future või unreal past?
Quick summary / memory hook:
Zero → general truth.
First → realistic future.
Second → unreal now/future.
Third → unreal past.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Mõned two-object verbs võivad moodustada kaks passive-lause tüüpi ning valik sõltub sellest, millise objekti tahame fookusesse panna.
Main rule / explanation: Active: They gave me the report / They gave the report to me. Passive: I was given the report / The report was given to me. Tell'i puhul saab personal object'ist sageli passive subject.
Form / structure: object-person + be + V3 + thing. thing + be + V3 + to + person.
When / why we use it: Kasutame passive'i, kui person või thing muutub peamiseks information focus'iks.
Examples:
They gave me the report. → Nad andsid mulle aruande.
I was given the report. → Mulle anti aruanne.
The report was given to me. → Aruanne anti mulle.
I was told about the change. → Mulle teatati muutusest.
Special cases / exceptions: Kõik two-object verbs ei luba mõlemat passive-pattern'it võrdselt loomulikult. Õpi common constructions.
Common mistakes:
❌ Kõigil two-object verb'idel on automaatselt kaks võrdselt loomulikku passive-vormi. → Ei.
✅ I was told about the change. — loomulik konstruktsioon tell'iga.
Don't confuse with: Küsi: mille tahan subject'iks teha — person või thing?
Quick summary / memory hook:
Two-object active can have different passive focuses.
I was given the report.
The report was given to me.

Lesson / Topic: Possessive ’s with time expressions – Two hours’ walk
Core idea: Time expression'idega possessive vormid võivad näidata kestust või vahemaad.
Main rule / explanation: Singular time noun: a day's work, one week's notice. Plural time noun ending in s: two weeks' holiday, five years' experience. Expressions vastavad küsimusele „how long?” ja võivad kirjeldada vajalikku aega/kaugust.
Form / structure: singular time + 's. plural time ending in s + '.
When / why we use it: Kasutame seda, kui time expression toimib possessive modifier'ina.
Examples:
a day's work. → päeva töö.
three weeks' holiday. → kolmenädalane puhkus.
ten minutes' drive. → kümneminutiline autosõit.
It's two hours' walk. → Kahe tunni tee on jalgsi.
It's a two-hour walk. → See on kahetunnine jalutuskäik.
Special cases / exceptions: Regular plural ending in s saab ainult apostrophe'i: hours', weeks', years'. Ära kirjuta hours's.

❌ five years's experience → ✅ five years' experience.
Don't confuse with: Võrdle possessive-vormi ja compound adjective'i: two hours' walk vs a two-hour walk.

singular time → 's.
regular plural time → s'.
No double s.

Core idea: Compound adjectives ühendavad kaks või rohkem sõna, mis kirjeldavad koos noun'i.
Main rule / explanation: Levinud pattern'id: well-known, full-time, user-friendly, high-speed, ten-year-old. Enne noun'i kasutatakse tavaliselt hyphen'it.
Form / structure: word-word + noun. number + singular noun + adjective ending.
When / why we use it: Kasutame compound adjective'i ühe määratlusena noun'i ees; sageli on vaja hyphen'it.
Examples:
a well-known company. → tuntud ettevõte.
a full-time job. → täiskohaga töö.

a five-year-old child. → viieaastane laps.
a high-quality product. → kvaliteetne toode.
Special cases / exceptions: Number-based compound'is jääb noun singular-vormi: five-year-old, mitte five-years-old. Noun'i järel: The child is five years old.
Common mistakes:
❌ a ten-years project → ✅ a ten-year project.
❌ The child is five-year-old. → ✅ The child is five years old.
Don't confuse with: Noun'i ees toimib compound ühe adjective'ina. Noun'i järel saab kasutada tavalist plural time expression'it.

compound adjective before noun → often hyphenated.
number + singular noun.
After noun → normal plural form.

Core idea: Paljud noun'id moodustavad kindlate preposition'itega püsivad ühendid. Professional English'is on need olulised collocations.
Main rule / explanation: Examples: access to, reason for, solution to, increase in, demand for, effect on, experience in, relationship with, interest in, responsibility for.

Core idea: Comparatives saab tugevdada või pehmendada ning neid võib kasutada ka järkjärgulise muutuse kirjeldamiseks.
Main rule / explanation: A little/a bit/slightly näitavad väikest erinevust. Much/far/a lot näitavad suurt erinevust. Even lisab emphasis'e. Comparative + and + comparative näitab jätkuvat muutust. The + comparative, the + comparative näitab seotud muutust.
Form / structure: slightly + comparative. much/far/a lot + comparative. even + comparative. comparative and comparative. the + comparative, the + comparative.
When / why we use it: Kasutame, kui tahame lisaks võrdlusele näidata difference'i suurust või muutuse protsessi.
Examples:
slightly cheaper → veidi odavam.
a little faster → veidi kiirem.
much more expensive → palju kallim.
far better → palju parem.
a lot easier → palju lihtsam.
even more useful → veel kasulikum.
The situation is getting better and better. → Olukord muutub järjest paremaks.
The more you practise, the easier it becomes. → Mida rohkem harjutad, seda lihtsamaks muutub.
Special cases / exceptions: Standard comparative ei sobi kokku very-ga: very better on vale. Kasuta much better/far better.
Common mistakes:
❌ very better → ✅ much better.
❌ very more expensive → ✅ much more expensive.
Don't confuse with: Kõigepealt basic comparative, siis modifier, kui soovid näidata difference'i suurust.
Quick summary / memory hook:
a bit/slightly = small difference.
much/far/a lot = large difference.
even = extra emphasis.
-er and -er = continuing change.

Lesson / Topic: Reduced infinitives: Omitting the infinitive phrase after 'to'
Core idea: Reduced infinitives võimaldavad juba arusaadavat infinitive phrase'i mitte korrata.
Main rule / explanation: Mõne konstruktsiooni järel võib alles jääda ainult to. Modal'i järel võib kontekstist mõistetud verb samuti ära jääda: I can help if you want me to. She should have.
Form / structure: want to / promise to etc. → to may remain. modal + understood verb can be omitted.
When / why we use it: Kasutame seda siis, kui kuulaja saab puuduva osa kontekstist kergesti taastada.
Examples:
I want to go, but I can't. → Ma tahan minna, aga ei saa.
She didn't call, although she promised to. → Ta ei helistanud, kuigi lubas.
I'd like to. → Ma sooviksin.
He asked me to. → Ta palus mul seda teha.
I can help if you want me to. → Ma saan aidata, kui soovid, et ma seda teeksin.
She didn't finish, although she should have. → Ta ei lõpetanud, kuigi oleks pidanud.
Special cases / exceptions: Ellipsis/reduced infinitive töötab ainult selge context'i korral. Kui omission tekitab ambiguity, korda sõnu parem.
Common mistakes:
❌ Jätta sõnad välja nii, et kuulaja ei suuda tegevust taastada. → Siis ei sobi lühendamine.
✅ She wants to go, and I want to. → Loomulik, kui go on arusaadav.
Don't confuse with: Kontrolli: kas listener saab missing verb phrase'i ilma oletamiseta taastada?
Quick summary / memory hook:
Reduced infinitive = avoid repetition.
Mõne expression'i järel jääb ainult to.
Modal võib jätta arusaadava action'i välja.
Context is essential.

Lesson / Topic: Advanced present simple and present continuous
Core idea: Present Simple ja Present Continuous'i valik sõltub mitte ainult ajast, vaid sellest, kas räägime püsivast olukorrast, ajutisest tegevusest, muutusest või ebatavalisest kordumisest.
Main rule / explanation: Present Simple näitab sagedamini stabiilset olukorda, harjumust, fakti või seisundit. Present Continuous näitab ajutist olukorda, muutust või ebatavalist/ärritavat kordumist.
Form / structure: S + V1/V-s. S + am/is/are + V-ing.
When / why we use it: She works for an international company. = stable fact. She is working from home this month. = temporary. You're always interrupting me. = repeated behaviour viewed as irritating/temporary.
Examples:
She works for an international company. → Ta töötab rahvusvahelises ettevõttes.
She is working from home this month. → Sel kuul töötab ta kodust.
More companies are moving their services online. → Üha rohkem ettevõtteid viib oma teenuseid veebi.
You're always interrupting me. → Sa segad mind pidevalt vahele.
Special cases / exceptions: Mõned traditsiooniliselt stative verbs jäävad state meaning'u puhul non-continuous: understand, believe, own. Mõni verb muudab tähendust ja võib siis olla continuous: I'm having lunch; I'm thinking about the proposal; We are seeing more customers this year.
Common mistakes:
❌ I am understanding the problem. → ✅ I understand the problem.
❌ She owns the company, so she is owning it. → ✅ She owns the company.
Don't confuse with: Ära vali Continuous'i ainult sellepärast, et tegevus toimub „praegu”. Vaata meaning'it: state, activity, temporary situation või developing trend.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Simple → stable/state/repeated.
Continuous → temporary/developing/unusual behaviour.
Meaning matters more than „now”.

Lesson / Topic: Advanced past simple, past continuous & past perfect
Core idea: Minevikuvormide edasijõudnud kasutus korraldab narrative'i: mis on põhisündmus, mis oli taust, mis juhtus varem ja mis kestis minevikuhetkeni.
Main rule / explanation: Past Simple = main completed events. Past Continuous = background/in-progress. Past Perfect = earlier past event. Past Perfect Continuous = duration/activity before a past point.
Form / structure: V2. was/were + V-ing. had + V3. had been + V-ing.
When / why we use it: She opened the file, checked the figures and sent the report. / She was checking the figures when the system crashed. / When we arrived, the meeting had already started. / She had been working for hours before she found the cause.
Examples:
She opened the file, checked the figures and sent the report. → Ta avas faili, kontrollis numbreid ja saatis aruande.
She was checking the figures when the system crashed. → Ta kontrollis numbreid, kui süsteem kokku jooksis.
When we arrived, the meeting had already started. → Kui kohale jõudsime, oli koosolek juba alanud.
She had been working on the problem for hours before she found the cause. → Ta oli probleemiga tunde töötanud, enne kui leidis põhjuse.
Special cases / exceptions: Past Perfect ei ole automaatselt vajalik iga varasema tegevuse puhul. See on kasulik siis, kui past events'ide relationship on valitud narrative viewpoint'i suhtes oluline.
Common mistakes:
❌ Kasutada Past Perfecti igas minevikulauses. → Näita konkreetset seost teise past point'iga.
❌ She had been work... → ✅ She had been working...
Don't confuse with: Kõigepealt loo timeline. Past Simple = main line; Past Continuous = background; Past Perfect = earlier; Past Perfect Continuous = duration before past point.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Past Simple = main events.
Past Continuous = background.
Past Perfect = earlier.
Past Perfect Continuous = duration before past point.

Lesson / Topic: Advanced modal verbs: will, would and should
Core idea: Will, would ja should võivad väljendada palju enamat kui tulevikku või nõuannet. Tähendus sõltub olukorrast.
Main rule / explanation: Will võib näidata valmisolekut, tüüpilist käitumist või kindlat oletust. Would võib näidata minevikuharjumust või muuta palve pehmemaks. Should võib näidata ootust või seda, mida peetakse normaalseks/ootuspäraseks.
Form / structure: will + V1. would + V1. should + V1. Formal conditional: Should + subject + V1...
When / why we use it: I'll help you. → willing. He will often ignore messages. → characteristic behaviour. That will be John calling. → strong expectation. Would you mind checking this? → polite request. The results should be ready by now. → expectation.
Examples:
I'll help you. → Ma aitan sind.
He will often ignore messages when he's busy. → Ta ignoreerib hõivatud olles sageli sõnumeid.
That will be John calling. → See on ilmselt John, kes helistab.
Would you mind checking this? → Kas te võiksite seda kontrollida?
The results should be ready by now. → Tulemused peaksid praeguseks valmis olema.
Should you need assistance, contact the support team. → Kui vajate abi, võtke tugitiimiga ühendust.
Special cases / exceptions: Modal'i tähendus sõltub context'ist. Will be at home võib olla prediction/strong expectation; would be at home võib sõltuvalt kontekstist olla hypothetical või mineviku vaatenurgast; should be at home on expectation based on what is normally true.
Common mistakes:
❌ Õppida will = ainult „tulevik”. → C1 tasemel sõltub tähendus context'ist.
❌ Should = alati nõuanne. → See võib tähendada ka ootust või formal conditional'it.
Don't confuse with: Küsi: kas kõneleja ennustab, on valmis, kirjeldab harjumust, pehmendab, ootab või esitab formaalse tingimuse?
Quick summary / memory hook:
will → willingness / typical behaviour / strong expectation.
would → past habit / softer request/opinion.
should → expectation / appropriateness / formal conditional.

Lesson / Topic: Advanced modal verbs: can / be able to, may / might
Core idea: Can ja be able to väljendavad mõlemad võimet, kuid be able to muutub oluliseks teistes aegades ja aspektides ning konkreetse õnnestunud minevikusündmuse puhul. May/might väljendavad võimalikkust.
Main rule / explanation: Can = ability now. Be able to sobib future/perfect forms'ides. Could = general past ability. Was/were able to või managed to on sageli selgemad ühe konkreetse õnnestunud minevikusündmuse puhul. May/might = possibility.
Form / structure: can + V1. be able to + V1. could + V1. may/might + V1. may/might have + V3.
When / why we use it: I can solve the problem. / We'll be able to access the system tomorrow. / We were able to solve the problem. / It may be true. / She might have forgotten.
Examples:
I can solve the problem. → Ma suudan probleemi lahendada.
We'll be able to access the system tomorrow. → Homme saame süsteemile ligi.
We were able to solve the problem. → Meil õnnestus probleem lahendada.
It may be true. → Võimalik, et see on tõsi.
She might have forgotten. → Võimalik, et ta unustas.
Special cases / exceptions: Might väljendab mõnikord veidi väiksemat kindlust kui may, kuid erinevus pole alati range. Could pole alati parim one-off successful past event'i puhul.
Common mistakes:
❌ I'll can access it tomorrow. → ✅ I'll be able to access it tomorrow.
❌ We could solve the specific problem yesterday. → Sageli selgem: We were able to solve the problem.
Don't confuse with: Can/could — modal. Be able to — paindlik tense/aspect. May/might — possibility.
Quick summary / memory hook:
can → ability now.
be able to → flexible tense/aspect.
could → general past ability.
was able to/managed to → specific past success.
may/might → possibility.

Lesson / Topic: The subjunctive in English: Present and past
Core idea: English kasutab subjunctive-laadseid vorme peamiselt formaalsetes soovituse, nõude, vajalikkuse ja hüpoteetilistes konstruktsioonides.
Main rule / explanation: Present subjunctive kasutab base form'i pärast sõnu nagu essential, important, insist, demand: It is essential that she be present. British English'is on levinud ka should + infinitive. Past subjunctive on kõige nähtavam were-vormis.
Form / structure: that + subject + V1. Formal BrE: that + subject + should + V1. Hypothetical were: If I were..., I wish it were...
When / why we use it: It is essential that every applicant be informed. / They insisted that he leave immediately. / If I were you, I would wait.
Examples:
It is essential that every applicant be informed. → On väga oluline, et iga kandidaat saaks teavitatud.
It is important that she be present. → On oluline, et ta kohal oleks.
They insisted that he leave immediately. → Nad nõudsid, et ta kohe lahkuks.
If I were you, I would wait. → Sinu asemel ma ootaksin.
I wish it were easier. → Kahju, et see pole lihtsam.
Special cases / exceptions: British English'is on selliste väljendite järel levinud ka should + infinitive. Were hüpoteetilises konstruktsioonis näitab ebareaalsust, mitte tavalist minevikuaega.
Common mistakes:
❌ It is essential that she is present. → Formaalses subjunctive pattern'is: ✅ It is essential that she be present.
❌ If I was you... → Standardne formaalne/hüpoteetiline: ✅ If I were you...
Don't confuse with: Subjunctive form valitakse struktuuri ja tähenduse, mitte tavalise tense sequence'i järgi.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Formal recommendation/demand → base verb.
Hypothetical → were.
Past-looking form may mark unreality, not past time.

Lesson / Topic: The perfect tenses: Forms and uses
Core idea: Perfect-vormid näitavad suhet kahe reference point'i vahel. Perfect ei tähenda lihtsalt „minevikku”.
Main rule / explanation: Present Perfect seob mineviku olevikuga. Present Perfect Continuous rõhutab kestust/tegevust olevikuni. Past Perfect asetab sündmuse varasemasse punkti minevikus. Past Perfect Continuous rõhutab kestust enne minevikuhetke. Future Perfect ja Future Perfect Continuous seovad lõpetatuse/kestuse tuleviku reference point'iga.
Form / structure: have/has + V3. have/has been + V-ing. had + V3. had been + V-ing. will have + V3. will have been + V-ing.
When / why we use it: Küsimus on: millise reference point'i suhtes tegevus toimus ja kas oluline on result, activity, duration või completion?
Examples:
I have finished the report. → Olen aruande lõpetanud.
I have been working all morning. → Olen terve hommiku töötanud.
The meeting had started before we arrived. → Koosolek oli alanud enne meie saabumist.
She had been waiting for an hour when he called. → Ta oli tema helistamise ajaks tund aega oodanud.
By Friday, we will have completed the project. → Reedeks oleme projekti lõpetanud.
By June, I will have been working here for ten years. → Juuniks olen siin kümme aastat töötanud.
Special cases / exceptions: Perfect on relationship marker. Ära vali vormi ainult sellepärast, et tegevus „oli minevikus”.
Common mistakes:
❌ Tõlkida Perfect kui eraldi sõna „juba”. → Vaata relationship'i reference point'ide vahel.
❌ I had finished when I arrived. → See muudab timeline'i: tegevus oli enne saabumist lõpetatud.
Don't confuse with: Kõigepealt vali reference point. Seejärel otsusta: completion/result või activity/duration.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Perfect = relationship between time points.
Simple Perfect → completion/result/experience.
Perfect Continuous → activity/duration.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Participle clauses võimaldavad koondada mitu seotud ideed lühemaks formaalseks konstruktsiooniks.
Main rule / explanation: Present participle, past participle, perfect participle ja perfect passive võivad väljendada aega, põhjust, tulemust, tingimust või accompanying circumstances.
Form / structure: -ing clause. V3 clause. Having + V3. Having been + V3.
When / why we use it: Knowing the risks, they changed the plan. / Designed for small businesses, the system is easy to use. / Having completed the analysis, she presented the results. / Having been informed of the changes, the team adjusted the schedule.
Examples:
Knowing the risks, they changed the plan. → Teades riske, muutsid nad plaani.
Designed for small businesses, the system is easy to use. → Väikeettevõtetele mõeldud süsteemi on lihtne kasutada.
Having completed the analysis, she presented the results. → Analüüsi lõpetanud, esitles ta tulemusi.
Having been informed of the changes, the team adjusted the schedule. → Muudatustest teavitatud, kohandas meeskond graafikut.
Special cases / exceptions: Participle clause'i implied subject peab tavaliselt kattuma main clause'i subject'iga.
Common mistakes:
❌ Having finished the report, the meeting started. → Jääb mulje, nagu koosolek lõpetas aruande.
✅ Having finished the report, I went to the meeting.
Don't confuse with: Kontrolli: kes teeb participle clause'i action'i? Sama subject peab olema main clause'is.
Quick summary / memory hook:
-ing = simultaneous/related action.
V3 = passive/background.
Having + V3 = earlier action.
Having been + V3 = earlier passive.

Core idea: Sõnajärge saab muuta, et tuua oluline info esile, väljendada vastandust või paigutada pikk info mugavamasse kohta.
Main rule / explanation: Emphasis'es kasutatakse fronting'ut, negative adverbial inversion'it ja cleft-construction'e. Mõnikord jäetakse pikk info lause lõppu.
Form / structure: Normal order. Fronted phrase + clause. Negative adverbial + auxiliary + subject. It-cleft / What-cleft.
When / why we use it: This problem, we need to solve first. / Never have I seen such a result. / Only after the meeting did we understand the problem. / What we need is more time. / It was the deadline that caused the problem.
Examples:
This problem, we need to solve first. → Selle probleemi peame esimesena lahendama.
Never have I seen such a result. → Ma pole kunagi sellist tulemust näinud.
Only after the meeting did we understand the problem. → Alles pärast koosolekut saime probleemist aru.
What we need is more time. → See, mida me vajame, on rohkem aega.
It was the deadline that caused the problem. → Just deadline tekitas probleemi.
Special cases / exceptions: Emphasis võib nõuda kindlat süntaktilist mustrit. Lihtne sõnade liigutamine võib tekitada vigase lause.
Common mistakes:
❌ Never I have seen... → ✅ Never have I seen...
❌ Only after the meeting we understood... → ✅ Only after the meeting did we understand...
Don't confuse with: Kõigepealt määra, milline info peab olema prominentne, siis vali selle fookuse loov struktuur.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Fronting = emphasis.
Negative/restrictive fronting → inversion.
Cleft = explicit focus.
End-weight = long information later.

Core idea: Prepositions töötavad C1 tasemel suuremate mustrite osana. Neid ei saa usaldusväärselt tuletada otsetõlke abil.
Main rule / explanation: Prepositions can follow verbs, adjectives and nouns. Questions/relative clauses'is võib preposition jääda lõppu või formaalses stiilis liikuda whom/which'i ette. Preposition to-le järgneb -ing.
Form / structure: verb + prep. adjective + prep. noun + prep. preposition + V-ing. Wh + clause + prep.
When / why we use it: depend on, belong to, insist on, object to; responsible for, aware of, capable of, interested in; reason for, solution to, effect on, access to.
Examples:
I depend on the result. → Ma sõltun tulemusest.
She is responsible for the project. → Ta vastutab projekti eest.
We need a solution to the problem. → Vajame probleemile lahendust.
Who did you speak to? → Kellega sa rääkisid?
To whom did you speak? → Kellega te rääkisite? (formal)
I'm interested in learning. → Olen õppimisest huvitatud.
I look forward to hearing from you. → Ootan teie vastust.
Special cases / exceptions: To võib olla preposition, mitte infinitive marker: look forward to hearing, object to paying.
Common mistakes:
❌ I look forward to hear from you. → ✅ I look forward to hearing from you.
❌ access of the system → ✅ access to the system.
Don't confuse with: Õpi noun/verb/adjective koos sellele kuuluva preposition'iga.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Verb + prep.
Adjective + prep.
Noun + prep.
Preposition to + V-ing.
Formal preposition placement → whom/which.

Core idea: Subject–verb agreement muutub keerukamaks, kui subject'i ja verb'i vahel on teised noun'id, quantifier'id või collective noun'id/amount expressions.
Main rule / explanation: Verb agrees with grammatical subject, not the nearest noun. Each/every/everyone võtavad singular verb'i. Collective nouns võivad variety ja meaning'i järgi erineda. Kogused/ajavahemikud võivad ühe tervikuna võtta singular'i. Titles on tavaliselt singular.
Form / structure: singular subject + singular verb. plural subject + plural verb.
When / why we use it: The list of required documents is on the website. / Each employee is responsible. / Everyone has received the message. / Ten minutes is enough. / Five years is a long time.
Examples:
The list of required documents is on the website. → Nõutavate dokumentide nimekiri on veebisaidil.
Each employee is responsible for the result. → Iga töötaja vastutab tulemuse eest.
Everyone has received the message. → Kõik on sõnumi kätte saanud.
Ten minutes is enough. → Kümnest minutist piisab.
“Great Expectations” is a novel. → „Suured lootused” on romaan.
Special cases / exceptions: Collective nouns võivad erineda: The team is working... / mõnes British context'is The team are discussing... Tähendus ja variety on olulised.
Common mistakes:
❌ The list of changes are ready. → ✅ The list of changes is ready.
❌ Nearest noun controls the verb. → ✅ Agreement sõltub tegelikust grammatical subject'ist.
Don't confuse with: Ära vaata nearest noun'i. Leia real grammatical subject.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Subject controls agreement.
Don't be distracted by intervening nouns.
each/every/everyone → singular.
Amounts/titles can be singular as units.

Core idea: Above ja over võivad mõlemad tähendada „kõrgemal”, kuid over on sagedamini seotud katmise, ristumise või millestki üle liikumisega.
Main rule / explanation: Above = at a higher level/position. Over = covering/extending across, movement across; over kasutatakse sageli ka numbers/quantities puhul.
Form / structure: above + noun. over + noun.
When / why we use it: Vali tähenduse järgi: lihtsalt kõrgemal → above; katab/ristub/liigub üle → over.
Examples:
The picture is above the sofa. → Pilt on diivani kohal.
The temperature is above zero. → Temperatuur on üle nulli.
There is a bridge over the river. → Jõe kohal on sild.
We flew over the mountains. → Lendasime üle mägede.
Over 500 people attended. → Kohal oli üle 500 inimese.
Special cases / exceptions: Mõnes kontekstis on mõlemad võimalikud. Oluline on põhiline relation.
Common mistakes: ❌ Kasutada above'i automaatselt iga „üle/kohal” kohta. → Kui oluline on crossing/covering, on over sageli loomulikum.
Don't confuse with:
above = higher level.
over = covering/crossing/movement; sageli > numbers.
Quick summary / memory hook:
above → higher.
over → across/covering/movement.

Core idea: Although ja however väljendavad mõlemad contrast'i, kuid grammatiliselt on need erinevad tööriistad.
Main rule / explanation: Although juhib subordinate clause'i. However on linking adverb, mis ühendab ideid ja vajab tavaliselt punctuation'it.
Form / structure: although + clause. Sentence. However, sentence.
When / why we use it: Üks dependent clause → although. Kaks iseseisvat ideed → however.
Examples:
Although it was expensive, we bought it. → Kuigi see oli kallis, ostsime selle.
It was expensive. However, we bought it. → See oli kallis. Kuid me ostsime selle.
The solution is, however, quite expensive. → Lahendus on siiski üsna kallis.
Special cases / exceptions: Standardkasutuses ära pane however'i kohe pärast although'i.
Common mistakes:
❌ Although it was expensive, however, we bought it. → ✅ Although it was expensive, we bought it.
❌ However it was expensive, we bought it. → ✅ Although it was expensive, we bought it.
Don't confuse with: although = grammar connector ühe struktuuri sees. however = linking adverb.
Quick summary / memory hook:
although + clause.
however + separate idea/punctuation.

Lesson / Topic: Amount of vs Number of vs Quantity of
Core idea: Number of, amount of ja quantity of valitakse noun'i tüübi ja koguse tähenduse järgi.
Main rule / explanation: Number of → plural countable nouns. Amount of → uncountable nouns. Quantity of → countable või uncountable, eriti mõõdetava koguse puhul.
Form / structure: the/a large number of + plural noun. the/a large amount of + uncountable. the/a large quantity of + countable/uncountable.
When / why we use it: Countable employees/questions → number. Uncountable money/information/traffic → amount. Measurable quantity → quantity.
Examples:
The number of employees has increased. → Töötajate arv on suurenenud.
The amount of traffic has increased. → Liikluse hulk on suurenenud.
A large quantity of water was needed. → Vaja oli suurt kogust vett.
Special cases / exceptions: Quantity of võib käia nii countable kui uncountable kohta; see rõhutab mõõdetavat kogust.
Common mistakes:
❌ the amount of employees → ✅ the number of employees.
❌ a number of money → ✅ an amount of money.
Don't confuse with: Kõigepealt: countable või uncountable?
Quick summary / memory hook:
number → plural countable.
amount → uncountable.
quantity → both, measurable.

Lesson / Topic: How to avoid double subjects in English
Core idea: Standard English'is on clause'il tavaliselt üks grammatical subject. Ära lisa pronoun'i pärast noun'i, mis on juba subject.
Main rule / explanation: Normal: The manager approved the request. Neutraalses standardstruktuuris pole vaja: The manager, he approved... Relative clause'is ei tohi samuti lisada liigset subject'i.
Form / structure: one grammatical subject per clause. Relative clause keeps its own subject/object structure.
When / why we use it: Leia subject ja kontrolli, kas sa ei korda seda teise pronoun'iga.
Examples:
The manager approved the request. → Juht kiitis taotluse heaks.
The report that I sent yesterday is ready. → Aruanne, mille ma eile saatsin, on valmis.
Siin on that tegusõna sent sihitis, mitte lisasubjekt.
Special cases / exceptions: Kõnekeeles võib esineda marked pattern: My brother, he works in IT., kuid see pole neutraalne standardstruktuur.
Common mistakes:
❌ The manager, he approved the request. → ✅ The manager approved the request.
❌ The report that I sent it yesterday... → ✅ The report that I sent yesterday...
Don't confuse with: Ära lisa pronoun'i, kui noun täidab struktuuris juba subject/object'i rolli.
Quick summary / memory hook:
One clause → one normal subject.
Avoid repeated subject pronouns.

Core idea: Between ja among on seotud asukoha ja suhetega rühmas, kuid tähtis pole ainult objektide arv.
Main rule / explanation: Between seostub traditsiooniliselt kahega, kuid võib käia ka rohkema kui kahe kohta, kui fookuses on individual relationships. Among = rühma sees/jaotumine rühmas.
Form / structure: between + people/things. among + group.
When / why we use it: Use between when individual items/relationships are in focus. Among when inside a group or distributed within it.
Examples:
The agreement is between the two companies. → Kokkulepe on kahe ettevõtte vahel.
The negotiations between the five countries continued. → Läbirääkimised viie riigi vahel jätkusid.
She was sitting among her colleagues. → Ta istus oma kolleegide seas.
The money was divided among the participants. → Raha jagati osalejate vahel.
Special cases / exceptions: Ära õpi absoluutset reeglit „between = 2, among = 3+”.
Common mistakes: ❌ Between can only be used with two. → Ei: between five countries on võimalik, kui fookuses on individual relationships.
Don't confuse with: Kas fookuses on individual relationships või group context?
Quick summary / memory hook:
between → individual relationships/items.
among → within a group/distribution.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Bring ja take sõltuvad viewpoint'ist: kas liigutakse speaker'i/reference point'i poole või sellest eemale.
Main rule / explanation: Bring = liikumine speaker'i või arutluse all oleva koha poole. Take = liikumine speaker'i/current location'i juurest eemale.
Form / structure: bring + object + to destination. take + object + to destination.
When / why we use it: Kujuta ette speaker'i reference point'i: kuhu object liigub selle punkti suhtes?
Examples:
Bring your laptop to the meeting. → Too oma sülearvuti koosolekule.
Take these documents to the manager. → Vii need dokumendid juhile.
Can you bring the report to my office? → Kas saad aruande minu kabinetti tuua?
Can you take this report to Sarah? → Kas saad selle aruande Sarah'le viia?
Special cases / exceptions: Peamine on viewpoint, mitte ainult objekti füüsiline liikumine.
Common mistakes: ❌ Valida bring/take ainult selle järgi, kummas suunas object liigub. → Vaata speaker/reference point'i.
Don't confuse with:
bring → toward reference point.
take → away from reference point.
Quick summary / memory hook: Viewpoint decides bring vs take.

Core idea: Clean ja wash võivad mõlemad käia mustuse eemaldamise kohta, kuid fookus on erinev.
Main rule / explanation: Clean = teha puhtaks, eemaldada mustus/tolm või muu soovimatu materjal. Wash = kasutada puhastamisel vett/vedelikku.

❌ Wash the kitchen. (kui mõte on üldine koristamine) → ✅ Clean the kitchen.
❌ Clean your hands. → Igapäevases kasutuses: Wash your hands.

clean = general cleaning.
wash = with water/liquid.

Core idea: Come ja go sõltuvad reference point'ist: liikumine speaker/listener/shared destination'i poole või sellest eemale.
Main rule / explanation: Come = movement toward speaker või muu shared reference point. Go = movement away from that point.

Come here. → Tule siia.

I'm going home. → Lähen koju.

come → toward reference point.
go → away from reference point.

Core idea: Have been to ja have gone to erinevad selle järgi, kas inimene on reference time'iks kohast tagasi tulnud.
Main rule / explanation: Have been to = visited and returned. Have gone to = läks sinna ja on reference time'il endiselt eemal / pole tagasi tulnud.
Form / structure: have/has been to + place. have/has gone to + place.
When / why we use it: Life experience → been to. Current absence → gone to.
Examples:
I've been to London twice. → Olen Londonis kaks korda käinud.
Sarah has gone to the supermarket. → Sarah läks supermarketisse.
Tom has been to Spain. → Tom on Hispaanias käinud.
Tom has gone to Spain. → Tom sõitis Hispaaniasse ja pole veel tagasi.
Special cases / exceptions: Kontekst otsustab, kas inimene on tagasi tulnud.
Common mistakes: ❌ I've gone to London twice. (kui jutt on kogemusest ja tagasitulekust) → ✅ I've been to London twice.
Don't confuse with:
been to = visited and returned.
gone to = went and is still away.
Quick summary / memory hook:
Experience → been.
Currently away → gone.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: If ja whether võivad mõlemad sisse juhatada indirect yes/no question'i, kuid whether'il on lisakasutusi.
Main rule / explanation: If/whether on paljudes indirect questions'ides mõlemad võimalikud. Whether on eelistatud või vajalik mõnes formaalsemas konstruktsioonis ning enne infinitive'i, with or not ja preposition'i järel.
Form / structure: if/whether + clause. whether + to + V1. whether or not + clause. prep + whether + clause.
When / why we use it: Tavaline indirect yes/no question lubab sageli mõlemat; special constructions → whether.
Examples:
I don't know if she is coming. → Ma ei tea, kas ta tuleb.
I don't know whether she is coming. → Ma ei tea, kas ta tuleb.
We need to decide whether to stay. → Peame otsustama, kas jääda.
I don't know whether or not he agrees. → Ma ei tea, kas ta on nõus või mitte.
It depends on whether they accept. → See sõltub sellest, kas nad nõustuvad.
Special cases / exceptions: Whether sobib eriti hästi enne to + V1, preposition'i järel ja whether or not konstruktsioonis.
Common mistakes:
❌ decide if to stay → ✅ decide whether to stay.
❌ It depends on if they accept. → ✅ It depends on whether they accept.
Don't confuse with: Tavalises indirect yes/no question'is võivad mõlemad sobida. Special positions → whether.
Quick summary / memory hook:
if/whether = indirect yes/no question.
whether + to V1.
whether or not.
preposition + whether.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Instead ja instead of näitavad mõlemad alternatiivi, kuid grammatiliselt toimivad erinevalt.
Main rule / explanation: Instead = adverb. Instead of = preposition, mille järel tuleb noun, pronoun või V-ing.
Form / structure: instead. instead of + noun/pronoun/V-ing.
When / why we use it: Instead võib asendada terve alternatiivi. Instead of juhatab sisse tegevuse/objekti, mis asendatakse.
Examples:
We didn't take the train. We drove instead. → Me ei sõitnud rongiga. Selle asemel sõitsime autoga.
Instead, we decided to walk. → Selle asemel otsustasime jalgsi minna.
We walked instead of taking the bus. → Läksime bussiga sõitmise asemel jala.
She called instead of sending an email. → Ta helistas meili saatmise asemel.
Special cases / exceptions: Pärast instead of kasutatakse verbi puhul -ing-vormi.
Common mistakes:
❌ instead of wait → ✅ instead of waiting.
❌ We drove instead of the train. → Tähenduse järgi parem: We drove instead.
Don't confuse with: adverb vs preposition.
Quick summary / memory hook:
instead = as an alternative.
instead of + noun/pronoun/V-ing.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Its ja it's erinevad sama selgelt nagu possessive ja contraction.
Main rule / explanation: Its = possessive determiner. It's = it is või it has.
Form / structure: its + noun. it's = it is / it has.
When / why we use it: Kontrolli, kas it's saab asendada sõnadega it is või it has.
Examples:
The company changed its policy. → Ettevõte muutis oma poliitikat.
It's cold today. → Täna on külm.
It's been a long day. → See on olnud pikk päev.
Special cases / exceptions: Possessive its ei võta apostrophe'i.
Common mistakes:
❌ The company changed it's policy. → ✅ The company changed its policy.
❌ Its cold today. → ✅ It's cold today.
Don't confuse with: Possession → its. Contraction → it's.
Quick summary / memory hook:
its = possessive.
it's = it is / it has.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Last vs The last, Next vs The next
Core idea: Last ja next muudavad tähendust vastavalt sellele, kas nende ees on the. Ilma the-ta viitavad nad sageli now suhtes olevale ajale; the-ga konkreetsele elemendile järjestuses.
Main rule / explanation: Last week = week immediately before this one. The last week of the course = final week of that course. Next week = following week from now. The next week = following week in a sequence/narrative.
Form / structure: last/next + time period. the last/the next + noun in a sequence.
When / why we use it: Vaata, kas jutt käib calendar period'ist relative to now või kindlast elemendist sequence'is.
Examples:
I saw her last week. → Nägin teda eelmisel nädalal.
The last week of the course was difficult. → Kursuse viimane nädal oli raske.
I'll see you next week. → Näeme järgmisel nädalal.
The next week was much quieter. → Järgnev nädal oli palju rahulikum.
Special cases / exceptions: Artikli kasutamine muudab reference point'i sõltuvalt kontekstist.
Common mistakes: ❌ Treat next month and the next month as always identical. → Context eristab neid.
Don't confuse with:
last/next = sageli suhe now'ga.
the last/the next = sequence/context'i element.
Quick summary / memory hook: Article changes the reference point.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Lie ja lay erinevad selle järgi, kas verb on intransitive „lamama/olema horisontaalses asendis” või transitive „midagi kuhugi asetama”.
Main rule / explanation: Lie = be in a horizontal position: lie–lay–lain. Lay = put something somewhere: lay–laid–laid.
Form / structure: lie + no direct object. lay + direct object.
When / why we use it: Küsi, kas verbil on object: I lie down. / I lay the book down.
Examples:
I need to lie down. → Mul on vaja pikali heita.
She is lying on the bed. → Ta lamab voodil.
Please lay the book on the table. → Palun pane raamat lauale.
He laid the keys on the desk. → Ta pani võtmed lauale.
Special cases / exceptions: Lie (recline)'i past on lay. Lay'l endal on past laid. Just see tekitab sageli confusion'i.
Common mistakes:
❌ Yesterday I laid on the sofa. → ✅ Yesterday I lay on the sofa.
❌ He lay the keys on the desk. → ✅ He laid the keys on the desk.
Don't confuse with: lie = position/state. lay = put something.
Quick summary / memory hook:
lie – lay – lain.
lay – laid – laid.
Object after lay.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Fewer kasutatakse tavaliselt plural countable noun'idega, less — uncountable noun'idega.
Main rule / explanation: fewer mistakes/employees/problems. less time/money/information. Mõõtühendites on less loomulik: less than ten minutes.
Form / structure: fewer + plural countable. less + uncountable.
When / why we use it: Kõigepealt määra noun'i grammatical type.
Examples:
We need fewer meetings. → Me vajame vähem koosolekuid.
We need less paperwork. → Me vajame vähem paberitööd.
It took less than ten minutes. → See võttis vähem kui kümme minutit.
Special cases / exceptions: Mõõtühendites on less tavaline: less than five kilometres. Ära vali ainult selle järgi, et vene keeles on tegu „eraldi asjadega”.
Common mistakes:
❌ less employees → ✅ fewer employees.
❌ fewer information → ✅ less information.
Don't confuse with:
countable plural → fewer.
uncountable → less.
Quick summary / memory hook:
fewer = countable plural.
less = uncountable.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Like ja as võivad kõlada sarnaselt, kuid like võrdleb tavaliselt ning as juhib clause'i või näitab rolli/funktsiooni.
Main rule / explanation: Like on tavaliselt preposition noun'i või pronoun'i ees. As võib juhtida clause'i või kirjeldada rolli/funktsiooni.
Form / structure: like + noun/pronoun. as + clause. as + role/noun.
When / why we use it: Küsi: „sarnane millelegi?” → like. „rollis / nii nagu?” → as.
Examples:
She works like a professional. → Ta töötab nagu professionaal.
It looks like rain. → Paistab, et tuleb vihma.
Do it as I showed you. → Tee nii, nagu ma sulle näitasin.
He works as a designer. → Ta töötab disainerina.
As you know, the meeting starts at nine. → Nagu sa tead, algab koosolek kell üheksa.
Special cases / exceptions: Formaalsemas kõnes/kirjas kasutatakse as-i sageli täieliku sentence'i ees: Do it as I told you.
Common mistakes:
❌ He works like a designer. (kui see on tema actual role) → ✅ He works as a designer.
❌ Do it like I told you. → Formaalses standardis: ✅ Do it as I told you.
Don't confuse with:
like = resemblance.
as = role/function or clause.
Quick summary / memory hook:
like + noun/pronoun.
as + clause/role.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Little vs A little, Few vs A few
Core idea: Little/few ilma a-ta annavad sageli tähenduse „vähe, peaaegu ebapiisavalt”. A little/a few näitavad väikest, kuid reaalset kogust või arvu.
Main rule / explanation: Little + uncountable. A little + uncountable. Few + plural countable. A few + plural countable.
Form / structure: little/a little + uncountable. few/a few + plural countable.
When / why we use it: Peamine erinevus on article a: almost none/insufficient vs some amount/number.
Examples:
We have little time. → Meil on vähe aega, tõenäoliselt liiga vähe.
We have a little time. → Meil on natuke aega.
Few people understood the problem. → Vähesed inimesed said probleemist aru.
A few people understood the problem. → Mõned inimesed said probleemist aru.
Special cases / exceptions: Article a muudab tähendust oluliselt. Võrdle little hope vs a little hope.
Common mistakes:
❌ a little people → ✅ a few people.
❌ a few time → ✅ a little time.
Don't confuse with:
little/a little → uncountable.
few/a few → plural countable.
a = small but real amount/number.
Quick summary / memory hook:
a little/a few = some.
little/few = not much/not many.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: See, look ja watch kirjeldavad eri liiki visual perception'it.
Main rule / explanation: See = perception ilma teadliku pingutuseta. Look = suuna oma silmad millegi poole ja vajab baasvormis tavaliselt at-i. Watch = jälgi mõnda aega, eriti liikuvat või muutuvat asja.
Form / structure: see + object. look at + object. watch + object.
When / why we use it: Lihtsalt märkama → see. Suunama pilgu → look at. Mõnda aega jälgima → watch.
Examples:
I can see the mountains. → Ma näen mägesid.
Look at this picture. → Vaata seda pilti.
We watched a film. → Vaatasime filmi.
She watched the children playing. → Ta jälgis lapsi mängimas.
Special cases / exceptions: Look vajab baaspattern'is at-i, kui tähendus on „suuna oma pilk millelegi”.
Common mistakes:
❌ Look the screen. → ✅ Look at the screen.
❌ I watched the mountains from the window. → Tavaliselt: I saw the mountains / looked at the mountains, sõltuvalt mõttest.
Don't confuse with:
see = perception.
look at = directed attention.
watch = sustained observation.
Quick summary / memory hook:
see = notice.
look at = direct eyes.
watch = observe over time.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Maybe ja may be kõlavad ühtemoodi, kuid on erinevad grammatilised konstruktsioonid.
Main rule / explanation: Maybe = adverb tähendusega perhaps. May be = modal may + verb be.
Form / structure: Maybe + clause. subject + may be + complement.
When / why we use it: Kui selle saab asendada sõnaga perhaps → maybe. Kui may + be on verb phrase'i osa → may be.
Examples:
Maybe she is busy. → Võib-olla on ta hõivatud.
She may be busy. → Võimalik, et ta on hõivatud.
Maybe we'll go tomorrow. → Võib-olla läheme homme.
They may be late. → Võib-olla jäävad nad hiljaks.
Special cases / exceptions: Asukoht näitab struktuuri: Maybe on sageli sentence-level adverb; may be on predicate'i osa.
Common mistakes:
❌ She maybe busy. → ✅ She may be busy. / Maybe she is busy.
❌ Maybe she may be busy. → Võimalik, kuid rõhk muutub; ära kasuta seda lihtsalt õigekirja variandina.
Don't confuse with:
maybe = perhaps.
may be = modal + be.
Quick summary / memory hook:
maybe = one word adverb.
may be = two-word verb phrase.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Never ja ever on mõlemad seotud aja/sagedusega, kuid neid kasutatakse erinevalt.
Main rule / explanation: Never = at no time. Ever esineb sageli questions, conditionals ja superlative-like expressions'ides.
Form / structure: never + verb. Have you ever...? if you ever... best ... I've ever...
When / why we use it: Ever küsib sageli „kas kunagi?” või tähendab „kunagi”. Never sisaldab juba negatiivset tähendust.
Examples:
I've never been there. → Ma pole seal kunagi käinud.
She never complains. → Ta ei kurda kunagi.
Have you ever been to Spain? → Kas sa oled kunagi Hispaanias käinud?
If you ever need help, call me. → Kui sul kunagi abi vaja on, helista mulle.
This is the best result I've ever seen. → See on parim tulemus, mida ma kunagi näinud olen.
Special cases / exceptions: Iseseisvas jaatavas lauses ei asenda ever tavaliselt never'it.
Common mistakes: ❌ I've ever seen it. → ✅ I've never seen it. / This is the best I've ever seen.
Don't confuse with:
never = no time.
ever = questions/conditions/experience/emphasis.
Quick summary / memory hook:
never = at no time.
ever = at any time, commonly in questions/conditions.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: On the other hand vs On the contrary
Core idea: On the other hand ja on the contrary võivad mõlemad ideid ühendada, kuid väljendavad erinevaid suhteid.
Main rule / explanation: On the other hand toob sisse teise aspekti. On the contrary lükkab otseselt ümber või parandab varasemat väidet/eeldust.
Form / structure: Sentence. On the other hand, sentence. / On the contrary, sentence.
When / why we use it: Kasuta on the other hand teise külje näitamiseks; on the contrary siis, kui tähendus on „vastupidi, see pole nii”.
Examples:
The job is well paid. On the other hand, the hours are long. → Töö on hästi tasustatud. Teisest küljest on tööaeg pikk.
“I thought the task was difficult.” “On the contrary, it was quite easy.” → „Ma arvasin, et ülesanne on raske.” „Vastupidi, see oli üsna lihtne.”
Special cases / exceptions: On the contrary vajab otsest contradiction/correction'i, mitte lihtsalt muud infot.
Common mistakes:
❌ Two different facts = automatically on the contrary. → Ei; sageli on parem on the other hand.
✅ On the contrary, it was easy. → otsene correction.
Don't confuse with:
other hand = another aspect.
contrary = opposite of what was suggested.
Quick summary / memory hook:
on the other hand = teine aspekt.
on the contrary = otsene ümberlükkamine.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Raise ja rise erinevad transitivity järgi: raise vajab tavaliselt object'i, rise tavaliselt mitte.
Main rule / explanation: Raise = someone raises something. Rise = something rises by itself. Forms: raise–raised–raised; rise–rose–risen.
Form / structure: raise + object. rise + subject/no direct object.
When / why we use it: Keski tõstab/suurendab midagi? → raise. Miski tõuseb/suureneb ise? → rise.
Examples:
They raised the price. → Nad tõstsid hinda.
She raised her hand. → Ta tõstis käe.
Prices rise. → Hinnad tõusevad.
The sun rises. → Päike tõuseb.
The temperature is rising. → Temperatuur tõuseb.
Special cases / exceptions: Rise on selles põhieristuses intransitive. Raise võtab direct object'i.
Common mistakes:
❌ They rose the price. → ✅ They raised the price.
❌ She raised. → Selles tähenduses on vaja object'i: She raised her hand.
Don't confuse with:
raise = transitive.
rise = intransitive.
Quick summary / memory hook:
raise–raised–raised.
rise–rose–risen.
Object → raise.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Remember & Forget: To Do vs Doing
Core idea: Remember/forget + to V1 käib tegevuse kohta, mida on vaja teha või oli vaja teha. + V-ing käib juba toimunud tegevuse mäletamise kohta.
Main rule / explanation: to-infinitive = task/action to do. V-ing = memory/experience of doing.
Form / structure: remember/forget + to + V1. remember/forget + V-ing.
When / why we use it: Võrdle: Did I remember the task? vs Do I remember the event?
Examples:
Remember to send the email. → Ära unusta meili saatmast.
I forgot to call him. → Unustasin talle helistada.
I remember meeting her. → Mäletan, et kohtusin temaga.
I'll never forget visiting that place. → Ma ei unusta kunagi selle koha külastamist.
I remembered to lock the door. → Ma ei unustanud ust lukustada.
I remember locking the door. → Ma mäletan, et lukustasin ukse.
Special cases / exceptions: Erinevus ei ole lihtsalt ajas. Küsimus on relationship between remembering and the action.
Common mistakes:
❌ I forgot meeting her. = tähendus muutub: see viitab sündmuse unustamisele. → ✅ I forgot to meet her. (unustasin teha.)
❌ I remembered meeting her. = „mäletasin kohtumist”, mitte „mäletasin, et pidin kohtuma”.
Don't confuse with:
to do = remember/forget the task.
doing = memory of past action.
Quick summary / memory hook:
remember/forget + to do → task.
remember/forget + doing → memory.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Say ja tell edastavad mõlemad infot, kuid tell võtab selles reporting pattern'is tavaliselt object'i ehk inimese, kellele räägitakse.
Main rule / explanation: Say focuses on words/message. Tell focuses on communicating to someone and usually takes an object in this reporting pattern.
Form / structure:
say something / say that...
tell someone something / tell someone to do something
tell the truth / tell a story / tell a joke / tell the time
When / why we use it: Kõigepealt vaata, kas message'i receiver on nimetatud.
Examples:
She said that she was tired. → Ta ütles, et on väsinud.
She told me that she was tired. → Ta ütles mulle, et on väsinud.
He told us the truth. → Ta rääkis meile tõtt.
He told a joke. → Ta rääkis nalja.
Tell me the time, please. → Ütle mulle, mis kell on.
Special cases / exceptions: Tell'i järel nimetatakse sageli receiver'it, kuid mitte alati. Fixed phrases tell the truth, tell a lie, tell a story, tell a joke, tell the time kasutavad seda ilma receiver'ita.
Common mistakes:
❌ He said me the truth. → ✅ He told me the truth.
❌ He told me to the truth. → ✅ He told me the truth.
❌ She told that she was tired. → ✅ She said that she was tired. / She told me that she was tired.
❌ He said a joke. → ✅ He told a joke.
Don't confuse with:
say = words/message.
tell = tell someone.
Quick summary / memory hook:
say something.
say that...
tell someone something.
tell someone to do.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Lesson / Topic: Try to do vs Try doing
Core idea: Try to do ja try doing võivad mõlemad tähendada „proovima”, kuid fookus on erinev.
Main rule / explanation: Try to do = pinguta tegevuse sooritamiseks. Try doing = katseta tegevust või meetodit, et näha, kas see töötab.
Form / structure: try + to + V1. try + V-ing.
When / why we use it: Küsi: kas jutt on effort'ist tegevuse tegemiseks või eksperimendist võimaliku solution'iga?
Examples:
Try to restart the computer. → Proovi arvuti taaskäivitada.
I tried to contact the client. → Proovisin kliendiga ühendust võtta.
Try restarting the computer. → Proovi arvuti taaskäivitamist.
Try using a different browser. → Proovi teist brauserit.
Special cases / exceptions: Need ei ole lihtsalt kaks stiilivarianti. Infinitive rõhutab effort'it; -ing viitab sageli method/experiment'ile.
Common mistakes:
❌ Try to restarting the computer. → ✅ Try restarting the computer.
❌ Try doing to contact the client. → ✅ Try to contact the client.
Don't confuse with:
to do = effort.
doing = experiment/method.
Quick summary / memory hook:
try to do = make an effort.
try doing = test a method.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Until ja by vastavad erinevatele ajaküsimustele: kas miski kestab kuni hetkeni või peab olema hiljemalt tähtajaks valmis.
Main rule / explanation: Until = situation/action continues up to a time. By = deadline/latest time something will happen.
Form / structure: verb + until + time. verb + by + time.
When / why we use it: Pidev kestus → until. Tähtaeg/completion → by.
Examples:
I'll work until six. → Töötan kella kuueni.
She stayed there until Friday. → Ta jäi sinna reedeni.
Please finish it by six. → Palun lõpeta see kuueks.
I'll have sent the report by Friday. → Saadan aruande reedeks.
Special cases / exceptions: Until võib tähendada „mitte enne”, sõltuvalt kontekstist: Send it until Friday pole tavaline viis deadline'i väljendamiseks.
Common mistakes:
❌ Please finish it until six. → ✅ Please finish it by six.
✅ I won't send it until Friday. → Siin tähendab until „mitte enne reedet”.
Don't confuse with:
until = continuation up to a time.
by = deadline/latest time.
Quick summary / memory hook:
until → continues to.
by → completed no later than.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Whereas ja while võivad mõlemad võrrelda kahte olukorda, kuid while'il on ka teisi tähendusi.
Main rule / explanation: Whereas näitab peamiselt facts/characteristics'ide contrast'i. While võib tähistada contrast'i, aega või mõnikord concession'it.
Form / structure: whereas + clause. while + clause.
When / why we use it: Kui vaja on ainult contrast'i faktide vahel → whereas. Kui while, määra kontekstist, kas tähendus on time või contrast.
Examples:
The first option is cheap, whereas the second is faster. → Esimene variant on odav, samas kui teine on kiirem.
The first option is cheap, while the second is faster. → Esimene variant on odav, samas kui teine on kiirem.
While I was working, she called. → Kui ma töötasin, helistas ta.
While I understand your point, I disagree. → Kuigi ma mõistan su mõtet, ei nõustu ma.
Special cases / exceptions: Whereas on formaalsem ja eriti tavaline kirjas. While võib tähendada during the time that, contrast või concession.
Common mistakes:
❌ Assume every while = whereas. → Ei: while võib tähendada aega.
✅ While I was working... = time, not contrast.
Don't confuse with:
whereas = contrast.
while = contrast OR time OR concession.
Quick summary / memory hook:
whereas → contrastive.
while → contrast/time/concession.
QA / notes: Translated directly from RU master; English formulas and example source text preserved.

Core idea: Wish, hope ja expect on seotud tuleviku või soovitud olukordadega, kuid väljendavad erinevat suhtumist tegelikkusse.
Main rule / explanation: Hope = desired and realistically possible. Expect = believe something is likely/anticipated. Wish = unreal, unlikely or impossible situation, or regret.
Form / structure: hope + clause/to V1. expect + noun/to V1/that-clause. wish + unreal structure.
When / why we use it: Kasuta neid realistic desire'i, expectation'i ja unreal/regret'i eristamiseks.
Examples:
I hope we can finish today. → Loodan, et saame täna lõpetada.
I expect the meeting to finish at five. → Eeldan, et koosolek lõpeb kell viis.
I wish I had more time. → Kahju, et mul pole rohkem aega.
I wish you were here. → Kahju, et sa siin ei ole.
We wish you a pleasant journey. → Soovime teile meeldivat reisi.
Special cases / exceptions: Wish pole lihtne hope'i sünonüüm, kui soovitud sündmus on realistlikult võimalik.
Common mistakes:
❌ I wish we can finish today. → Realistic possibility: ✅ I hope we can finish today.
❌ I expect I had more time. → Unreal present: ✅ I wish I had more time.
Don't confuse with: realistic desire → hope; likely expectation → expect; unreal/regret → wish.
Quick summary / memory hook:
hope = desired + possible.
expect = likely/anticipated.
